title: Entanglement Certification Using Noncontextuality Inequalities
authors: Yujie Zhang, Jonah Spodek, David Schmid, Carter Reid, Liam J. Morrison, Thomas Jennewein, Kevin J. Resch, And Robert W. Spekkens
abstract:
Author(s): Yujie Zhang, Jonah Spodek, David Schmid, Carter Reid, Liam J. Morrison, Thomas Jennewein, Kevin J. Resch, and Robert W. Spekkens

Researchers demonstrate a gauge-independent entanglement certification method based on noncontextuality inequalities that detects entangled states without requiring prior measurement device characterization.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031057] Published Tue Sep 01, 2026.
tldr: Researchers demonstrate a gauge-independent entanglement certification method based on noncontextuality inequalities that detects entangled states without requiring prior measurement device characterization.
motivation: Certifying entanglement typically relies on assumptions about measurement devices, which may be unreliable or untrusted. A method that avoids prior device characterization would provide stronger, more robust entanglement verification.
method: The authors develop and experimentally implement a gauge-independent entanglement certification protocol using noncontextuality inequalities, likely in a photonic setup. The inequalities are used to witness entanglement without detailed knowledge of the measurement apparatus.
result: The method successfully detects entangled states without prior measurement device characterization, demonstrating its effectiveness in a proof-of-principle experiment.
conclusion: Noncontextuality inequalities offer a powerful, gauge-independent approach to entanglement certification, advancing device-independent and semi-device-independent quantum information protocols.

title: Device-independent Quantum Digital Signatures Under Realistic Conditions
authors: Yi Fan, Jing-Wei Bian, Bing-Hong Li, Jingwei Wen, Hua-Lei Yin, And Zeng-Bing Chen
abstract:
Author(s): Yi Fan, Jing-Wei Bian, Bing-Hong Li, Jingwei Wen, Hua-Lei Yin, and Zeng-Bing Chen

Quantum digital signatures (QDS) provide information-theoretic security for data integrity, authenticity, and nonrepudiation by exploiting the laws of quantum mechanics. While existing QDS protocols have achieved significant efficiency improvements via one-time universal hashing, they rely on truste…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 032617] Published Tue Sep 22, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes device-independent quantum digital signatures that remain secure under realistic experimental conditions without trusting the quantum devices.
motivation: Existing efficient quantum digital signature protocols rely on trusted devices, which is a strong practical assumption; device independence would remove this trust requirement and enhance security.
method: The authors develop a device-independent quantum digital signature protocol, likely combining Bell nonlocality tests with one-time universal hashing, and analyze its performance under realistic noise and imperfections.
result: The protocol achieves information-theoretic security for data integrity, authenticity, and nonrepudiation while tolerating realistic device imperfections.
conclusion: This work advances practical device-independent quantum cryptography by demonstrating that secure quantum digital signatures can be realized under realistic conditions.

title: Certifying Ergotropy Under Partial Information
authors: Egle Pagliaro, Leonardo Zambrano, Mir Alimuddin, Alioscia Hamma, Antonio Acín, And Donato Farina
abstract:
Author(s): Egle Pagliaro, Leonardo Zambrano, Mir Alimuddin, Alioscia Hamma, Antonio Acín, and Donato Farina

Ergotropy, the maximum work extractable from a quantum system, is a central resource in quantum physics. Computing ergotropy is well established when the system state is fully known, but its estimation under partial information remains an open problem. Here we introduce a general certification frame…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 130401] Published Mon Sep 21, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a general certification framework for ergotropy—the maximum extractable work from a quantum system—when only partial information about the state is available.
motivation: Computing ergotropy is well understood when the quantum state is fully known, but estimating or certifying it under partial information is an open problem relevant to practical quantum thermodynamics.
method: The authors develop a certification framework that bounds ergotropy using incomplete information, likely combining information-theoretic measures with thermodynamic constraints.
result: They obtain general bounds or certificates for ergotropy under partial information, enabling reliable work extraction estimates without full state tomography.
conclusion: This work advances quantum thermodynamics by providing tools to certify a key resource under realistic informational limitations.

title: Eigenstate Thermalization In Thermal First-Order Phase Transitions
authors: Maksym Serbyn, Alexander Avdoshkin, Oriana K. Diessel, And David A. Huse
abstract:
Author(s): Maksym Serbyn, Alexander Avdoshkin, Oriana K. Diessel, and David A. Huse

Researchers demonstrate that thermal first-order phase transitions require a generalization of the eigenstate thermalization hypothesis, leading to the coexistence of distinct eigenstate classes and Schrödinger-cat-like states.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031042] Published Tue Aug 18, 2026.
tldr: The paper demonstrates that thermal first-order phase transitions require a generalization of the eigenstate thermalization hypothesis, leading to coexisting eigenstate classes and Schrödinger-cat-like states.
motivation: Standard eigenstate thermalization hypothesis (ETH) may fail near first-order phase transitions, and understanding how ETH must be modified is important for quantum statistical mechanics and thermalization.
method: The authors analyze eigenstate properties across thermal first-order phase transitions, likely using theoretical arguments and numerical studies of model Hamiltonians.
result: They find that distinct eigenstate classes coexist and that Schrödinger-cat-like states emerge, necessitating a generalized ETH framework for such transitions.
conclusion: This work extends ETH to thermal first-order phase transitions and clarifies how quantum coherence and phase coexistence manifest in individual eigenstates.

title: Andreev Bound-state Optoelectronics: Absorption Spectroscopy And Microwave-to-optical Transduction
authors: Benjamin Remez, Pouyan Ghaemi, Jay D. Sau, And Mohammad Hafezi
abstract:
Author(s): Benjamin Remez, Pouyan Ghaemi, Jay D. Sau, and Mohammad Hafezi

Voltage-tunable semiconductor-superconductor qubits and optical connectivity address different bottlenecks to scaling up superconducting quantum computing. Here, the authors show theoretically that these approaches can be combined in one device: semiconductor optical transitions in a hybrid junction directly access its microwave-active Andreev bound states. This light–Andreev interaction enables optical spectroscopy and control of the bound states, while providing a mechanism for coherent microwave-to-optical photon transduction.


[Phys. Rev. B 114, L171302] Published Thu Sep 24, 2026.
tldr: The paper theoretically proposes a hybrid semiconductor-superconductor device in which optical transitions couple to microwave-active Andreev bound states, enabling optical spectroscopy and coherent microwave-to-optical transduction.
motivation: Scaling superconducting quantum computing requires both optical connectivity and voltage-tunable qubits, which are typically addressed by separate platforms.
method: The authors analyze a hybrid junction where semiconductor optical transitions directly interact with Andreev bound states, using theoretical modeling of the light–Andreev coupling.
result: They show that this interaction allows optical access and control of the bound states and provides a mechanism for coherent microwave-to-optical photon conversion.
conclusion: The proposed platform could enable optical spectroscopy/control of Andreev-based qubits and serve as a transducer for quantum networking with superconducting circuits.

title: Infinite Temperature At Zero Energy
authors: Matteo Ippoliti And David M. Long
abstract:
Author(s): Matteo Ippoliti and David M. Long

Researchers construct local Hamiltonians whose eigenstates inherit infinite-temperature properties, producing ground states with extensive entanglement.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031030] Published Fri Aug 07, 2026.
tldr: The paper constructs local Hamiltonians whose eigenstates exhibit infinite-temperature properties, yielding ground states with extensive entanglement.
motivation: Understanding whether local Hamiltonians can host ground states with volume-law entanglement challenges conventional area-law expectations and informs entanglement theory in many-body systems.
method: The authors design local Hamiltonians with spectral features that force eigenstates to inherit infinite-temperature characteristics, likely using frustration-free or stoquastic constructions.
result: The ground states of these Hamiltonians possess extensive (volume-law) entanglement entropy, demonstrating that local interactions can produce highly entangled ground states.
conclusion: This work expands the landscape of entanglement in local Hamiltonians and may have implications for quantum simulation and the classification of many-body phases.

title: Finite-Size Quantum Key Distribution Rates From Rényi Entropies Using Conic Optimization
authors: Mariana Navarro, Andrés González Lorente, Pablo V. Parellada, Carlos Pascual-García, And Mateus Araújo
abstract:
Author(s): Mariana Navarro, Andrés González Lorente, Pablo V. Parellada, Carlos Pascual-García, and Mateus Araújo

A conic optimization method addressing a critical challenge in key rate estimation for quantum key distribution is presented, providing tighter security bounds and fast numerical convergence.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033051] Published Thu Sep 10, 2026.
tldr: A conic optimization method computes finite-size quantum key distribution rates from Rényi entropies, yielding tighter security bounds and fast numerical convergence.
motivation: Accurate finite-size key rate estimation is critical for practical QKD security, but existing methods often give loose bounds or are computationally expensive.
method: The key rate estimation is formulated as a conic optimization problem using Rényi entropies to bound the eavesdropper's information in the finite-size regime.
result: The approach provides tighter finite-size security bounds for QKD and achieves fast numerical convergence compared to standard techniques.
conclusion: This work improves practical QKD security analysis by enabling efficient and tighter finite-size key rate certification using conic optimization.

title: Robust Superradiance And Spontaneous Spin Ordering In Disordered Waveguide Quantum Electrodynamics
authors: Xin H. H. Zhang, Daniel Malz, And Peter Rabl
abstract:
Author(s): Xin H. H. Zhang, Daniel Malz, and Peter Rabl

Spontaneous self-organization of atomic spins protects the hallmark burst of superradiance against strong spatial and spectral disorder in photonic waveguides.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033034] Published Wed Aug 19, 2026.
tldr: Spontaneous self-organization of atomic spins in disordered waveguide QED protects superradiant bursts against strong spatial and spectral disorder.
motivation: Superradiance is usually fragile to disorder, motivating the question of whether collective spin ordering can stabilize it in photonic waveguide platforms.
method: The authors analyze a waveguide QED model of atomic spins with spatial and spectral disorder, likely using theoretical and numerical techniques to study spontaneous ordering and radiative dynamics.
result: They find robust superradiance and spontaneous spin ordering that survive strong disorder, preserving the hallmark superradiant burst.
conclusion: Disorder-induced self-organization can make collective radiative phenomena resilient, with implications for waveguide QED and hybrid quantum platforms.

title: Generalized Finite-time Optimal Control Framework In Stochastic Thermodynamics
authors: Atul Tanaji Mohite And Heiko Rieger
abstract:
Author(s): Atul Tanaji Mohite and Heiko Rieger

Optimal processes in stochastic thermodynamics represent a frontier for understanding the control and design of nonequilibrium systems, with broad practical applications in biology, chemistry, and nanoscale/mesoscale systems. Optimal transport theory and thermodynamic geometry have emerged as leadin…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033340] Published Mon Sep 21, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops a generalized finite-time optimal control framework for stochastic thermodynamics by combining optimal transport theory and thermodynamic geometry.
motivation: Optimal control of nonequilibrium systems is crucial for understanding and designing nanoscale and mesoscale processes, but finite-time optimal protocols remain challenging to characterize generally.
method: The authors integrate optimal transport theory with thermodynamic geometry to formulate a generalized framework for finite-time optimal control in stochastic thermodynamics.
result: The framework yields a unified approach to deriving optimal protocols and fundamental bounds for finite-time thermodynamic transformations, with broad applicability across nonequilibrium systems.
conclusion: This work provides a powerful theoretical tool for finite-time thermodynamic optimization, bridging stochastic thermodynamics, optimal transport, and thermodynamic geometry.

title: Bell Inequalities From Outcome Equalities
authors: Ricardo Faleiro, Flavien Hirsch, Emmanuel Zambrini Cruzeiro, And Nicolas Gisin
abstract:
Author(s): Ricardo Faleiro, Flavien Hirsch, Emmanuel Zambrini Cruzeiro, and Nicolas Gisin

In this work we study a particular class of Bell inequalities involving only direct equality comparisons of outcomes. In the bipartite case, the scenario can be interpreted as a natural generalization of full-correlator inequalities (xor games) beyond binary outputs. We define the subpolytope of the…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 032448] Published Tue Sep 22, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a class of Bell inequalities based on direct equality comparisons of outcomes, generalizing full-correlator XOR games to non-binary outputs.
motivation: Bell inequalities are essential for testing quantum nonlocality and enabling device-independent protocols, but many known inequalities rely on binary outcomes or specific correlation functions.
method: The authors study bipartite Bell scenarios with outcome equalities and define a subpolytope of the Bell polytope, characterizing its facets and quantum violations.
result: They identify new Bell inequalities that can detect nonlocality beyond standard XOR games and provide a framework for constructing such inequalities systematically.
conclusion: These inequalities expand the toolbox for Bell tests and may find applications in device-independent quantum information processing.

title: Semidefinite Block-Matrix Relaxations For Computing Quantum Correlations
authors: Nicola D’alessandro, Carles Roch I Carceller, And Armin Tavakoli
abstract:
Author(s): Nicola D’Alessandro, Carles Roch i Carceller, and Armin Tavakoli

Researchers provide a computational method for bounding the correlations arising in a multitude of quantum information problems.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031050] Published Tue Aug 25, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces semidefinite block-matrix relaxations to compute bounds on quantum correlations across many information-theoretic problems.
motivation: Computing quantum correlations is central to entanglement detection, Bell nonlocality, and device-independent protocols, but exact characterizations are often computationally intractable.
method: The authors develop a hierarchy of semidefinite programming relaxations based on block-matrix structures to bound sets of quantum correlations.
result: The method provides computable outer approximations to quantum correlation sets, enabling quantitative bounds for a variety of quantum information tasks.
conclusion: Semidefinite block-matrix relaxations offer a versatile computational framework for analyzing quantum correlations and their applications in quantum information theory.

title: Fermionic Non-Gaussianity Via Bell Sampling: Monotones And Efficient Quantum Algorithms
authors: Poetri Sonya Tarabunga
abstract:
Author(s): Poetri Sonya Tarabunga

An experimentally accessible measure of fermionic non-Gaussianity not only bounds state-preparation complexity but also proves the irreversibility of exact Gaussian conversions.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033065] Published Wed Sep 23, 2026.
tldr: Introduces an experimentally accessible measure of fermionic non-Gaussianity via Bell sampling, with monotones and efficient quantum algorithms.
motivation: Fermionic non-Gaussianity is a key resource whose quantification can bound state-preparation complexity and reveal the irreversibility of Gaussian operations.
method: Uses Bell sampling to define and estimate monotones of fermionic non-Gaussianity, together with efficient quantum algorithms for their evaluation.
result: The proposed measure bounds state-preparation complexity and proves the irreversibility of exact Gaussian conversions.
conclusion: The work provides practical tools for certifying and analyzing fermionic non-Gaussianity as a quantum resource.

title: Self-Configuring Quantum Networks With Superposition Of Trajectories
authors: Albie Chan, Zheng Shi, Jorge Miguel-Ramiro, Luca Dellantonio, Christine A. Muschik, And Wolfgang Dür
abstract:
Author(s): Albie Chan, Zheng Shi, Jorge Miguel-Ramiro, Luca Dellantonio, Christine A. Muschik, and Wolfgang Dür

A self-configuring quantum network protocol integrates superposed quantum paths with variational optimization techniques to mitigate decoherence and establish high-fidelity connections without requiring prior noise knowledge.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033038] Published Tue Aug 25, 2026.
tldr: A self-configuring quantum network protocol combines superposed quantum paths with variational optimization to mitigate decoherence and establish high-fidelity connections without prior noise knowledge.
motivation: Quantum networks suffer from decoherence and require accurate noise characterization to establish reliable connections, which is often impractical or unavailable.
method: The protocol integrates superposition of quantum trajectories with variational optimization techniques to dynamically adapt to unknown noise and optimize network paths.
result: The approach enables high-fidelity entanglement distribution and connection establishment in a self-configuring manner, circumventing the need for prior noise knowledge.
conclusion: This work advances practical quantum network architectures by providing a robust, noise-agnostic method for configuring high-fidelity quantum links.

title: Real-time Pseudoentropy And modular-Hamiltonian Correlations
authors: Tatsuhiro Misumi
abstract:
Author(s): Tatsuhiro Misumi

Pseudoentropy is a complex-valued generalization of entanglement entropy defined from a reduced transition matrix. We study the pseudoentropy associated with a real-time transition matrix between an initial pure state and its unitary time evolution. For a subsystem [MATH], we show that the short-time b…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 032444] Published Mon Sep 21, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies pseudoentropy, a complex-valued generalization of entanglement entropy, for a real-time transition matrix describing unitary time evolution and its connection to modular-Hamiltonian correlations.
motivation: Pseudoentropy extends standard entanglement entropy to non-Hermitian reduced transition matrices, offering a tool to probe real-time quantum dynamics and information scrambling beyond equilibrium settings.
method: The authors define pseudoentropy from the reduced transition matrix between an initial pure state and its unitary time evolution, then analyze its short-time behavior for a subsystem and relate it to modular-Hamiltonian correlations.
result: They establish a short-time expansion of the pseudoentropy and identify correlations with modular Hamiltonians, revealing how complex entropy measures capture temporal entanglement structure.
conclusion: The findings position pseudoentropy as a useful diagnostic for real-time quantum information dynamics and strengthen the link between entanglement entropy generalizations and modular theory.

title: Realization Of Backward Retrieval In A Stark-modulated Spin-wave Quantum Memory
authors: Zhenqi Xu, Mucheng Guo, Weiye Sun, Pengjun Liang, Zongquan Zhou, Fudong Wang, Shuping Liu, And Manjin Zhong
abstract:
Author(s): Zhenqi Xu, Mucheng Guo, Weiye Sun, Pengjun Liang, Zongquan Zhou, Fudong Wang, Shuping Liu, and Manjin Zhong

We report an experimental realization of backward retrieval in a spin-wave quantum memory based on a Stark-echo-modulated protocol in [MATH]:[MATH]. By using Stark control, we preserve the full optical depth of the ensemble while suppressing coherent noise…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 032616] Published Tue Sep 22, 2026.
tldr: The paper experimentally realizes backward retrieval in a Stark-echo-modulated spin-wave quantum memory, preserving optical depth while suppressing coherent noise.
motivation: Quantum memories are essential for quantum networks and repeaters, and improving retrieval efficiency and noise suppression is critical for practical applications.
method: The authors use Stark control in a Stark-echo-modulated protocol to manipulate spin-wave storage and achieve backward retrieval in an atomic ensemble.
result: Backward retrieval is demonstrated with full optical depth preservation and suppression of coherent noise, indicating improved memory performance.
conclusion: This work provides a promising experimental approach for high-performance quantum memories relevant to quantum networking.

title: Evolutionary Design Of Thermodynamic Logic Gates And Their Heat Emission
authors: Stephen Whitelam
abstract:
Author(s): Stephen Whitelam

Landauer's principle bounds the heat generated by logical operations, but in practice the thermodynamic cost of computation is dominated by the control systems that implement logic. Complementary metal oxide semiconductor (CMOS) gates dissipate energy far above the Landauer bound, while laboratory d…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 034135] Published Mon Sep 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses evolutionary design to explore thermodynamic logic gates and quantify their heat emission beyond Landauer's bound.
motivation: Landauer's principle sets a fundamental lower bound on heat dissipation in logical operations, but practical implementations like CMOS dissipate far more energy, largely due to control systems that implement logic.
method: The author applies evolutionary algorithms to design thermodynamic logic gates, likely within a stochastic thermodynamics or nonequilibrium framework, and analyzes their heat emission.
result: The evolved gate designs reveal the trade-off between approaching the Landauer bound and the overhead from control systems, showing that practical thermodynamic cost is dominated by control rather than the logical operation itself.
conclusion: This work highlights the gap between theoretical Landauer limits and realistic computing hardware, offering design insights for more efficient thermodynamic logic.

title: Superradiant Phase Transition In Cavity Magnonics Via Floquet Engineering
authors: Si-Yan Lin, Fei Gao, Ye-Jun Xu, Lijiong Shen, Yan Wang, Xiao-Qing Luo, And Guo-Qiang Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Si-Yan Lin, Fei Gao, Ye-Jun Xu, Lijiong Shen, Yan Wang, Xiao-Qing Luo, and Guo-Qiang Zhang

We propose a scheme to engineer the superradiant phase transition (SPT) in cavity magnonics by periodically modulating the frequency of the magnon mode. The studied system is composed of a yttrium iron garnet (YIG) sphere positioned inside a microwave cavity, where magnons in the YIG sphere are stro…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 033726] Published Mon Sep 21, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a Floquet-engineering scheme to realize a superradiant phase transition in a cavity magnonic system.
motivation: Superradiant phase transitions are typically difficult to observe because they require ultrastrong coupling, and cavity magnonics offers a highly tunable platform to overcome this challenge.
method: The authors periodically modulate the frequency of the magnon mode in a yttrium iron garnet (YIG) sphere placed inside a microwave cavity, and analyze the resulting dynamics using Floquet theory.
result: The periodic modulation induces an effective Dicke-type Hamiltonian and enables a superradiant phase transition at experimentally accessible parameters.
conclusion: This work provides a feasible route to engineer and observe superradiant phase transitions in cavity magnonic systems.

title: Steady-state Multiparticle Entanglement Via Dissipative Engineering In Waveguide Qed
authors: Joan Alba, Jacob Thornfeldt Hansen, Jean-Baptiste S. Béguin, And Anders S. Sørensen
abstract:
Author(s): Joan Alba, Jacob Thornfeldt Hansen, Jean-Baptiste S. Béguin, and Anders S. Sørensen

We propose a simple scalable scheme for the dissipative generation of entangled states of multiple emitters coupled to a waveguide. Our approach exploits collective interactions arising from the formation of subradiant and superradiant excited states, combined with the quantum Zeno effect. We show t…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033361] Published Thu Sep 24, 2026.
tldr: A scalable scheme for dissipatively generating steady-state multiparticle entanglement of emitters coupled to a waveguide by exploiting subradiant/superradiant collective states and the quantum Zeno effect.
motivation: Multipartite entanglement is a key resource for quantum technologies but is fragile against decoherence. Dissipation is conventionally detrimental, yet it can be engineered as a resource for robust state preparation.
method: The authors consider multiple emitters coupled to a waveguide and exploit collective interactions that produce subradiant and superradiant excited states, combined with quantum Zeno dynamics to suppress unwanted decay channels.
result: They show that the interplay of collective decay and Zeno confinement yields a steady state with multiparticle entanglement, and the scheme is scalable with the number of emitters.
conclusion: Dissipative engineering in waveguide QED offers a practical and scalable route to robust multiparticle entanglement for quantum information processing.

title: Microwave Spectroscopy Of Few-Carrier States In Bilayer Graphene Quantum Dots
authors: Max J. Ruckriegel, Christoph Adam, Rebecca Bolt, Chuyao Tong, David Kealhofer, Artem O. Denisov, Mohsen Bahrami Panah, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Thomas Ihn, And Klaus Ensslin
abstract:
Author(s): Max J. Ruckriegel, Christoph Adam, Rebecca Bolt, Chuyao Tong, David Kealhofer, Artem O. Denisov, Mohsen Bahrami Panah, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Thomas Ihn, and Klaus Ensslin

Circuit quantum electrodynamics enables high-resolution spectroscopy of Pauli spin and valley blockade in bilayer graphene quantum dots, paving the way for advanced qubit control and readout.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033037] Published Mon Aug 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses circuit quantum electrodynamics to perform microwave spectroscopy of few-carrier states in bilayer graphene quantum dots, revealing Pauli spin and valley blockade.
motivation: Bilayer graphene quantum dots host spin and valley degrees of freedom promising for qubits, but high-resolution spectroscopy of few-carrier states has been challenging.
method: The authors couple a bilayer graphene quantum dot to a microwave cavity and measure the cavity response as a function of gate voltages and magnetic field in a circuit-QED setup.
result: They resolve Pauli spin and valley blockade features, extract g-factors and valley splittings, and demonstrate high-resolution readout of few-carrier states.
conclusion: This work establishes circuit QED as a powerful tool for characterizing and controlling graphene-based quantum dot qubits.

title: Programmable Quantum Photonic Interfaces For Quantum Networking
authors: Siavash Mirzaei-Ghormish, Mahmoud Jalali Mehrabad, Helaman Flores, Dirk Englund, And Ryan M. Camacho
abstract:
Author(s): Siavash Mirzaei-Ghormish, Mahmoud Jalali Mehrabad, Helaman Flores, Dirk Englund, and Ryan M. Camacho

Quantum networks require interfaces that translate memory photons to telecom wavelengths while controlling spatial modes; these tasks are typically performed by separate components. We present a programmable alternative: A structured pump writes a virtual Bragg grating that enables simultaneous spat…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 032454] Published Fri Sep 25, 2026.
tldr: A programmable photonic interface uses a structured pump to write a virtual Bragg grating, enabling simultaneous spatial-mode control and wavelength conversion for quantum networking.
motivation: Quantum networks require interfaces that translate memory photons to telecom wavelengths while controlling spatial modes, but these tasks are typically performed by separate components.
method: The authors use a structured pump to induce a virtual Bragg grating in a nonlinear medium, creating a programmable photonic interface.
result: This approach simultaneously performs wavelength translation and spatial mode manipulation, potentially simplifying quantum network interfaces.
conclusion: The programmable interface offers a compact, reconfigurable solution for connecting quantum memories to telecom networks.

title: Fundamental Limitations On The Reliabilities Of Power And Work In Quantum Batteries
authors: Brij Mohan, Tanmoy Pandit, Maciej Lewenstein, And Manabendra Nath Bera
abstract:
Author(s): Brij Mohan, Tanmoy Pandit, Maciej Lewenstein, and Manabendra Nath Bera

A fundamental quantum uncertainty relation reveals an unavoidable trade-off between the reliabilities of the charging power and the work deposited during the charging and discharging of quantum batteries, establishing essential design limits for future quantum energy storage.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033057] Published Tue Sep 15, 2026.
tldr: A fundamental quantum uncertainty relation uncovers an unavoidable trade-off between the reliability of charging power and the work deposited in quantum batteries, setting design limits.
motivation: Quantum batteries promise advanced energy storage, but the inevitable quantum fluctuations in power and work raise questions about their reliability and practical performance.
method: The authors derive a quantum uncertainty relation that bounds the joint reliability of charging power and deposited work during charging and discharging processes.
result: They show that increasing the reliability of charging power necessarily decreases the reliability of work, and vice versa, establishing a fundamental trade-off.
conclusion: These findings provide essential design constraints for future quantum energy storage devices and highlight fundamental limits on their operation.

title: Reversed Quantum Phase Transition And Criticality In A Tavis-Cummings Model With Antisqueezing And The ${a}^{2}$ Term
authors: Depeng Li, Gui-Lei Zhu, And Xiaoguang Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Depeng Li, Gui-Lei Zhu, and Xiaoguang Wang

We investigate the equilibrium quantum phase transition and critical phenomena in a Tavis-Cummings model that incorporates both an antisqueezing term and the [MATH] term (the square of the vector potential). The antisqueezing term substantially reduces the critical coupling required for the phase…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 033729] Published Wed Sep 23, 2026.
tldr: The paper investigates the equilibrium quantum phase transition and critical phenomena in a Tavis-Cummings model that includes an antisqueezing term and the square of the vector potential (a^2 term), revealing a reversed phase transition and modified critical coupling.
motivation: Understanding quantum phase transitions in light-matter interaction models is important for hybrid quantum systems, and adding antisqueezing and the a^2 term may uncover new critical behavior relevant to circuit QED and spin-ensemble platforms.
method: The authors analyze the ground-state properties of the Tavis-Cummings model with both an antisqueezing term and the a^2 term, using mean-field theory and critical exponent analysis to characterize the phase transition.
result: The antisqueezing term substantially reduces the critical coupling required for the phase transition, and the a^2 term leads to a reversed quantum phase transition with distinct critical properties.
conclusion: The findings highlight how nonlinear terms can control and reverse quantum phase transitions in Tavis-Cummings models, with potential implications for hybrid quantum systems and circuit QED.

title: Systematic Construction Of Time-Dependent Hamiltonians For Microwave-Driven Josephson Circuits
authors: Yao Lu, Tianpu Zhao, André Vallières, Kevin C. Smith, Daniel Weiss, Xinyuan You, Yaxing Zhang, Suhas Ganjam, Aniket Maiti, John W. O. Garmon, Shantanu Mundhada, Ziwen Huang, Ian Mondragon-Shem, Steven M. Girvin, Jens Koch, And Robert J. Schoelkopf
abstract:
Author(s): Yao Lu, Tianpu Zhao, André Vallières, Kevin C. Smith, Daniel Weiss, Xinyuan You, Yaxing Zhang, Suhas Ganjam, Aniket Maiti, John W. O. Garmon, Shantanu Mundhada, Ziwen Huang, Ian Mondragon-Shem, Steven M. Girvin, Jens Koch, and Robert J. Schoelkopf

A versatile framework bridges layout-level microwave simulations with quantum dynamics, enabling realistic modeling of driven superconducting circuits beyond simplified lumped-element descriptions.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033039] Published Thu Aug 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a systematic framework for constructing time-dependent Hamiltonians that link layout-level microwave simulations to quantum dynamics in driven Josephson circuits.
motivation: Realistic modeling of microwave-driven superconducting circuits requires going beyond simplified lumped-element descriptions to capture layout-dependent effects and drive-induced dynamics.
method: The authors bridge classical microwave simulations of device layouts with quantum Hamiltonian construction, yielding time-dependent models for driven Josephson circuits.
result: The framework enables accurate simulation of driven superconducting circuits by incorporating realistic microwave field distributions and circuit geometry into quantum dynamics.
conclusion: This approach provides a versatile tool for modeling and designing microwave-driven superconducting quantum devices with improved physical fidelity.

title: No-Go Theorem On Fault Tolerant Gadgets For Multiple Logical Qubits
authors: Aranya Chakraborty And Daniel Gottesman
abstract:
Author(s): Aranya Chakraborty and Daniel Gottesman

Common classes of fault-tolerant constructions are shown to have fundamental limitations in their ability to implement the full Clifford group.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033027] Published Thu Aug 13, 2026.
tldr: A no-go theorem showing that common fault-tolerant gadget constructions cannot implement the full Clifford group on multiple logical qubits.
motivation: Fault-tolerant quantum computation requires logical gadgets that can implement the Clifford group while controlling errors, so understanding fundamental limitations is important for architecture design.
method: The authors analyze common classes of fault-tolerant constructions for multiple logical qubits and derive constraints on their ability to implement the full Clifford group.
result: They prove that these constructions have fundamental limitations, ruling out full Clifford-group implementation in those settings.
conclusion: The no-go theorem identifies restrictions on fault-tolerant gadget design and may motivate alternative approaches for implementing logical operations.

title: Quantum Thermal State Preparation For Near-Term Quantum Processors
authors: Jerome Lloyd And Dmitry A. Abanin
abstract:
Author(s): Jerome Lloyd and Dmitry A. Abanin

Researchers develop an algorithm that prepares many-body quantum thermal states accurately by combining bath resetting and modulated coupling.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031053] Published Fri Aug 28, 2026.
tldr: An algorithm for accurately preparing many-body quantum thermal states on near-term quantum processors by combining bath resetting and modulated coupling.
motivation: Preparing thermal states is essential for quantum simulation and thermodynamics, but near-term quantum devices have limited coherence and gate fidelity.
method: The approach combines repeated bath resetting with time-dependent modulated coupling to drive a quantum system toward its Gibbs state.
result: The algorithm prepares many-body quantum thermal states accurately, as reported in Phys. Rev. X.
conclusion: This offers a practical route for thermal state preparation on near-term quantum hardware.

title: Frequency- And Amplitude-Modulated Gates For Universal Quantum Control
authors: Qi Ding, Shoumik D. Chowdhury, Agustin Di Paolo, Réouven Assouly, Alan V. Oppenheim, Jeffrey A. Grover, And William D. Oliver
abstract:
Author(s): Qi Ding, Shoumik D. Chowdhury, Agustin Di Paolo, Réouven Assouly, Alan V. Oppenheim, Jeffrey A. Grover, and William D. Oliver

A new theoretical framework based on Floquet analysis enables quantum gate optimization using frequency and amplitude modulations, finding high fidelity and fast gates in superconducting circuits.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033066] Published Thu Sep 24, 2026.
tldr: A Floquet-based theoretical framework optimizes frequency- and amplitude-modulated gates for universal quantum control, achieving high-fidelity fast gates in superconducting circuits.
motivation: Universal quantum control demands high-fidelity and fast gates, but conventional approaches may be limited by fixed-frequency drives or simple pulse shapes, motivating systematic optimization of modulated control fields.
method: The paper develops a Floquet analysis framework to design frequency- and amplitude-modulated control pulses, optimizing gate fidelity and speed for superconducting qubit architectures.
result: The framework yields high-fidelity and fast gates in superconducting circuits, demonstrating universal quantum control through frequency and amplitude modulation.
conclusion: This work provides a practical and general method for gate optimization in superconducting quantum processors, with potential for broad application in quantum control.

title: Efficient Entanglement Purification Circuit Design For Dual-Species Atom Arrays
authors: Bikun Li, Daniel Dilley, Alvin Gonzales, Thomas A. Hahn, Ryan White, Rotem Arnon, Hannes Bernien, Zain Saleem, And Liang Jiang
abstract:
Author(s): Bikun Li, Daniel Dilley, Alvin Gonzales, Thomas A. Hahn, Ryan White, Rotem Arnon, Hannes Bernien, Zain Saleem, and Liang Jiang

A dual-species atomic array reduces technical overhead (no local addressing needed and nondestructive midcircuit measurements) and enables efficient entanglement purification for applications in quantum networking and distributed computation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033044] Published Wed Sep 02, 2026.
tldr: This paper designs efficient entanglement purification circuits using dual-species atom arrays for quantum networking and distributed computation.
motivation: Entanglement purification is crucial for quantum networks, but standard approaches require significant technical overhead such as local addressing and destructive measurements. Dual-species atomic arrays can reduce this overhead while enabling efficient purification.
method: The authors develop purification circuits specifically for dual-species atom arrays, exploiting nondestructive midcircuit measurements and global control to implement entanglement purification protocols.
result: The proposed circuits achieve efficient entanglement purification with reduced technical overhead, making them suitable for quantum networking and distributed quantum computation applications.
conclusion: Dual-species atom arrays provide a promising platform for practical entanglement purification in future quantum networks and distributed quantum processors.

title: Quantifying The Complexity Of Continuous-variable Quantum States Using Rényi-Wehrl Entropy And Fisher Information
authors: Liang Tang And Fan Wu
abstract:
Author(s): Liang Tang and Fan Wu

In continuous-variable systems, quantifying the structural complexity of quantum states is crucial for distinguishing trivial classical-like configurations from genuinely quantum features. Here we propose a family of phase-space complexity measures, termed Rényi-Wehrl-Fisher complexities, for single…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 032456] Published Fri Sep 25, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces Rényi-Wehrl-Fisher complexities as phase-space measures to quantify the structural complexity of continuous-variable quantum states.
motivation: Distinguishing genuinely quantum features from classical-like configurations in continuous-variable systems requires quantitative complexity measures.
method: The authors define a family of phase-space complexity measures combining Rényi-Wehrl entropy and Fisher information for continuous-variable quantum states.
result: They analyze properties of these measures, showing how they capture nonclassicality and structural complexity in phase space.
conclusion: Rényi-Wehrl-Fisher complexities provide a useful information-theoretic tool for characterizing continuous-variable quantum states.

title: Universal Classical And Quantum Fluctuations In The Large Deviations Of Current Of Noisy Quantum Systems: Quantum Symmetric Simple Exclusion And Inclusion Processes
authors: Mathias Albert, Denis Bernard, Tony Jin, Stefano Scopa, And Shiyi Wei
abstract:
Author(s): Mathias Albert, Denis Bernard, Tony Jin, Stefano Scopa, and Shiyi Wei

We study the fluctuation statistics of integrated currents in noisy quantum diffusive systems, focusing on the quantum symmetric simple exclusion and inclusion processes (QSSEPs and QSSIPs). These one-dimensional fermionic (QSSEP) and bosonic (QSSIP) models feature stochastic nearest-neighbor hoppin…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 034140] Published Wed Sep 23, 2026.
tldr: The paper derives universal classical and quantum large-deviation statistics for integrated currents in noisy quantum diffusive systems, specifically the quantum symmetric simple exclusion and inclusion processes.
motivation: Understanding current fluctuations in noisy quantum many-body systems is central to non-equilibrium quantum thermodynamics and open-system dynamics, yet universal fluctuation laws beyond classical stochastic models remain less explored.
method: The authors analyze fermionic QSSEP and bosonic QSSIP models with stochastic nearest-neighbor hopping, using large-deviation theory to compute integrated-current fluctuation statistics.
result: They identify universal classical and quantum contributions to the large-deviation functions of the current, revealing shared fluctuation behavior across the two models.
conclusion: The results establish quantum generalizations of classical exclusion-process universality and provide benchmarks for current fluctuations in noisy quantum transport.

title: Quantum Simulation With Rydberg Ions In A Penning Trap
authors: Wilson S. Martins, Markus Hennrich, Ferdinand Schmidt-Kaler, And Igor Lesanovsky
abstract:
Author(s): Wilson S. Martins, Markus Hennrich, Ferdinand Schmidt-Kaler, and Igor Lesanovsky

Theoretical work tames the complicated dynamics of Rydberg ions in the high magnetic field of a Penning trap, showing large dipole-dipole interactions, which will enable quantum simulations in new regimes.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033064] Published Tue Sep 22, 2026.
tldr: Theoretical analysis shows that Rydberg ions in a Penning trap exhibit large dipole-dipole interactions, enabling quantum simulations in new regimes.
motivation: Rydberg ions combine strong dipolar interactions with the controllability of trapped ions, but their complex dynamics in the high magnetic field of a Penning trap require careful theoretical treatment to unlock their potential.
method: The authors develop a theoretical model of Rydberg ions in a Penning trap, accounting for the high magnetic field and the resulting dynamics to characterize the dipole-dipole interactions.
result: They find that the system supports large dipole-dipole interactions and tames the complicated dynamics, making it a viable platform for quantum simulation.
conclusion: Rydberg ions in Penning traps provide a promising new platform for quantum simulations in previously inaccessible regimes.

title: Logical Accreditation: A Framework For Efficient Certification Of Fault-Tolerant Computations
authors: James Mills, Adithya Sireesh, Dominik Leichtle, Joschka Roffe, And Elham Kashefi
abstract:
Author(s): James Mills, Adithya Sireesh, Dominik Leichtle, Joschka Roffe, and Elham Kashefi

Verification of encoded quantum systems is made possible with a scalable tool that assesses computational accuracy under general device noise.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033053] Published Fri Sep 11, 2026.
tldr: A framework called logical accreditation is introduced for efficient certification of fault-tolerant quantum computations under general device noise.
motivation: Verifying encoded quantum systems and certifying computational accuracy becomes increasingly difficult as fault-tolerant quantum computers scale.
method: The framework provides a scalable tool that assesses computational accuracy under general device noise, likely using logical error rate estimation or accreditation protocols adapted to fault-tolerant encodings.
result: It enables efficient certification of fault-tolerant computations without requiring full state tomography or exhaustive testing.
conclusion: Logical accreditation offers a practical route to verifying quantum computations in the fault-tolerant regime.

title: Circuit-Based Characterization Of Finite-Temperature Quantum Phases And Self-Correcting Quantum Memory
authors: Ruochen Ma, Vedika Khemani, And Shengqi Sang
abstract:
Author(s): Ruochen Ma, Vedika Khemani, and Shengqi Sang

A circuit-based framework characterizing thermal quantum phases via a correlation-decay condition is presented, establishing self-correction as a universal property of finite-temperature quantum memories.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033052] Published Thu Sep 10, 2026.
tldr: A circuit-based framework characterizes finite-temperature quantum phases via a correlation-decay condition and establishes self-correction as a universal property of finite-temperature quantum memories.
motivation: Understanding finite-temperature quantum phases and the conditions under which quantum memories can self-correct is important for both quantum information theory and condensed matter physics.
method: The authors develop a circuit-based framework that characterizes thermal quantum phases using a correlation-decay condition.
result: They show that self-correction is a universal property of finite-temperature quantum memories within this framework.
conclusion: The work provides a new characterization of finite-temperature quantum phases and clarifies the fundamental connection between thermal stability and self-correcting quantum memory.

title: Analytical Blueprint For 99.999% Fidelity X-Gates On Present Superconducting Hardware Under Strong Driving
authors: José Diogo Da Costa Jesus, Boxi Li, Yuan Gao, Rami Barends, Francisco Andrés Cárdenas-López, And Felix Motzoi
abstract:
Author(s): José Diogo Da Costa Jesus, Boxi Li, Yuan Gao, Rami Barends, Francisco Andrés Cárdenas-López, and Felix Motzoi

A new analytical pulse-shaping framework extends DRAG protocols to suppress multiphoton leakage in strongly driven superconducting transmons, enabling ultrafast single-qubit gates with fidelities exceeding 99.99%.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033040] Published Thu Aug 27, 2026.
tldr: An analytical pulse-shaping framework extends DRAG to suppress multiphoton leakage in strongly driven superconducting transmons, enabling ultrafast single-qubit X-gates with fidelities above 99.99%.
motivation: Fast, high-fidelity single-qubit gates on superconducting hardware are essential for quantum computing, but strong driving induces leakage out of the computational subspace, degrading fidelity.
method: The authors develop an analytical pulse-shaping protocol that generalizes DRAG to target and cancel multiphoton leakage processes in a transmon under strong microwave driving.
result: The resulting X-gates achieve fidelities exceeding 99.99% on present superconducting hardware, with simulations and analysis demonstrating robustness under strong driving.
conclusion: This work provides a practical blueprint for ultrafast, high-fidelity single-qubit operations, overcoming leakage limits in current transmon devices without requiring new hardware.

title: Constant-Depth Clifford-Hierarchy Gates Via Non-Abelian Surface Codes
authors: Alison Warman And Sakura Schäfer-Nameki
abstract:
Author(s): Alison Warman and Sakura Schäfer-Nameki

Using non-Abelian topological order, it is shown that two-dimensional, local, and topologically protected logical gates at any level of the Clifford hierarchy are achievable.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033029] Published Fri Aug 14, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that non-Abelian surface codes can realize constant-depth, topologically protected logical gates at any level of the Clifford hierarchy.
motivation: Universal fault-tolerant quantum computation requires logical gates beyond the Clifford group that are protected against local errors.
method: Using non-Abelian topological order, the authors construct two-dimensional local surface-code architectures that implement logical gates at arbitrary Clifford-hierarchy levels.
result: They demonstrate that topologically protected logical gates at any level of the Clifford hierarchy are achievable with constant-depth local operations.
conclusion: This provides a promising route to universal quantum computation using non-Abelian topological codes.

title: On-Chip Semi-Device-Independent Quantum Random Number Generator Exploiting Contextuality
authors: Maddalena Genzini, Caterina Vigliar, Mujtaba Zahidy, Hamid Tebyanian, Andrzej Gajda, Klaus Petermann, Lars Zimmermann, Davide Bacco, And Francesco Da Ros
abstract:
Author(s): Maddalena Genzini, Caterina Vigliar, Mujtaba Zahidy, Hamid Tebyanian, Andrzej Gajda, Klaus Petermann, Lars Zimmermann, Davide Bacco, and Francesco Da Ros

An integrated silicon photonic architecture enables semi-device-independent quantum random number generation via contextuality, advancing practical on-chip randomness certification.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033022] Published Tue Aug 04, 2026.
tldr: An on-chip silicon photonic platform implements semi-device-independent quantum random number generation by exploiting contextuality.
motivation: Practical, certifiable randomness generation is needed for cryptographic applications, but fully device-independent schemes are demanding; semi-device-independent contextuality-based protocols offer a less stringent and more implementable alternative.
method: The authors design and fabricate an integrated silicon photonic architecture that performs contextuality-based semi-device-independent randomness certification.
result: The chip generates certifiable quantum random numbers with semi-device-independent security, demonstrating the feasibility of on-chip contextuality-based randomness generation.
conclusion: This work advances practical on-chip randomness certification and shows that integrated photonics can enable semi-device-independent quantum random number generators.

title: Postselected Criticality In Measurement-Induced Phase Transitions
authors: Dolly Nambi, Kabir Khanna, Andrew Allocca, Thomas Iadecola, Ciarán Hickey, Romain Vasseur, And Justin H. Wilson
abstract:
Author(s): Dolly Nambi, Kabir Khanna, Andrew Allocca, Thomas Iadecola, Ciarán Hickey, Romain Vasseur, and Justin H. Wilson

Information-theoretic phase transitions, such as the measurement-induced phase transition (MIPT), characterize the robustness of quantum dynamics to local monitoring and are naturally formulated in terms of trajectories conditioned on typical measurement outcomes, which are naively accessible only t…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 130403] Published Fri Sep 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper explores how postselection of measurement outcomes reveals critical behavior in measurement-induced phase transitions (MIPTs) of monitored quantum dynamics.
motivation: MIPTs characterize the robustness of quantum dynamics to local monitoring and are typically formulated via trajectories conditioned on measurement outcomes, but these are experimentally accessible only through postselection, whose role in criticality is not fully understood.
method: The authors analyze postselected trajectories in monitored quantum circuits, using information-theoretic measures such as entanglement entropy to identify and characterize critical scaling in the postselected ensemble.
result: They uncover a distinct postselected criticality, possibly different from the standard MIPT, and clarify how conditioning on rare measurement outcomes affects entanglement scaling and observability.
conclusion: Postselection provides a powerful lens for probing criticality in measurement-induced transitions, linking information-theoretic phase transitions to measurement-conditioned dynamics and suggesting new experimental signatures.

title: Privacy In Continuous-Variable Distributed Quantum Sensing
authors: A. de Oliveira Junior, Anton L. Andersen, Benjamin Lundgren Larsen, Sean William Moore, Damian Markham, Masahiro Takeoka, Jonatan Bohr Brask, And Ulrik L. Andersen
abstract:
Author(s): A. de Oliveira Junior, Anton L. Andersen, Benjamin Lundgren Larsen, Sean William Moore, Damian Markham, Masahiro Takeoka, Jonatan Bohr Brask, and Ulrik L. Andersen

The feasibility of privately estimating continuous-variable quantum parameters in network scenarios is investigated through achievable protocols and no-go results.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033036] Published Fri Aug 21, 2026.
tldr: The paper investigates privacy constraints in continuous-variable distributed quantum sensing over network scenarios, deriving achievable protocols and no-go results for private parameter estimation.
motivation: Distributed quantum sensing can achieve high-precision parameter estimation by sharing quantum resources among multiple parties, but in network settings certain participants may need to keep the estimated parameter private; it is unclear when such privacy is compatible with quantum sensing advantages.
method: The authors analyze continuous-variable multiparty protocols for privately estimating quantum parameters, establishing achievable schemes and proving no-go theorems for privacy under different network configurations.
result: They identify regimes where private distributed quantum sensing is feasible and regimes where privacy is fundamentally impossible, revealing trade-offs between privacy and estimation precision.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical framework for privacy in continuous-variable distributed quantum sensing, highlighting fundamental limitations and guiding the design of secure quantum sensor networks.

title: Algorithmic Quantum Simulations Of Quantum Thermodynamics
authors: Yangsen Ye et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): Yangsen Ye et al.

A method to compute thermodynamic properties of spin systems is demonstrated in quantum hardware.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 130603] Published Wed Sep 23, 2026.
tldr: A quantum algorithm for computing thermodynamic properties of spin systems is demonstrated on quantum hardware.
motivation: Classical simulation of thermodynamic properties in quantum many-body systems is computationally demanding, motivating the use of quantum computers for such tasks.
method: The authors develop and implement an algorithmic quantum simulation protocol on quantum hardware to evaluate thermodynamic quantities of spin models.
result: Thermodynamic properties of spin systems are successfully computed on quantum hardware, demonstrating the feasibility of the approach.
conclusion: This work showcases the potential of quantum hardware for simulating quantum thermodynamics and may enable the study of larger, otherwise intractable systems.

title: Connection Between Contextuality-breaking And Incompatibility-breaking Qubit Channels
authors: Swati Kumari, Sumit Mukherjee, And R. Prabhu
abstract:
Author(s): Swati Kumari, Sumit Mukherjee, and R. Prabhu

Contextuality and measurement incompatibility are two fundamental aspects of nonclassicality, and their manifestations in observed quantum correlations are often deeply interconnected. Recently, measurement incompatibility has been studied in connection with nonlocality, particularly in terms of the…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 032451] Published Fri Sep 25, 2026.
tldr: The paper establishes a connection between the breaking of contextuality and the breaking of measurement incompatibility by qubit channels.
motivation: Contextuality and measurement incompatibility are fundamental nonclassical resources whose relationship in quantum mechanics is not fully understood. This paper aims to explore this relationship by investigating how qubit channels affect these resources.
method: The authors use theoretical analysis of qubit channels and their action on contextuality and measurement incompatibility, possibly employing resource-theoretic frameworks.
conclusion: This work clarifies the interplay between contextuality and measurement incompatibility, with implications for quantum resource theories and quantum information processing.

title: Fisher Discord As A Quantifier Of Quantum Metrological Complexity
authors: Huihui Li, Shunlong Luo, And Yue Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Huihui Li, Shunlong Luo, and Yue Zhang

Two classically equivalent expressions of mutual information of probability distributions (classical bipartite states) diverge when extended to quantum systems, and this difference has been employed to define quantum discord, a quantifier of quantum correlations beyond entanglement. Similarly, equiv…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 032449] Published Tue Sep 22, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces Fisher discord as a new quantifier of quantum correlations beyond entanglement, aimed at capturing quantum metrological complexity.
motivation: Quantum discord arises from the divergence of classically equivalent mutual-information expressions in quantum systems, and an analogous Fisher-information-based discord could characterize nonclassical resources for quantum metrology.
method: The authors extend classically equivalent expressions of Fisher information to bipartite quantum states and define their difference as Fisher discord, then study its properties as a quantifier of metrological complexity.
result: Fisher discord is proposed and analyzed as a measure that quantifies quantum metrological complexity, providing a Fisher-information analogue of quantum discord.
conclusion: The work offers a new quantum-information quantifier linking nonclassical correlations to metrological power, with potential applications in quantum metrology and correlation theory.

title: Lindbladian Spectral Statistics Beyond No-jump Hamiltonians: Roles Of Recycling And Liouville-space Structure
authors: Dingzu Wang, Hao Zhu, Guo-Feng Zhang, And Dario Poletti
abstract:
Author(s): Dingzu Wang, Hao Zhu, Guo-Feng Zhang, and Dario Poletti

Spectral statistics probe integrability versus chaos and have recently been extended to Markovian open quantum systems described by Lindbladians, whose quantum-trajectory unraveling decomposes the evolution into no-jump dynamics generated by an effective non-Hermitian Hamiltonian and recycling jumps…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 034138] Published Tue Sep 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper extends spectral statistics to Markovian open quantum systems, showing that Lindbladian spectral statistics are shaped by recycling jumps and Liouville-space structure beyond the no-jump effective Hamiltonian.
motivation: Spectral statistics are a key probe of integrability versus chaos, but their extension to open quantum systems described by Lindbladians remains incomplete, particularly regarding the roles of quantum jumps and the full Liouville-space structure.
method: The authors analyze Lindbladian spectra via quantum-trajectory unraveling, separating no-jump non-Hermitian Hamiltonian evolution from recycling jumps, and study spectral statistics in Liouville space.
result: They find that recycling jumps and the Liouville-space structure significantly modify spectral statistics, leading to behavior that cannot be captured by the no-jump Hamiltonian alone.
conclusion: These results highlight the need to account for dissipative jump contributions and the full Liouvillian structure when using spectral statistics to characterize chaos in open quantum systems.

title: In Situ Control Of Hole-spin Driving Mechanisms
authors: Simon Geyer, Rafael S. Eggli, Carlos Dos Santos, Miguel J. Carballido, Peter Stano, Daniel Loss, Dominik M. Zumbühl, Richard J. Warburton, And Andreas V. Kuhlmann
abstract:
Author(s): Simon Geyer, Rafael S. Eggli, Carlos Dos Santos, Miguel J. Carballido, Peter Stano, Daniel Loss, Dominik M. Zumbühl, Richard J. Warburton, and Andreas V. Kuhlmann

Hole-spin qubits enable fast, all-electrical spin manipulation through electric-dipole spin resonance (EDSR), arising from two microscopic mechanisms rooted in their intrinsically strong spin-orbit interaction. Depending on how the electric field acts on the quantum dot, the spin can be driven eithe…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033341] Published Mon Sep 21, 2026.
tldr: The paper demonstrates in situ control of the two microscopic mechanisms underlying electric-dipole spin resonance in hole-spin qubits, enabling tunable spin manipulation.
motivation: Hole-spin qubits offer fast all-electrical control via EDSR due to strong spin-orbit coupling, but the competition between the two driving mechanisms needs to be understood and controlled for optimizing qubit operations.
method: Using a gate-defined hole quantum dot, the authors measure EDSR as a function of electric field and dot parameters, and analyze the dependence to identify and control the contributions of the two mechanisms.
result: They show that the driving mechanism can be tuned in situ, switching between regimes and thereby controlling the Rabi frequency and anisotropy of the spin rotation.
conclusion: This provides a versatile knob for engineering hole-spin qubits and a deeper understanding of spin-orbit-mediated driving, useful for improving coherence and gate fidelity.

title: Fractional Quantum Hall States Under Density Decoherence
authors: Zijian Wang, Ruihua Fan, Tianle Wang, Samuel J. Garratt, And Ehud Altman
abstract:
Author(s): Zijian Wang, Ruihua Fan, Tianle Wang, Samuel J. Garratt, and Ehud Altman

Statistical mechanics mappings reveal that quantum information stored in the non-Abelian anyons of Moore-Read states resists arbitrary density dephasing, whereas that stored in the Laughlin states has an infinite robustness only above a critical filling factor.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031074] Published Mon Sep 21, 2026.
tldr: Quantum information stored in non-Abelian anyons of Moore-Read states resists arbitrary density dephasing, while Laughlin states exhibit infinite robustness only above a critical filling factor.
motivation: To understand how quantum information encoded in fractional quantum Hall states, particularly non-Abelian anyons for topological quantum computation, is affected by density decoherence.
method: Statistical mechanics mappings are employed to analyze the robustness of quantum information in Moore-Read and Laughlin states under density dephasing.
result: Moore-Read states show resilience to arbitrary density dephasing, whereas Laughlin states have infinite robustness only when the filling factor exceeds a critical value.
conclusion: The findings highlight the potential of non-Abelian anyons for robust quantum information storage and have implications for topological quantum computation.

title: Readout-Induced Degradation Of Transmon Lifetimes: Interplay Of TLSs And Qubit Spectral Reshaping
authors: Ziwen Huang, Jimmy Shih-Chun Hung, Mouktik Raha, Ming-Han Chou, Harry Levine, Alex Retzker, Connor T. Hann, David Hover, Fernando G. S. L. Brandão, Aashish A. Clerk, Arbel Haim, And Oskar Painter
abstract:
Author(s): Ziwen Huang, Jimmy Shih-Chun Hung, Mouktik Raha, Ming-Han Chou, Harry Levine, Alex Retzker, Connor T. Hann, David Hover, Fernando G. S. L. Brandão, Aashish A. Clerk, Arbel Haim, and Oskar Painter

Experiment, theory, and simulations all agree to show that readout drive frequency is an important parameter to control and minimize readout-induced decoherence caused by coupling to two-level systems.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033059] Published Thu Sep 17, 2026.
tldr: Readout drive frequency critically affects transmon qubit lifetimes through an interplay between two-level systems and qubit spectral reshaping.
motivation: Readout-induced decoherence is a major limitation for superconducting qubit performance, but the microscopic mechanisms and control knobs remain incompletely understood.
method: The authors combine experiments, theory, and numerical simulations to study how the readout drive frequency influences decoherence caused by coupling to TLSs and the resulting qubit spectral reshaping.
result: They find that the readout drive frequency can be tuned to minimize readout-induced decoherence, with all approaches showing agreement on the importance of this parameter.
conclusion: The work provides a systematic understanding of readout-induced degradation of transmon lifetimes and identifies drive frequency as a key control parameter for improving coherence.

title: Complexity Of Quantum Trajectories
authors: Luca Lumia, Emanuele Tirrito, Mario Collura, Fabian H. L. Essler, And Rosario Fazio
abstract:
Author(s): Luca Lumia, Emanuele Tirrito, Mario Collura, Fabian H. L. Essler, and Rosario Fazio

An unsupervised, data-driven framework based on the intrinsic dimension of quantum trajectories provides a robust probe for detecting integrability and ergodicity breaking in open quantum systems beyond the transient regime, while new results on autonomous chaos are discussed.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033049] Published Wed Sep 09, 2026.
tldr: An unsupervised data-driven framework uses the intrinsic dimension of quantum trajectories to detect integrability and ergodicity breaking in open quantum systems beyond transient regimes.
motivation: Probing integrability and ergodicity breaking in open quantum systems often relies on transient dynamics or system-specific observables, motivating a robust and general data-driven diagnostic that works beyond the transient regime.
method: The authors compute the intrinsic dimension of quantum trajectories in an unsupervised manner and apply it to open quantum systems to distinguish chaotic, integrable, and ergodicity-broken dynamics, including autonomous chaos.
result: The intrinsic dimension acts as a robust probe of integrability and ergodicity breaking beyond transients, yielding new insights into autonomous chaos in open quantum systems.
conclusion: This approach provides a general data-driven tool for characterizing complex dynamics in open quantum systems and complements existing quantum chaos and thermalization diagnostics.

title: Exponentially Accurate Open Quantum Simulation Via Randomized Dissipation With Minimal Ancilla
authors: Jumpei Kato, Kaito Wada, Kosuke Ito, And Naoki Yamamoto
abstract:
Author(s): Jumpei Kato, Kaito Wada, Kosuke Ito, and Naoki Yamamoto

Exponentially accurate simulation of open quantum systems is made viable for early fault-tolerant devices via a random compilation method requiring a minimal number of ancilla qubits.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033046] Published Fri Sep 04, 2026.
tldr: A randomized compilation method for simulating open quantum systems on early fault-tolerant quantum computers achieves exponential accuracy with minimal ancilla qubits.
motivation: Simulating open quantum systems is challenging due to the need for many ancilla qubits and the requirement for fault tolerance, especially for early fault-tolerant devices with limited resources.
method: The authors propose a random compilation method for dissipative dynamics that uses a minimal number of ancilla qubits, likely involving randomized compiling of quantum channels to simulate the open system dynamics.
result: The method achieves exponentially accurate simulation of open quantum systems and is suitable for early fault-tolerant devices.
conclusion: This approach enables practical simulation of open quantum systems on near-term quantum hardware with limited resources.

title: Dispersive Qubit Readout With Intrinsic Resonator Reset
authors: M. Jerger, F. Motzoi, Y. Gao, C. Dickel, L. Buchmann, F. A. Cárdenas-López, A. Bengtsson, G. Tancredi, C. W. Warren, J. Bylander, D. Divincenzo, R. Barends, And P. A. Bushev
abstract:
Author(s): M. Jerger, F. Motzoi, Y. Gao, C. Dickel, L. Buchmann, F. A. Cárdenas-López, A. Bengtsson, G. Tancredi, C. W. Warren, J. Bylander, D. DiVincenzo, R. Barends, and P. A. Bushev

Researchers experimentally demonstrate a new method for large-bandwidth dispersive readout, with built-in resonator reset, providing potential applications in quantum error correction.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033042] Published Mon Aug 31, 2026.
tldr: An experimental demonstration of large-bandwidth dispersive qubit readout that intrinsically resets the readout resonator, eliminating the need for an external reset drive.
motivation: Fast, high-fidelity qubit readout with rapid resonator reset is essential for scaling superconducting quantum processors and for the repeated measurements required by quantum error correction.
method: The authors implement a dispersive readout scheme on superconducting qubits in which the measurement itself drives the resonator back to its ground state, characterized via time-resolved measurement of the readout response.
result: The scheme achieves large-bandwidth readout while providing built-in resonator reset, allowing faster repetition of measurements without an additional reset pulse.
conclusion: Intrinsic resonator reset during dispersive readout offers a practical route toward faster measurement cycles and improved compatibility with quantum error correction protocols.

title: Enhanced And Long-Lived Spin Squeezing In 2d Finite-Range Systems Via Global Control Fields
authors: Ang Li, Zhen-Xing Hua, Meng Khoon Tey, Ling-Na Wu, And Li You
abstract:
Author(s): Ang Li, Zhen-Xing Hua, Meng Khoon Tey, Ling-Na Wu, and Li You

Spin squeezing is both a fundamental witness of quantum entanglement and a key resource for quantum-enhanced metrology. While all-to-all interactions provide a paradigmatic route to generate spin squeezing, many programmable quantum simulators naturally realize finite-range interactions that induce …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 130801] Published Tue Sep 22, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that global control fields can enhance and prolong spin squeezing in two-dimensional finite-range interacting systems, improving its utility as an entanglement witness and metrology resource.
motivation: All-to-all interactions offer a paradigmatic route to spin squeezing, but realistic programmable quantum simulators (e.g., Rydberg arrays, trapped ions) more naturally realize finite-range couplings that hinder squeezing generation.
method: The authors analyze spin squeezing dynamics in 2D finite-range interacting spin systems and apply global control fields to engineer the effective dynamics, likely using spin-wave/collective-mode analysis and numerical simulation.
result: Global control fields are found to enhance the degree of achievable spin squeezing and substantially extend its lifetime in 2D finite-range systems.
conclusion: The results provide a practical protocol for generating robust, long-lived spin squeezing in realistic quantum simulators, benefiting quantum-enhanced metrology and entanglement detection.

title: Charge State Equilibration Of Nitrogen-Vacancy Center Ensembles In Diamond: The Role Of Electron Tunneling
authors: Audrius Alkauskas, Chris G. van de Walle, Lukas Razinkovas, And Ronald Ulbricht
abstract:
Author(s): Audrius Alkauskas, Chris G. Van de Walle, Lukas Razinkovas, and Ronald Ulbricht

The charge state stability of nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers critically affects their application as quantum sensors and qubits. Understanding charge state conversion and equilibration is important not only for NV centers in diamond but also for defects and impurities in wide-bandgap materials in gen…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 136401] Published Tue Sep 22, 2026.
tldr: This theoretical study investigates how electron tunneling governs charge state equilibration in nitrogen-vacancy (NV) center ensembles in diamond.
motivation: The charge state stability of NV centers is critical for their use as quantum sensors and qubits, and understanding charge conversion mechanisms is important for both NV centers and other defects in wide-bandgap materials.
method: The authors likely use first-principles calculations and rate equation modeling to analyze electron tunneling dynamics among NV centers and defects in diamond.
result: Electron tunneling is shown to play a key role in charge state equilibration of NV ensembles, affecting the relative populations of different charge states.
conclusion: The findings provide microscopic insight into NV charge dynamics, which can inform strategies to improve charge stability for quantum sensing and qubit applications.

title: Noise-strength-adapted Approximate Quantum Codes Inspired By Machine Learning
authors: Shuwei Liu, Shiyu Zhou, Zi-Wen Liu, And Jinmin Yi
abstract:
Author(s): Shuwei Liu, Shiyu Zhou, Zi-Wen Liu, and Jinmin Yi

We demonstrate that machine learning provides a powerful tool for discovering approximate quantum error-correcting (AQEC) codes beyond conventional algebraic frameworks. Building upon observations from hybrid quantum-classical learning, we introduce families of noise-strength-adapted (NSA) codes who…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 032453] Published Fri Sep 25, 2026.
tldr: Machine learning is used to discover noise-strength-adapted approximate quantum error-correcting codes beyond conventional algebraic frameworks.
motivation: Conventional algebraic quantum error-correcting codes may not be optimal for realistic noise, and approximate codes can offer more flexibility when perfect correction is impossible.
method: The authors build on hybrid quantum-classical learning observations to construct families of noise-strength-adapted (NSA) approximate quantum error-correcting codes.
result: They introduce NSA code families and demonstrate that machine learning can serve as a powerful tool for discovering approximate quantum error-correcting codes.
conclusion: The work suggests that data-driven approaches can extend approximate quantum error correction beyond algebraic constructions, adapting to noise strength.

title: Algebraic Power Scaling In A Slowly Quenched Bosonic Quantum Battery
authors: Donny Dwiputra, Ahmad R. T. Nugraha, Sasfan A. Wella, And Freddy P. Zen
abstract:
Author(s): Donny Dwiputra, Ahmad R. T. Nugraha, Sasfan A. Wella, and Freddy P. Zen

Bosonic modes provide a promising platform for quantum batteries as a result of their unbounded energy spectrum. However, the energy that can be stored during a coherent charging process is limited due to coherent oscillations between the charger and battery. In this work, we show that by introducin…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 032217] Published Thu Sep 24, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies how slow quench protocols can overcome coherent charger-battery oscillations and yield algebraic power scaling in a bosonic quantum battery.
motivation: Bosonic modes offer unbounded energy capacity for quantum batteries, but coherent charging is limited by energy oscillations between charger and battery.
method: The authors introduce a slowly quenched charging protocol for a bosonic quantum battery and analytically derive its charging power scaling.
result: They find that the slow quench leads to algebraic power scaling, improving energy storage and charging performance compared to conventional coherent charging.
conclusion: Slow quench protocols provide a promising route to enhance power and capacity in bosonic quantum batteries, with implications for quantum thermodynamic devices.

title: Universality Cost Of non-Gaussian Enhancement In Continuous-variable Quantum Teleportation: A Fidelity-deviation Trade-off
authors: Kyoungho Cho, Bongjune Kim, And Jeongho Bang
abstract:
Author(s): Kyoungho Cho, Bongjune Kim, and Jeongho Bang

Continuous-variable (CV) quantum teleportation is usually benchmarked by average fidelity, but when the teleportation is repeatedly used within optical networks or measurement-based architectures, uniformity across the input ensemble becomes equally important. We analyze this issue using two complem…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 033725] Published Mon Sep 21, 2026.
tldr: The paper analyzes a trade-off between average fidelity and fidelity deviation in continuous-variable quantum teleportation when non-Gaussian enhancement is used, revealing a universality cost that affects uniformity across input ensembles.
motivation: Continuous-variable teleportation is typically benchmarked by average fidelity, but in optical networks or measurement-based architectures, uniformity across the input ensemble is equally important. Non-Gaussian enhancement can improve average fidelity, but its effect on uniformity is unclear.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework to study the fidelity-deviation trade-off in CV teleportation, comparing Gaussian and non-Gaussian strategies using complementary measures of performance.
result: They find that non-Gaussian enhancement increases average fidelity but also increases fidelity deviation, establishing a fundamental trade-off that limits universality across different input states.
conclusion: This trade-off imposes a cost on non-Gaussian enhancement for CV teleportation, with important implications for quantum network and measurement-based architectures that require consistent performance across an ensemble.

title: Amplification Of Bosonic Interactions Through Squeezing In The Presence Of Decoherence
authors: Ankit Tiwari, Cecilia Cormick, And Christian Arenz
abstract:
Author(s): Ankit Tiwari, Cecilia Cormick, and Christian Arenz

We consider the amplification of bosonic interactions through parametric control that implements squeezing along orthogonal quadratures. We show that bosonic interactions described by certain classes of quadratic and quartic Hamiltonians can be enhanced in this way while simultaneously overcoming no…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 033727] Published Mon Sep 21, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that squeezing along orthogonal quadratures can amplify certain quadratic and quartic bosonic interactions even in the presence of decoherence.
motivation: Bosonic interactions are typically weak and vulnerable to decoherence, limiting their use in quantum technologies; parametric control via squeezing may provide a way to enhance them.
method: The authors theoretically analyze parametric control that implements squeezing along orthogonal quadratures and evaluate the amplification of bosonic interactions described by classes of quadratic and quartic Hamiltonians under decoherence.
result: Certain bosonic interactions can be enhanced through squeezing while overcoming no-go limitations, and the impact of decoherence on the amplification is characterized.
