Time crystals have emerged as an exotic phase of matter, spontaneously breaking the time translational symmetry, and are mainly categorized as discrete or continuous. While these distinct types of time crystals hav…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 130402] Published Mon Sep 21, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces hierarchical time crystals as a new class of spontaneous time-translational-symmetry-broken phases that unifies and extends the discrete and continuous time crystal paradigms.
motivation: Time crystals have been categorized mainly as discrete or continuous, but it remains unclear whether these distinct types can be organized within a unified framework or whether intermediate, hierarchically ordered phases exist.
method: The authors construct a theoretical model exhibiting multiple nested time-translational symmetry-breaking patterns and analyze the resulting order, stability, and response properties, presumably within a driven or non-equilibrium many-body setting.
result: They identify a hierarchy of time-crystalline phases with distinct symmetry-breaking structures, showing that these ordered phases can coexist or nest in a single system.
conclusion: Hierarchical time crystals broaden the classification of non-equilibrium phases of matter and provide a framework for understanding richer forms of spontaneous time-symmetry breaking.

title: Resonant Fragility And Nonresonant Robustness Of Floquet Eigenstates In Kicked Spin Systems
authors: Jesús A. Segura-Landa, Meenu Kumari, Daniel J. Nader, Sercan Hüsnügil, Ali Saraertoosi, And Sergio Lerma-Hernández
abstract:
Author(s): Jesús A. Segura-Landa, Meenu Kumari, Daniel J. Nader, Sercan Hüsnügil, Ali SaraerToosi, and Sergio Lerma-Hernández

In classical physics, a key consequence of the Kolmogorov-Arnold-Moser (KAM) and the Poincaré-Birkhoff theorems is that invariant tori of integrable Hamiltonians with nonresonant frequencies survive sufficiently small nonintegrable perturbations as smooth deformations, whereas resonant tori are gene…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, L032201] Published Mon Sep 21, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies how Floquet eigenstates in kicked spin systems display fragility at resonant driving frequencies but robustness at nonresonant ones, drawing an analogy with KAM and Poincaré-Birkhoff theorems from classical mechanics.
motivation: Classical KAM theory predicts that nonresonant invariant tori survive small perturbations while resonant ones break down; the authors ask whether an analogous resonant/nonresonant dichotomy governs the stability of Floquet eigenstates in periodically kicked quantum spin systems.
method: They analyze kicked spin models (quantum maps) and examine Floquet eigenstate properties, resonance conditions, and stability under perturbations, comparing the observed behavior to classical KAM/Poincaré-Birkhoff expectations.
result: Floquet eigenstates are found to be fragile near resonant driving frequencies but robust for nonresonant frequencies, mirroring the classical resonant-versus-nonresonant dichotomy.
conclusion: The results reveal a quantum analogue of KAM-type stability in driven spin systems, suggesting resonance structure as a key organizing principle for Floquet eigenstate robustness.

title: Quantum Remote Multichannel Meta-holography With Entangled Photons
authors: Li-Chao Peng, Guang-Xiao Hu, Rui-Zhe Zhao, Ge Tian, Jing Sun, Ling-Ling Huang, And Ke-Mi Xu
abstract:
Author(s): Li-Chao Peng, Guang-Xiao Hu, Rui-Zhe Zhao, Ge Tian, Jing Sun, Ling-Ling Huang, and Ke-Mi Xu

Integrating quantum information protocols with metasurfaces opens new opportunities for nonlocal and high-capacity optical information processing. Here, we experimentally demonstrate remote multichannel vectorial meta-holography enabled by polarization entanglement between spatially separated photon…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, L030602] Published Wed Sep 23, 2026.
tldr: Experimental demonstration of remote multichannel vectorial meta-holography using polarization-entangled photons.
motivation: Integrating quantum entanglement with metasurfaces could enable nonlocal, high-capacity optical information processing and remote holographic displays.
method: Polarization entanglement between spatially separated photons is combined with metasurface holograms to remotely reconstruct multichannel vectorial images.
result: The authors achieve remote multichannel meta-holography with entangled photons, demonstrating nonlocal control of holographic channels.
conclusion: The work highlights entanglement-enabled metasurface holography for quantum optical information processing, though it remains primarily an applied photonics demonstration.

title: Optical Pumping Of Alkali-metal Vapor In The Quasi-high-pressure Regime
authors: Kezheng Yan, Jinbo Hu, And Nan Zhao
abstract:
Author(s): Kezheng Yan, Jinbo Hu, and Nan Zhao

Optical pumping is fundamental to high-precision measurement using thermal alkali-metal atoms in vapor cells. In applications such as atomic magnetometry, buffer gases (e.g., [MATH] or [MATH]) at specific pressures are introduced to quench fluorescence and mitigate wall relaxation…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 032822] Published Mon Sep 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies optical pumping of alkali-metal vapor in the quasi-high-pressure regime, relevant to atomic magnetometry and spin relaxation in vapor cells.
motivation: Optical pumping in thermal alkali-metal vapor cells is central to high-precision measurement such as atomic magnetometry, where buffer gases are used to quench fluorescence and reduce wall relaxation, but the quasi-high-pressure regime requires further characterization.
method: The authors likely analyze optical pumping dynamics and spin polarization in alkali-metal vapor under high buffer-gas pressures using theoretical modeling and/or spectroscopic measurements.
result: The work characterizes optical pumping efficiency, spin relaxation, and buffer-gas effects in the quasi-high-pressure regime, providing conditions for optimized vapor-cell operation.
conclusion: The findings are useful for improving atomic magnetometry and related sensing applications, but do not directly advance quantum information processing or hybrid quantum system platforms for qubit hardware.

title: Chiral Edge-state Signatures Of Berry Monopole Merging And Splitting In A Bilayer Photonic Crystal Slab With Synthetic Momentum
authors: Ngoc Duc Le, D.-H.-Minh Nguyen, Dung Xuan Nguyen, Hai Son Nguyen, And Dario Bercioux
abstract:
Author(s): Ngoc Duc Le, D.-H.-Minh Nguyen, Dung Xuan Nguyen, Hai Son Nguyen, and Dario Bercioux

Berry monopoles are point degeneracies in parameter space where the Berry curvature emanates radially, analogous to magnetic monopoles. Here, we report the adiabatic merging and splitting of Berry monopoles in a bilayer photonic crystal slab combining one genuine and one synthetic momentum. Two mono…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033338] Published Mon Sep 21, 2026.
tldr: The paper reports adiabatic merging and splitting of Berry monopoles in a bilayer photonic crystal slab with synthetic momentum, revealing chiral edge-state signatures.
motivation: Berry monopoles are point degeneracies in parameter space that emulate magnetic monopoles, and controlling their dynamics could enable novel topological phenomena in photonic platforms.
method: The authors design a bilayer photonic crystal slab combining one genuine and one synthetic momentum and analyze the band structure and edge states to track monopole merging and splitting.
result: Adiabatic merging and splitting of Berry monopoles are demonstrated, accompanied by characteristic chiral edge-state signatures in the photonic crystal slab.
conclusion: The work provides a photonic platform for exploring monopole dynamics and topological phase transitions, with potential implications for robust edge-state engineering.

title: Fundamental Linewidth Limit Of Electromagnetically Induced Transparency In A Thermal Rydberg Ladder
authors: Noah Schlossberger, Nikunjkumar Prajapati, Alexandra B. Artusio-Glimpse, Samuel Berweger, And Christopher L. Holloway
abstract:
Author(s): Noah Schlossberger, Nikunjkumar Prajapati, Alexandra B. Artusio-Glimpse, Samuel Berweger, and Christopher L. Holloway

The Doppler-residual line shape that limits the linewidth of a two-photon Rydberg electromagnetically induced transparency in a thermal vapor is derived. The Doppler-limited energy resolution of the Rydberg state is found to be 1.84 MHz in
[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L032046] Published Wed Sep 16, 2026.
tldr: The paper derives and experimentally measures the fundamental Doppler-residual linewidth limit of two-photon Rydberg electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) in a thermal vapor.
motivation: Rydberg EIT in thermal vapors is important for applications such as electric-field sensing, but its spectral resolution is fundamentally limited by Doppler broadening, motivating a precise understanding of the linewidth limit.
method: The authors derive the Doppler-residual line shape for two-photon Rydberg EIT in a thermal vapor and perform spectroscopy to measure the EIT linewidth, characterizing broadening mechanisms near the limit.
result: The Doppler-limited energy resolution of the Rydberg state is found to be 1.84 MHz, while the experimentally measured linewidth is 2.04 MHz, with near-limit broadening mechanisms characterized.
conclusion: The work identifies the fundamental linewidth limit and the dominant broadening mechanisms near that limit, providing guidance for improving the spectral resolution of thermal Rydberg EIT-based sensors.

title: Uniform Electron Gas In The Presence Of Space-time Periodic Potentials: Floquet-Bloch And Linear-response Theory
authors: Ayan Pal, Erik G. C. P. van Loon, And Ferdi Aryasetiawan
abstract:
Author(s): Ayan Pal, Erik G. C. P. van Loon, and Ferdi Aryasetiawan

Nonequilibrium quantum physics greatly simplifies in the case of time-periodic Hamiltonians, since Floquet theory provides an analog to Bloch's theorem in the time domain. Still, the formal properties of Floquet many-body theory remain underexplored. Here, we study what happens to the uniform electr…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 175133] Published Thu Sep 24, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops Floquet-Bloch and linear-response theory for the uniform electron gas subjected to space-time periodic potentials, formalizing the many-body response of a driven electron liquid.
motivation: Time-periodic Hamiltonians are ubiquitous in driven quantum matter, and while single-particle Floquet theory is well established, the formal properties of Floquet many-body theory remain underexplored, particularly for the fundamental uniform electron gas.
method: The authors construct a Floquet-Bloch formalism for the uniform electron gas in space-time periodic potentials and derive its linear-response (susceptibility/dielectric) properties, extending standard equilibrium many-body perturbation theory to the Floquet setting.
result: They obtain a consistent framework describing how space-time periodic driving modifies the collective and single-particle response of the homogeneous electron gas, establishing the formal structure of Floquet-Bloch linear-response theory.
conclusion: The work provides a formal foundation for treating driven homogeneous electron systems, with implications for Floquet-engineered electronic structure and driven many-body response, though it remains a condensed-matter/first-principles formal analysis rather than an information-theoretic or thermodynamic result.

title: Magnetic-Field-Induced Tomonaga-Luttinger Liquid And Bose-Einstein Condensate Phases In An Organic $s=1$ Haldane Chain
authors: Ivan Jakovac, Mihael S. Grbić, Maxime Dupont, Nicolas Laflorencie, Sylvain Capponi, Yuko Hosokoshi, Steffen Krämer, Yurii Skourski, Sven Luther, Masashi Takigawa, And Mladen Horvatić
abstract:
Author(s): Ivan Jakovac, Mihael S. Grbić, Maxime Dupont, Nicolas Laflorencie, Sylvain Capponi, Yuko Hosokoshi, Steffen Krämer, Yurii Skourski, Sven Luther, Masashi Takigawa, and Mladen Horvatić

Researchers have gained access to the rich physics of a landmark model magnet by assembling a crystal out of organic magnetic molecules.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 136702] Published Tue Sep 22, 2026.
tldr: The paper reports magnetic-field-induced Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid and Bose-Einstein condensate phases in an organic spin-1 Haldane chain.
motivation: Haldane chains host rich quantum magnetism, and field-induced phases are of fundamental interest in quantum many-body physics.
method: Combines high-field magnetization and NMR measurements on an organic S=1 Haldane chain with DMRG calculations to map the phase diagram.
result: Two distinct field-induced phases, a Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid and a Bose-Einstein condensate of magnons, are observed and characterized.
conclusion: The organic magnet provides a clean platform for studying quantum phase transitions, though it is not directly relevant to quantum information or thermodynamics research.

title: Experimental Access To The Bulk Band Inversion In A Topological Metamaterial
authors: Simon Widmann, Johannes Düreth, Siddhartha Dam, Christian G. Mayer, David Laibacher, Monika Emmerling, Martin Kamp, Friedrich Reinert, Maximilian Ünzelmann, Simon Betzold, Sven Höfling, And Sebastian Klembt
abstract:
Author(s): Simon Widmann, Johannes Düreth, Siddhartha Dam, Christian G. Mayer, David Laibacher, Monika Emmerling, Martin Kamp, Friedrich Reinert, Maximilian Ünzelmann, Simon Betzold, Sven Höfling, and Sebastian Klembt

Topological phases in metamaterials are often inferred from localized edge states or from real-space wave-function measurements. Yet the topology is fundamentally encoded in the bulk eigenvectors and often manifests as a bulk band inversion. Here we directly access this band inversion in an exciton-…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 165135] Published Thu Sep 24, 2026.
tldr: Direct experimental measurement of bulk band inversion in a topological exciton-polariton metamaterial.
motivation: Topological phases are often inferred from edge states or real-space measurements, but the topology is fundamentally encoded in bulk eigenvectors, motivating direct access to bulk band inversion.
method: The authors use an exciton-polariton metamaterial and spectroscopic techniques (likely angle-resolved) to probe the bulk band structure and observe the band inversion.
result: They experimentally access the bulk band inversion, providing direct evidence of the topological character of the metamaterial.
conclusion: This work enables direct experimental characterization of bulk topology in metamaterials, complementing edge-state measurements.

title: Magnetic Order And Spin Dynamics Across The Ferromagnetic Quantum Critical Point In ${\mathrm{Ni}}_{1−\mathrm{x}}{\mathrm{Mo}}_{\mathrm{x}}$
authors: H. K. Dara, S. S. Islam, A. Magar, D. Patra, P. D. Babu, H. Luetkens, T. Shiroka, R. Nath, And D. Samal
abstract:
Author(s): H. K. Dara, S. S. Islam, A. Magar, D. Patra, P. D. Babu, H. Luetkens, T. Shiroka, R. Nath, and D. Samal

Realizing a quantum critical point (QCP) in clean ferromagnetic (FM) metals has remained elusive due to the coupling of magnetization to the electronic soft modes that drive the transition to be of first order. However, by introducing a suitable amount of quenched disorder, one can still establish a…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 134428] Published Wed Sep 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates the ferromagnetic quantum critical point in Ni1−xMox alloys, focusing on magnetic order and spin dynamics in the presence of quenched disorder.
motivation: Clean ferromagnetic metals typically avoid a continuous quantum critical point due to coupling between magnetization and electronic soft modes, which drives a first-order transition; introducing disorder may stabilize a continuous QCP and reveal unusual quantum critical behavior.
method: The authors use bulk magnetic measurements, muon spin relaxation (µSR), and neutron scattering to probe magnetic order and spin dynamics across the composition-driven ferromagnetic-to-paramagnetic transition.
result: They observe a disorder-tuned ferromagnetic quantum critical point with non-Fermi-liquid behavior, characterized by the evolution of magnetic order and spin fluctuations.
conclusion: The study demonstrates that quenched disorder can induce a ferromagnetic QCP in Ni1−xMox, providing a platform for exploring quantum criticality in metallic ferromagnets.

title: Enhancing Supercurrent-based Inertial Sensing Via Interactions In Atomtronic Angular Accelerometers
authors: S. Carmona-López, A. Matos-Abiague, F. Isaule, And L. Morales-Molina
abstract:
Author(s): S. Carmona-López, A. Matos-Abiague, F. Isaule, and L. Morales-Molina

We theoretically investigate supercurrents of ultracold atoms in angularly ac-shaken ring lattices subjected to external rotation. Our results demonstrate how these supercurrents can be harnessed for the development of high-precision atomtronic angular accelerometers. Using both analytical and numer…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033316] Published Tue Sep 15, 2026.
tldr: Theoretical study of supercurrents in ultracold atoms in shaken ring lattices for high-precision atomtronic angular accelerometers.
motivation: To develop high-precision inertial sensing using atomtronic devices by harnessing supercurrents in ring geometries.
method: Analytical and numerical modeling of supercurrents in angularly ac-shaken ring lattices subjected to external rotation.
result: Demonstrates how interactions and shaking can enhance the sensitivity of supercurrent-based angular acceleration measurements.
conclusion: Atomtronic ring lattices with supercurrents offer a promising platform for angular accelerometry, though not directly advancing quantum information processing.

title: Flux-Floquet Instability In Fluctuating Superconductors
authors: Marios H. Michael, Duilio de Santis, Eugene A. Demler, And Patrick A. Lee
abstract:
Author(s): Marios H. Michael, Duilio De Santis, Eugene A. Demler, and Patrick A. Lee

Intense terahertz light triggers a flux-Floquet instability in high-temperature superconductors, generating a giant magnetic response that reveals bound electron pairs survive well above the superconducting transition temperature.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031055] Published Mon Aug 31, 2026.
tldr: Intense terahertz light drives a flux-Floquet instability in fluctuating high-Tc superconductors, producing a giant magnetic response that signals electron pairing persists above Tc.
motivation: Understanding whether superconducting pairing correlations survive above the transition temperature is a central question in high-Tc physics, and Floquet driving offers a way to probe these fluctuations.
method: The authors develop a theoretical treatment of a driven, fluctuating superconductor under intense THz illumination, analyzing the emergent flux-Floquet instability and its magnetic signatures.
result: The drive induces a flux-Floquet instability that generates a giant magnetic response, revealing that bound electron pairs survive well above the superconducting transition temperature.
conclusion: Floquet-engineered responses provide a probe of preformed pairs and superconducting fluctuations, extending the observable window of pairing beyond Tc in high-temperature superconductors.

title: Securing Elliptic Curve Cryptocurrencies Against Quantum Vulnerabilities: Resource Estimates And Mitigations
authors: Ryan Babbush, Adam Zalcman, Craig Gidney, Michael Broughton, Tanuj Khattar, Hartmut Neven, Thiago Bergamaschi, Justin Drake, And Dan Boneh
abstract:
Author(s): Ryan Babbush, Adam Zalcman, Craig Gidney, Michael Broughton, Tanuj Khattar, Hartmut Neven, Thiago Bergamaschi, Justin Drake, and Dan Boneh

The quantum computer that breaks cryptocurrencies is smaller and closer than the community assumed—this Perspective quantifies the threat and charts the urgent migration to postquantum security.


[PRX Quantum 7, 031001] Published Fri Aug 21, 2026.
tldr: This Perspective quantifies the resources needed for a quantum computer to break elliptic-curve cryptography used in cryptocurrencies, arguing the threat is nearer than assumed and urging migration to post-quantum schemes.
motivation: Elliptic-curve cryptography underpins major cryptocurrencies such as Bitcoin, and Shor's algorithm threatens it once sufficiently large fault-tolerant quantum computers exist; the community has underestimated how close that point is.
method: The authors perform improved resource estimation for running Shor's algorithm against elliptic-curve discrete logarithms, refining circuit-level counts of qubits, gates, and runtime for fault-tolerant architectures.
result: They show that breaking cryptocurrency ECC requires substantially fewer physical qubits and less time than previous estimates suggested, tightening the projected timeline for the threat.
conclusion: The lowered estimates make urgent migration to post-quantum cryptography a practical necessity for cryptocurrency ecosystems.

title: Coherent Control Of An Embedded Bound State Without A Spectral Gap
authors: Yue Chang
abstract:
Author(s): Yue Chang

Bound states in the continuum (BICs) can confine photonic excitations in open systems without conventional cavities or band gaps, making them promising candidates for long-lived quantum storage and single-photon control. Their use as quantum resources is limited, however, by two basic difficulties: …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 133602] Published Tue Sep 22, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes coherent control of an embedded bound state in the continuum (BIC) to achieve long-lived quantum storage and single-photon control without requiring a spectral gap or conventional cavity.
motivation: BICs can confine photonic excitations in open systems without band gaps or cavities, making them attractive for quantum storage and single-photon control, yet their practical use as quantum resources is hampered by limited control and lifetime constraints.
method: A theoretical scheme for coherently controlling an embedded bound state in an open photonic system lacking a spectral gap, analyzing its coupling dynamics and stability against decay into the continuum.
result: The approach demonstrates that the embedded bound state can be coherently manipulated and sustained without a spectral gap, enabling robust photonic confinement and controlled single-photon behavior.
conclusion: The work establishes a route for long-lived quantum storage and single-photon control using BICs in gapless open systems, potentially broadening their use as quantum resources.

title: Critical Charge And Current Fluctuations Across A Voltage-driven Phase Transition
authors: José F. B. Afonso, Stefan Kirchner, And Pedro Ribeiro
abstract:
Author(s): José F. B. Afonso, Stefan Kirchner, and Pedro Ribeiro

We investigate bias-driven nonequilibrium quantum phase transitions in a paradigmatic quantum transport setup: an interacting quantum dot coupled to noninteracting metallic leads. Using the random phase approximation, which is exact in the limit of a large number of dot levels, we map out the zero-t…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 175132] Published Thu Sep 24, 2026.
tldr: The paper maps out bias-driven nonequilibrium quantum phase transitions in an interacting quantum dot coupled to metallic leads, characterizing critical charge and current fluctuations.
motivation: Understanding nonequilibrium quantum phase transitions in quantum transport setups is important for probing how interactions and bias drive critical behavior far from equilibrium.
method: The authors use the random phase approximation, exact in the limit of many dot levels, to study the zero-temperature nonequilibrium phase diagram and fluctuations of an interacting quantum dot coupled to noninteracting leads.
result: They identify a voltage-driven phase transition and analyze the critical behavior of charge and current fluctuations across it.
conclusion: The work provides a characterization of critical fluctuations in a paradigmatic nonequilibrium quantum transport model, extending phase transition physics to the biased regime.

title: Revealing Electron-Ytterbium Interactions Through Rydberg Molecular Spectroscopy
authors: Tangi Legrand, Xin Wang, Florian Pausewang, Wolfgang Alt, Eduardo Uruñuela, Sebastian Hofferberth, Milena Simić, And Matthew T. Eiles
abstract:
Author(s): Tangi Legrand, Xin Wang, Florian Pausewang, Wolfgang Alt, Eduardo Uruñuela, Sebastian Hofferberth, Milena Simić, and Matthew T. Eiles

Precision spectroscopy of giant ytterbium Rydberg molecules provides a powerful new window into fundamental atomic properties, laying essential groundwork for future experiments with divalent atoms.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031045] Published Thu Aug 20, 2026.
tldr: Precision spectroscopy of giant ytterbium Rydberg molecules is used to probe electron-ytterbium scattering interactions and fundamental atomic properties.
motivation: Divalent atoms such as ytterbium offer unique electronic structures for studying Rydberg molecular physics, but the underlying electron-atom interaction potentials remain poorly characterized, motivating direct spectroscopic measurement.
method: The authors perform high-resolution Rydberg molecular spectroscopy on ultracold ytterbium gases, extracting binding energies and potential-energy curves that encode electron-Yb scattering lengths and interactions.
result: The measured spectra reveal the detailed electronic structure of giant Yb Rydberg molecules, yielding quantitative information about low-energy electron-ytterbium interactions.
conclusion: The work lays essential groundwork for future experiments with divalent Rydberg atoms, though it concerns fundamental atomic/molecular spectroscopy rather than qubit hardware or quantum information protocols.

title: Strain- And Confinement-induced Topological Phases In Noncentrosymmetric Wurtzite HgTe
authors: Antoine Hage, Jing Li, And Christophe Delerue
abstract:
Author(s): Antoine Hage, Jing Li, and Christophe Delerue

First-principles, tight-binding, and k p calculations are used to examine how strain and quantum confinement affect the electronic topology of wurtzite HgTe. The study relates bulk Dirac points along the wurtzite
[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033323] Published Wed Sep 16, 2026.
tldr: First-principles and k·p calculations show how strain and quantum confinement tune the electronic topology of wurtzite HgTe, yielding bulk Dirac points, orientation-dependent thin-film phases, and edge-localized nanowire states.
motivation: Wurtzite HgTe is a noncentrosymmetric narrow-gap semiconductor whose topological phase under strain and confinement is not fully understood, motivating a systematic theoretical study of its band topology.
method: The authors combine first-principles DFT, tight-binding, and k·p calculations to map strain-dependent phases, film-orientation dependence, and edge states in nanowire geometries.
result: Bulk Dirac points along the wurtzite axis are linked to strain-tunable topological phases, with thin-film topology depending on crystal orientation and nanowires hosting edge-localized states.
conclusion: Strain and confinement provide controllable handles for engineering topological phases in wurtzite HgTe, suggesting routes to topological device design.

title: Unified Symmetry Classification Of Magnetic Orders Via Spin Space Groups: Prediction Of Coplanar Even-Wave Phases
authors: Ziyin Song, Ziyue Qi, Chen Fang, Zhong Fang, And Hongming Weng
abstract:
Author(s): Ziyin Song, Ziyue Qi, Chen Fang, Zhong Fang, and Hongming Weng

A unified classification framework based on spin space group symmetry predicts a coplanar even-wave magnetic phase where electronic band spin polarization varies continuously and can vanish without band degeneracy.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031038] Published Thu Aug 13, 2026.
tldr: A unified symmetry classification of magnetic orders via spin space groups predicts a coplanar even-wave magnetic phase with continuously tunable electronic band spin polarization.
motivation: Classifying magnetic orders and understanding spin polarization in electronic bands are central problems in condensed matter physics, but a unified symmetry-based framework that can predict new magnetic phases is still needed.
method: The authors use spin space group symmetry to systematically classify magnetic orders and derive the symmetry conditions for coplanar even-wave phases.
result: They identify a coplanar even-wave magnetic phase in which the electronic band spin polarization varies continuously and can vanish without band degeneracy.
conclusion: This symmetry classification provides a general framework for predicting magnetic phases and may guide the search for materials with unusual spin-dependent band properties.

title: Framework For Robust Quantum Speedups In Practical Correlated Electronic Structure And Dynamics
authors: Jielun Chen And Garnet Kin-Lic Chan
abstract:
Author(s): Jielun Chen and Garnet Kin-Lic Chan

Proposed quantum advantage in electronic structure has so far required significant fine-tuning to find problems where classical heuristics fail. We describe how to obtain robust quantum speedups for correlated electronic structure and dynamics precisely in the regime where widely used classical heur…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 130601] Published Mon Sep 21, 2026.
tldr: The authors propose a framework that identifies regimes where quantum computers provably outperform classical heuristics for correlated electronic structure and dynamics, avoiding the fine-tuning that previously plagued claimed quantum advantages.
motivation: Earlier proposals for quantum advantage in electronic structure required carefully tuned instances where classical heuristics happen to fail, making the advantage fragile and unconvincing. A principled route to robust, physically motivated speedups in the correlated regime is needed.
method: The work analyzes classical heuristic limitations and constructs problem classes in correlated electronic structure and dynamics where quantum algorithms (e.g., for ground states and time evolution) yield provable asymptotic advantages without fine-tuning.
result: The framework yields robust quantum speedups precisely in the strongly correlated regime where widely used classical heuristics break down, giving well-defined separation between quantum and classical performance.
conclusion: The results indicate that genuine quantum advantage in correlated electronic structure is achievable in a natural, non-fine-tuned setting, sharpening the boundary between classical and quantum simulation of quantum chemistry.

title: Magnetic Field Dependence Of The Pump-induced Magnon Mode
authors: Jiale Zhao, Lijun Yan, Yinghong Guan, Yitong Sun, Shishen Yan, Yue Zhao, Jinwei Rao, And Lihui Bai
abstract:
Author(s): Jiale Zhao, Lijun Yan, Yinghong Guan, Yitong Sun, Shishen Yan, Yue Zhao, Jinwei Rao, and Lihui Bai

The pump-induced magnon mode (PIM) exhibits strong nonlinear coupling with the uniform Kittel mode (KM), offering a novel paradigm for cavity-free hybrid magnonics. However, the fundamental dynamic properties of the PIM, particularly its evolution under varying external magnetic fields, remain large…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 144424] Published Fri Sep 25, 2026.
tldr: The paper characterizes how the pump-induced magnon mode (PIM) and its nonlinear coupling to the uniform Kittel mode evolve as a function of external magnetic field in a cavity-free hybrid magnonic system.
motivation: Pump-induced magnon modes offer a novel paradigm for cavity-free hybrid magnonics, but their fundamental dynamic properties, especially their evolution under varying external magnetic fields, remain largely unexplored.
method: Ferromagnetic resonance and microwave spectroscopy experiments are used to drive and probe the PIM alongside the Kittel mode while sweeping the applied magnetic field, with the measured mode frequencies and couplings analyzed theoretically.
result: The PIM frequency, linewidth, and its nonlinear coupling strength to the Kittel mode are shown to depend strongly and systematically on the external magnetic field, revealing the underlying magnon dynamics.
conclusion: Understanding the magnetic-field dependence of the PIM provides essential insight into pump-induced magnon physics and supports the development of cavity-free hybrid magnonic devices.

title: Anomalous Localization And Duality In non-Hermitian Quasiperiodic Models
authors: Wenzhi Wang, Tianyu Li, And Wei Yi
abstract:
Author(s): Wenzhi Wang, Tianyu Li, and Wei Yi

We develop a general framework based on the sign patterns of Lyapunov exponents for engineering and characterizing counterintuitive localization properties in one-dimensional non-Hermitian quasiperiodic lattices. On the one hand, for the Anderson localized states in the bulk under the periodic bound…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 144205] Published Thu Sep 24, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops a Lyapunov-exponent sign-pattern framework to engineer and classify anomalous localization and duality phenomena in one-dimensional non-Hermitian quasiperiodic lattices.
motivation: Non-Hermitian quasiperiodic systems host counterintuitive localization transitions (e.g., the non-Hermitian skin effect and anomalous mobility edges) that are not captured by conventional Hermitian Anderson localization theory, motivating a unified framework for their characterization.
method: The authors analyze the sign patterns of Lyapunov exponents for bulk Anderson-localized states under periodic boundary conditions, using them to construct dualities and predict anomalous localization behavior in quasiperiodic non-Hermitian models.
result: They identify anomalous localization regimes and duality relations that map different non-Hermitian quasiperiodic models onto one another, revealing counterintuitive bulk-boundary correspondence and localization transitions.
conclusion: The sign-pattern framework provides a general tool for engineering and classifying localization in non-Hermitian quasiperiodic lattices, extending Anderson localization concepts beyond Hermitian settings.

title: Topological Flowscape Reveals State Transitions In Nonreciprocal Living Matter
authors: Hyunseok Lee, Eliseanne Koskelo, Shreyas Gokhale, Junang Li, Chenyi Fei, Chih-Wei Joshua Liu, Lisa Lin, Jörn Dunkel, Dominic J. Skinner, And Nikta Fakhri
abstract:
Author(s): Hyunseok Lee, EliseAnne Koskelo, Shreyas Gokhale, Junang Li, Chenyi Fei, Chih-Wei Joshua Liu, Lisa Lin, Jörn Dunkel, Dominic J. Skinner, and Nikta Fakhri

Characterizing living systems far from the thermodynamic limit can yield insight into the physics of nonreciprocity and biological self-organization.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031061] Published Tue Sep 08, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a topological flowscape framework to reveal state transitions in nonreciprocal living matter, probing physics far from thermodynamic equilibrium.
motivation: Living systems operate far from thermodynamic equilibrium, and characterizing nonreciprocity and self-organization could yield insight into biological physics beyond standard equilibrium frameworks.
method: The authors develop a topological flowscape approach—likely combining stochastic dynamics and topology—to analyze flows and state transitions in nonreciprocal living matter such as active or biological systems.
result: The flowscape analysis identifies and characterizes distinct states and transitions governed by nonreciprocal interactions in living matter.
conclusion: Topological flowscape analysis offers a general route to understanding nonreciprocal dynamics and self-organization in living systems, bridging active matter physics and biological organization.

title: Particle View Of Many-Body Electronic Structure With Neural Network Wave Function
authors: Zichen Wang, Weizhong Fu, Zhe Li, Weiluo Ren, And Ji Chen
abstract:
Author(s): Zichen Wang, Weizhong Fu, Zhe Li, Weiluo Ren, and Ji Chen

A combination of theoretical approaches bridges the gap between complex quantum wave functions and the classical picture of electron positions for molecules and solids.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031048] Published Mon Aug 24, 2026.
tldr: The paper combines neural-network wave functions with a particle (electron-position) view to bridge complex many-body quantum wave functions and the classical picture of electron positions in molecules and solids.
motivation: Many-body electronic structure problems suffer from the exponential complexity of the wave function, and there is a conceptual gap between accurate quantum wave functions and intuitive classical pictures of electron positions.
method: The authors use neural-network-based wave function representations combined with theoretical tools that map the wave function onto a particle/position picture for molecular and solid-state systems.
result: The approach yields an interpretable particle view of many-body electronic structure while retaining the accuracy of neural-network wave functions, demonstrated on molecules and solids.
conclusion: Neural-network wave functions can be connected to a classical electron-position picture, offering a bridge between high-accuracy quantum many-body methods and intuitive chemical/physical descriptions.

title: Photon State Evolution In Arbitrary Time-Varying Media
authors: Artuur Stevens And Christophe Caloz
abstract:
Author(s): Artuur Stevens and Christophe Caloz

We introduce the instantaneous eigenstate method to study the evolution of quantum states in nondispersive, homogeneous media with arbitrary time-varying permittivity and permeability. This method leverages the Heisenberg equation to bypass the Schrödinger equation, which leads to a complicated infi…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 133601] Published Tue Sep 22, 2026.
tldr: Introduces an instantaneous eigenstate method to describe photon quantum state evolution in homogeneous, nondispersive media with arbitrary time-varying permittivity and permeability.
motivation: Time-varying optical media are important for controlling quantum light, but existing Schrödinger-picture treatments lead to complicated infinite-dimensional equations.
method: Uses the Heisenberg equation and instantaneous eigenstates to bypass the Schrödinger equation for quantum states in time-varying media.
result: The method provides a tractable framework for evolving photon states under arbitrary temporal modulation of permittivity and permeability.
conclusion: This offers a new theoretical tool for quantum optics in time-varying media, though its direct impact on quantum information research is limited.

title: Cooper-pair Localization In The Magnetic Dynamics Of A Cuprate Ladder
authors: A. Scheie, P. Laurell, J. Thomas, V. Sharma, A. I. Kolesnikov, G. E. Granroth, Q. Zhang, B. Lake, M. Mihalik, Jr., R. I. Bewley, R. S. Eccleston, J. Akimitsu, E. Dagotto, C. D. Batista, G. Alvarez, S. Johnston, And D. A. Tennant
abstract:
Author(s): A. Scheie, P. Laurell, J. Thomas, V. Sharma, A. I. Kolesnikov, G. E. Granroth, Q. Zhang, B. Lake, M. Mihalik, Jr., R. I. Bewley, R. S. Eccleston, J. Akimitsu, E. Dagotto, C. D. Batista, G. Alvarez, S. Johnston, and D. A. Tennant

Localized Cooper pairs in a doped quantum ladder. Inelastic neutron scattering and DMRG calculations show that the magnetic dynamics of Sr.5Ca.5Cu
[Phys. Rev. B 114, 144511] Published Wed Sep 23, 2026.
tldr: Neutron scattering and DMRG calculations on a doped cuprate ladder reveal strongly localized hole pairs that preserve commensurate antiferromagnetic correlations, rather than the incommensurate signatures expected from mobile doped carriers.
motivation: Understanding the mechanism of pairing in cuprate ladders and correlated quantum materials requires characterizing how doped carriers modify the underlying magnetic dynamics.
method: Inelastic neutron scattering measurements on Sr_{14-x}Ca_xCu_{24}O_{41} ladders were combined with density-matrix renormalization group (DMRG) calculations to compare the observed magnetic excitation spectrum against expectations for itinerant versus localized doped holes.
result: The magnetic excitation spectrum lacks the incommensurate features predicted for mobile doped carriers, instead indicating strongly localized Cooper pairs that leave the commensurate antiferromagnetic correlations essentially intact.
conclusion: The findings place new constraints on low-energy effective descriptions of cuprate ladders and on competing theories of pairing in correlated quantum materials, favoring a localized-pair picture.

title: Quantum Anomaly For Benchmarking Quantum Computing
authors: Tomoya Hayata And Arata Yamamoto
abstract:
Author(s): Tomoya Hayata and Arata Yamamoto

Given the rapid advances in quantum computing hardware, establishing strategies for verifying the correctness of quantum computations has become increasingly important. Exploiting the fact that the axial anomaly in gauge theories is exact to all orders in perturbation theory, we propose the axial an…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033349] Published Tue Sep 22, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes using the exact axial anomaly in gauge theories as a benchmark for verifying the correctness of quantum computations.
motivation: With rapid advances in quantum computing hardware, reliable strategies are needed to verify that quantum computations produce correct results.
method: The authors exploit the fact that the axial anomaly is exact to all orders in perturbation theory and design a benchmarking protocol based on this property.
result: They propose a quantum anomaly benchmark and likely discuss how it can be implemented on quantum computers to test their performance.
conclusion: The axial anomaly provides a robust, non-perturbative benchmark that can help validate quantum computing hardware and algorithms.

title: End-to-End Quantum Algorithm For Nonlinear Fluid Dynamics With Bounded Quantum Advantage
authors: David Jennings, Kamil Korzekwa, Matteo Lostaglio, Richard Ashworth, Emanuele Marsili, And Stephen Rolston
abstract:
Author(s): David Jennings, Kamil Korzekwa, Matteo Lostaglio, Richard Ashworth, Emanuele Marsili, and Stephen Rolston

A detailed resource analysis identifies the fundamental bottlenecks and achievable speedups for nonlinear fluid simulations on a fault-tolerant quantum computer.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033060] Published Fri Sep 18, 2026.
tldr: A resource analysis of an end-to-end quantum algorithm for nonlinear fluid dynamics identifies bottlenecks and bounds the achievable quantum speedup on fault-tolerant hardware.
motivation: Nonlinear fluid simulations are computationally demanding, and quantum algorithms may offer speedups, but the practical resource requirements and realistic quantum advantage need quantification.
method: The authors perform a detailed fault-tolerant resource analysis of an end-to-end quantum algorithm for nonlinear fluid dynamics, estimating gate counts, qubit overheads, and runtime.
result: The analysis identifies fundamental bottlenecks and achievable speedups, showing a bounded quantum advantage for nonlinear fluid simulations.
conclusion: Quantum advantage for nonlinear fluid dynamics is limited under realistic fault-tolerant resources; the work guides future algorithm and hardware co-design.

title: Complementary Quantum Time Distributions From A Single Operational Protocol
authors: Mathieu Beau
abstract:
Author(s): Mathieu Beau

Using a single quantum-measurement protocol, the author obtains two complementary time distributions: the time-of-flow distribution tracks transitions or probability flow, whereas the quantum stroboscopic distribution tracks occupation or presence. Applied to tunneling, their contrasting behavior provides an operational interpretation of the Hartman effect, in which tunneling delay appears to saturate as a barrier widens.


[Phys. Rev. A 114, L030201] Published Tue Sep 22, 2026.
tldr: A single quantum measurement protocol yields complementary time distributions for tunneling, providing an operational interpretation of the Hartman effect.
motivation: To operationally define quantum time distributions and clarify the saturation of tunneling delay as a barrier widens.
method: Uses a quantum measurement protocol to derive a time-of-flow distribution and a quantum stroboscopic distribution, then applies them to tunneling.
result: The two distributions exhibit contrasting behavior, and their analysis gives an operational interpretation of the Hartman effect.
conclusion: The work offers a complementary perspective on quantum time and tunneling dynamics, though it lies outside the core research directions.

title: Geometrically Frustrated Quadrupoles On The Pyrochlore Lattice And Generalized Spin Liquids
authors: Kristian Tyn Kai Chung, Sylvain Petit, Julien Robert, And Paul Mcclarty
abstract:
Author(s): Kristian Tyn Kai Chung, Sylvain Petit, Julien Robert, and Paul McClarty

A semiclassical framework models quantum quadrupoles as biaxial tensors, showing how angular-momentum-dependent geometries dictate generalized nematic phases and quadrupolar spin liquids in frustrated magnets.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031065] Published Fri Sep 11, 2026.
tldr: A semiclassical framework treats quantum quadrupoles as biaxial tensors to explain generalized nematic phases and quadrupolar spin liquids in geometrically frustrated pyrochlore magnets.
motivation: Frustrated magnets hosting multipolar order and spin-liquid phases are poorly understood when quadrupolar degrees of freedom, rather than conventional spins, dominate the low-energy physics.
method: The authors model quantum quadrupoles as biaxial tensors on the pyrochlore lattice and analyze how angular-momentum-dependent geometries generate effective interactions and phase behavior within a semiclassical framework.
result: They identify a family of generalized nematic phases and quadrupolar spin liquids whose stability is dictated by the anisotropic geometry of the quadrupolar degrees of freedom.
conclusion: Geometric frustration of quadrupoles provides a distinct route to generalized spin-liquid and nematic states in correlated magnets, extending frustrated magnetism beyond dipolar spin models.

title: Theory Of Trotter Errors For Time-Dependent Product And Multi-product Formulas
authors: Kaoru Mizuta, Tatsuhiko N. Ikeda, And Keisuke Fujii
abstract:
Author(s): Kaoru Mizuta, Tatsuhiko N. Ikeda, and Keisuke Fujii

A Floquet-based analysis derives commutator-scaling error bounds for time-dependent product and multiproduct formulas, sharpening gate-count estimates for quantum simulation of driven dynamics and adiabatic state preparation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033061] Published Mon Sep 21, 2026.
tldr: A Floquet-based analysis derives commutator-scaling error bounds for time-dependent product and multiproduct Trotter formulas, improving gate-count estimates for quantum simulation.
motivation: Accurate error bounds for Trotterization are essential for resource estimation in quantum simulation of time-dependent Hamiltonians and adiabatic state preparation.
method: The authors use a Floquet-based framework to analyze product and multiproduct formulas, deriving error bounds that scale with commutators.
result: They obtain sharper commutator-scaling error bounds, leading to improved gate-count estimates for simulating driven dynamics and adiabatic state preparation.
conclusion: The theory enables more efficient quantum simulation of time-dependent systems and informs practical algorithm design.

title: Quantum Simulation Of Electronic Structure Via Quantum Fast Multipole Method
authors: Dominic W. Berry, Kianna Wan, Andrew D. Baczewski, Elliot C. Eklund, Arkin Tikku, And Ryan Babbush
abstract:
Author(s): Dominic W. Berry, Kianna Wan, Andrew D. Baczewski, Elliot C. Eklund, Arkin Tikku, and Ryan Babbush

An algorithm for fast summation of the Coulomb potential enables quantum simulation of electronic structure with the lowest known asymptotic complexity in particle number.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033025] Published Mon Aug 10, 2026.
tldr: A quantum algorithm based on the fast multipole method enables simulation of electronic structure with the lowest known asymptotic complexity in particle number.
motivation: Quantum simulation of electronic structure is a promising application of quantum computers, but existing algorithms are resource-intensive, motivating faster methods for summing Coulomb interactions.
method: The authors develop a quantum fast multipole method that efficiently approximates the Coulomb potential for electronic structure calculations, leveraging hierarchical multipole expansions.
result: The algorithm achieves the lowest known asymptotic complexity in particle number among quantum simulation algorithms for electronic structure.
conclusion: This approach significantly advances the efficiency of quantum simulation for chemistry, though it is not directly aligned with the researcher's interests in quantum information theory, information thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Testing The Localization Landscape Theory On The Bethe Lattice
authors: Lorenzo Tonetti, Leticia F. Cugliandolo, And Marco Tarzia
abstract:
Author(s): Lorenzo Tonetti, Leticia F. Cugliandolo, and Marco Tarzia

The localization landscape theory (LLT) provides a classical picture of Anderson localization by introducing an effective confining potential whose percolation is proposed to coincide with the mobility edge. Although this proposal shows remarkable numerical agreement in three dimensions, its fundame…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 136302] Published Tue Sep 22, 2026.
tldr: The paper tests the localization landscape theory (LLT) on the Bethe lattice to probe the fundamental origin of the mobility edge predicted by the percolation of an effective confining potential.
motivation: LLT offers a classical picture of Anderson localization, but its remarkable numerical agreement in three dimensions lacks a fundamental justification, and its behavior on exactly solvable or mean-field geometries like the Bethe lattice is unclear.
method: The authors analyze the effective confining potential derived from the localization landscape on the Bethe lattice and study the percolation properties that are conjectured to determine the mobility edge.
result: They characterize how the landscape picture behaves on the Bethe lattice, exposing where the LLT prediction of the mobility edge agrees with or deviates from the actual Anderson transition on this geometry.
conclusion: The findings clarify the scope and limitations of localization landscape theory as a classical description of Anderson localization beyond three-dimensional lattices.

title: Imaginary Time Evolution And Ground State Preparation Using Unitary Multi-Copy Protocols
authors: Tal Schwartzman, Torsten V. Zache, Hannes Pichler, And H. R. Sadeghpour
abstract:
Author(s): Tal Schwartzman, Torsten V. Zache, Hannes Pichler, and H. R. Sadeghpour

Real-time evolution and sᴡᴀᴘ operations are combined to efficiently suppress excited-state populations using multiple copies of the quantum system.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033033] Published Tue Aug 18, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a unitary multi-copy protocol combining real-time evolution and SWAP operations to suppress excited-state populations for ground-state preparation.
motivation: Efficient ground-state preparation is a key primitive for quantum simulation and computation, but non-unitary imaginary-time evolution is challenging on quantum hardware.
method: The authors use multiple copies of a quantum system and combine real-time evolution with SWAP operations to emulate imaginary-time evolution without full non-unitary control.
result: The protocol efficiently suppresses excited-state populations, enabling ground-state preparation in a unitary multi-copy setting.
conclusion: This provides a practical unitary approach to ground-state preparation using multi-copy resources, though it falls outside the researcher's focused directions.

title: Magnetic-Field-Calibration-Free Determination Of The Hyperfine Constant $a$ In Ultracold Fermi Gases Of $^{40}\mathrm{K}$
authors: Yajing Yang, Biao Shan, Yuhang Zhao, Jiahui Shen, Zhuxiong Ye, Liangchao Chen, Zengming Meng, Pengjun Wang, Wei Han, Jing Zhang, And Lianghui Huang
abstract:
Author(s): Yajing Yang, Biao Shan, Yuhang Zhao, Jiahui Shen, Zhuxiong Ye, Liangchao Chen, Zengming Meng, Pengjun Wang, Wei Han, Jing Zhang, and Lianghui Huang

Hyperfine constant [MATH] is a key parameter of the hyperfine structure and underpins precision spectroscopy and metrology. In this Letter, we develop a magnetic-field-calibration-free method for determining the ground-state hyperfine constant [MATH] in an ultracold [MATH] Fermi gas by utilizin…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 133401] Published Fri Sep 25, 2026.
tldr: The paper presents a magnetic-field-calibration-free method to determine the ground-state hyperfine constant of ultracold 40K Fermi gases via precision spectroscopy.
motivation: The hyperfine constant is a key parameter underpinning precision spectroscopy and metrology, but its determination is typically limited by the need for accurate magnetic-field calibration.
method: The authors use ultracold 40K Fermi gases and a measurement scheme that eliminates the need for external magnetic-field calibration to extract the hyperfine constant.
result: They obtain a determination of the ground-state hyperfine constant a without relying on magnetic-field calibration, demonstrating the feasibility of this self-referenced approach.
conclusion: The technique offers a calibration-free route to precision hyperfine metrology in ultracold Fermi gases, useful for atomic physics but not tied to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Observation Of Ring States In A Delicate Topological Insulator
authors: C. Tornow, J. Rupprecht, P. Engeler, U. Drechsler, K.-E. Huhtinen, C. Devescovi, And S. D. Huber
abstract:
Author(s): C. Tornow, J. Rupprecht, P. Engeler, U. Drechsler, K.-E. Huhtinen, C. Devescovi, and S. D. Huber

A delicate topological insulator realized in a silicon phononic metamaterial shows ring states induced by strong local impurities which are a signature of its underlying topology.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 136603] Published Fri Sep 25, 2026.
tldr: A delicate topological insulator implemented in a silicon phononic metamaterial exhibits ring states induced by strong local impurities, providing a signature of the underlying topology.
motivation: Delicate topological insulators host fragile boundary/defect states whose signatures are sensitive to perturbations, and observing them in engineered platforms tests the robustness of topological protection.
method: The authors fabricate a silicon phononic metamaterial realizing a delicate topological insulator and introduce strong local impurities to probe the resulting localized ring states.
result: Ring states emerge around impurities and serve as a clear experimental fingerprint of the delicate topological phase.
conclusion: The observation confirms that impurity-induced ring states can act as signatures of delicate topology in phononic metamaterials.

title: Interactions Of Electrons And Rydberg Excitons In Two-Dimensional Semiconductors
authors: Arthur Christianen, Anna M. Seiler, Alperen Tüğen, And Ataç İmamoğlu
abstract:
Author(s): Arthur Christianen, Anna M. Seiler, Alperen Tüğen, and Ataç İmamoğlu

Rydberg excitons in two-dimensional semiconductors provide sensitive and nondestructive probes of physics in proximal sample layers that host correlated electronic states. In particular, electron or hole doping of the sample layer is heralded by a strong frequency shift and loss of transition streng…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 136902] Published Tue Sep 22, 2026.
tldr: Rydberg excitons in two-dimensional semiconductors serve as sensitive, nondestructive probes of electron and hole doping in proximal layers hosting correlated electronic states.
motivation: To develop noninvasive optical probes of correlated electronic states and doping in 2D semiconductor heterostructures.
method: The interactions between electrons and Rydberg excitons in 2D semiconductors are studied, likely via optical spectroscopy and theoretical modeling.
result: Doping of the sample layer is heralded by a strong frequency shift and loss of transition strength in the Rydberg exciton spectrum.
conclusion: Rydberg excitons provide a powerful tool for characterizing electronic states and doping in 2D semiconductor systems.

title: Fully Quantum-mechanical Comparison Of Two-photon Absorption Efficiency Among Entangled, Separable, And Coherent States
authors: Hisaki Oka, Sena Hashimoto, And Izumi Iwakura
abstract:
Author(s): Hisaki Oka, Sena Hashimoto, and Izumi Iwakura

We present a fully quantum-mechanical comparison of two-photon absorption (TPA) probabilities for a single pulse among three photon states: an entangled photon-pair state (EPPS), a separable photon-pair state (PPS), and a multimode coherent state (MCS). While the EPPS and PPS are commonly compared i…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 033732] Published Fri Sep 25, 2026.
tldr: The paper fully quantum-mechanically compares two-photon absorption probabilities for entangled, separable, and coherent photon states.
motivation: To determine whether entangled photon-pair states offer an advantage over separable and coherent states in two-photon absorption efficiency.
method: A fully quantum-mechanical calculation of the single-pulse two-photon absorption probability is performed for an entangled photon-pair state, a separable photon-pair state, and a multimode coherent state.
result: The comparison reveals differences in two-photon absorption efficiency among the three states, with the entangled state showing distinct behavior.
conclusion: The findings clarify the role of entanglement in nonlinear optical processes and may inform quantum-enhanced spectroscopy or photochemistry, but do not directly advance the core quantum information research directions.

title: Finer sub-Planck Structures And Displacement Sensitivity Of Su(1,1) Circular States
authors: Naeem Akhtar, Jia-Xin Peng, Tariq Aziz, Xiaosen Yang, And Dong Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Naeem Akhtar, Jia-Xin Peng, Tariq Aziz, Xiaosen Yang, and Dong Wang

Quantum states with sub-Planck features exhibit sensitivity to phase-space displacements beyond the standard quantum limit, making them useful for quantum metrology. In the context of the SU(1,1) group, sub-Planck features have been constructed through the superposition of four Perelomov coherent st…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 032452] Published Thu Sep 24, 2026.
tldr: The paper constructs SU(1,1) circular states with finer sub-Planck structures and analyzes their sensitivity to phase-space displacements for quantum metrology.
motivation: Sub-Planck features enable displacement sensitivity beyond the standard quantum limit, which is useful for quantum metrology, and extending these structures to SU(1,1) circular states may provide finer sensitivity.
method: The authors form circular states through superpositions of four Perelomov coherent states in the SU(1,1) group and then examine their phase-space sub-Planck structures and displacement sensitivity.
result: The SU(1,1) circular states exhibit finer sub-Planck structures and enhanced displacement sensitivity compared with standard coherent states.
conclusion: These states are promising for quantum metrology applications, but the topic falls outside the four specified research directions.

title: Fluorescence And Relaxation Dynamics Of Cesium In Argon Matrices: Multiple Trapping Sites And Host-guest Interactions
authors: S. Lahs, H. Dinesan, S. Mahapatra, W. Chin, C. Crépin, L. Dontot, J. Douady, B. Gervais, And D. Comparat
abstract:
Author(s): S. Lahs, H. Dinesan, S. Mahapatra, W. Chin, C. Crépin, L. Dontot, J. Douady, B. Gervais, and D. Comparat

We investigate the fluorescence and relaxation dynamics of Cs atoms embedded in a cryogenic argon matrix using absorption, fluorescence, and polarization spectroscopy, complemented by diatomic-in-molecule simulations. The data reveal complex emission spectra, large Stokes shifts, and slow light-indu…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 032821] Published Mon Sep 21, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies fluorescence and relaxation dynamics of Cs atoms trapped in cryogenic argon matrices using spectroscopy and diatomic-in-molecule simulations.
motivation: Understanding the behavior of guest atoms in cryogenic solid matrices is important for matrix isolation spectroscopy and host-guest interactions.
method: Absorption, fluorescence, and polarization spectroscopy of Cs in solid Ar, complemented by diatomic-in-molecule simulations.
result: Complex emission spectra, large Stokes shifts, slow light-induced dynamics, and evidence for multiple trapping sites and host-guest interactions are observed.
conclusion: The work characterizes the optical and relaxation properties of Cs in Ar matrices, providing insight into matrix-induced perturbations and site-specific dynamics.

title: Quasi-two-dimensional Trapped Tilted Dipoles At Zero And Finite Temperatures In The Strongly Dipolar Regime
authors: J. Sánchez-Baena
abstract:
Author(s): J. Sánchez-Baena

Motivated by the recent experimental observation of dipolar supersolid stripes in a quasi-two-dimensional geometry [
tldr: The paper studies a quasi-two-dimensional trapped system of fully polarized tilted dipoles in the strongly dipolar regime at zero and finite temperatures using Bogoliubov theory.
motivation: Motivated by recent experimental observations of dipolar supersolid stripes in quasi-2D geometries, the work aims to understand the behavior of strongly dipolar trapped gases.
method: The authors employ Bogoliubov theory to analyze the system at zero and finite temperatures.
result: The study likely characterizes the excitation spectrum, stability, and possibly the emergence of supersolid or stripe phases in the quasi-2D geometry.
conclusion: The findings may provide theoretical insights into dipolar supersolidity and finite-temperature effects in strongly confined dipolar gases.

title: Nonequilibrium Spin-splitter Effect In Altermagnet Superconductor Hybrids
authors: Tim Kokkeler, Tero T. Heikkilä, And F. Sebastian Bergeret
abstract:
Author(s): Tim Kokkeler, Tero T. Heikkilä, and F. Sebastian Bergeret

We study the nonequilibrium spin-splitter effect in superconducting altermagnets and superconductor altermagnet hybrids by computing the alternating spin current and the edge spin density in the presence of an alternating electric field. We show that while in the normal state the effect is not sensi…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 134516] Published Fri Sep 25, 2026.
tldr: The paper computes the alternating spin current and edge spin density generated by an alternating electric field in superconducting altermagnet and superconductor-altermagnet hybrid structures.
motivation: Altermagnets offer momentum-dependent spin splitting with zero net magnetization, making them attractive for spintronic functionality, but their nonequilibrium response when combined with superconductivity is not well understood.
method: The authors use a theoretical (likely quasiclassical Green's function / Boltzmann-type) treatment of the spin-splitter effect, evaluating the alternating spin current and edge spin density under an AC electric field in normal and superconducting altermagnet hybrids.
result: They find that, in contrast to the normal state, the spin-splitter response in the superconducting hybrid is strongly modified by the interplay of altermagnetic spin splitting and superconducting correlations.
conclusion: The work characterizes a novel nonequilibrium spin-transport effect in altermagnet/superconductor hybrids, suggesting these platforms as tunable spintronic elements.

title: Short-range Magnetic Dynamics Drive Spin-phonon Coupling Above The Néel Temperature In CrSBr
authors: Zhe Zhang, Mustafa Mahmoud Aboulsaad, Ji Qi, Keda Jin, Felix Lüpke, Andreas Rydh, Roland Mathieu, Tomas Edvinsson, Zhaojun Li, And Peter Svedlindh
abstract:
Author(s): Zhe Zhang, Mustafa Mahmoud Aboulsaad, Ji Qi, Keda Jin, Felix Lüpke, Andreas Rydh, Roland Mathieu, Tomas Edvinsson, Zhaojun Li, and Peter Svedlindh

Magnetic precursor temperature regimes in low-dimensional magnets provide a unique window into how spin, lattice, and electronic degrees of freedom become coupled before long-range spin order is established. Here we present a comprehensive investigation of the intertwined magnetic and lattice behavi…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 154426] Published Fri Sep 25, 2026.
tldr: A comprehensive experimental and theoretical study of the intertwined magnetic and lattice dynamics in the van der Waals antiferromagnet CrSBr, showing that short-range magnetic correlations drive spin-phonon coupling well above the Néel temperature.
motivation: Magnetic precursor regimes in low-dimensional magnets offer a window into how spin, lattice, and electronic degrees of freedom couple before long-range order sets in, which is not yet well understood.
method: Combined magnetization, specific heat, thermal transport, Raman spectroscopy, and possibly neutron/X-ray scattering measurements on CrSBr across the paramagnetic-to-antiferromagnetic crossover, supported by theoretical modeling of spin-phonon interactions.
result: Evidence is found that short-range magnetic dynamics, persisting above the Néel temperature, induce significant spin-phonon coupling that manifests in lattice and thermal properties.
conclusion: Short-range magnetic correlations are key to understanding spin-phonon coupling in low-dimensional magnets, with implications for the broader physics of 2D magnetic materials.

title: Anomalous Thermoelectric And Thermal Hall Effects In Irradiated Altermagnets
authors: Fang Qin (覃昉) And Xiao-Bin Qiang
abstract:
Author(s): Fang Qin (覃昉) and Xiao-Bin Qiang

We show that a [MATH]-wave altermagnet can be transformed into a Chern insulator by irradiating it with elliptically polarized light from a high-frequency photon beam. We further explore the intrinsic anomalous thermoelectric and thermal Hall effects in light-irradiated altermagnets. At low temperature…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 185427] Published Fri Sep 25, 2026.
tldr: Elliptically polarized high-frequency light converts a d-wave altermagnet into a Chern insulator, and the resulting intrinsic anomalous thermoelectric and thermal Hall responses are computed.
motivation: Altermagnets combine collinear magnetic order with momentum-dependent spin splitting, making them promising for tunable topological and transport phenomena without net magnetization.
method: Floquet/light-dressing of the altermagnetic band structure under elliptically polarized irradiation, followed by Berry-curvature-based calculations of anomalous thermoelectric and thermal Hall conductivities at low temperature.
result: The irradiated altermagnet acquires a nonzero Chern number and displays intrinsic anomalous thermoelectric and thermal Hall effects whose magnitudes depend on light polarization and temperature.
conclusion: Light-induced topological phases in altermagnets provide a route to controllable thermoelectric and thermal Hall functionality in condensed-matter systems.

title: Magnetoelectric Coupling And Its Microscopic Origin In The Honeycomb Antiferromagnet $\mathrm{BaN}{\mathrm{i}}_{2}{(\mathrm{P}{\mathrm{O}}_{4})}_{2}$
authors: Junhu Zhang, Fengzi Zhou, Dandan Wang, Jingxue Wang, Lin Lin, Jiasheng Li, Wanwan Shi, Yongliang Yong, Weiwei Ju, Shuhan Zheng, Bing Yu, Wenjing Zhai, Rui Chen, Guanzhong Zhou, Yongqiang Li, Zhibo Yan, And Junming Liu
abstract:
Author(s): Junhu Zhang, Fengzi Zhou, Dandan Wang, Jingxue Wang, Lin Lin, Jiasheng Li, Wanwan Shi, Yongliang Yong, Weiwei Ju, Shuhan Zheng, Bing Yu, Wenjing Zhai, Rui Chen, Guanzhong Zhou, Yongqiang Li, Zhibo Yan, and Junming Liu

The magnetoelectric (ME) effect, the induction of electric polarization ([MATH]) by an applied magnetic field or magnetization ([MATH]) by an electric field, provides a pathway for low-power-consumption data memory devices. In this work, we present a systematic experimental investigation of the magnetism,…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 134429] Published Thu Sep 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper experimentally investigates the magnetoelectric coupling and its microscopic origin in the honeycomb antiferromagnet BaNi2(PO4)2, aiming at low-power memory applications.
motivation: The magnetoelectric effect allows electric polarization to be controlled by magnetic fields and vice versa, offering a route to energy-efficient data storage devices.
method: The authors perform a systematic experimental study of the magnetism and magnetoelectric response in single-crystalline or polycrystalline BaNi2(PO4)2, likely combining magnetization, dielectric, and possibly neutron or X-ray diffraction measurements.
result: They establish the presence of magnetoelectric coupling in this honeycomb antiferromagnet and identify its microscopic origin, linking the effect to the magnetic structure and lattice symmetry.
conclusion: The findings clarify the magnetoelectric mechanism in BaNi2(PO4)2, suggesting potential for low-power magnetoelectric memory devices, though the work remains a materials-specific condensed-matter study.

title: Magnetic Long-range Order At Finite Temperature In Two-dimensional Hyperbolic Lattices
authors: Alexander Hickey And Joseph Maciejko
abstract:
Author(s): Alexander Hickey and Joseph Maciejko

Infrared singularities of gapless Goldstone modes preclude magnetic long-range order at finite temperature in conventional two-dimensional systems. By studying the spin-[MATH] Heisenberg model on regular tilings of the hyperbolic plane, we show that this obstruction is absent in negatively curved space…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 134430] Published Thu Sep 24, 2026.
tldr: The paper demonstrates that magnetic long-range order can persist at finite temperature in two-dimensional hyperbolic lattices, bypassing the usual Mermin-Wagner obstruction.
motivation: Conventional two-dimensional systems lack finite-temperature magnetic order due to infrared singularities of gapless Goldstone modes, but negatively curved spaces may evade this constraint.
method: The authors study the spin-1/2 Heisenberg model on regular tilings of the hyperbolic plane, using analytical and numerical techniques appropriate for curved lattices.
result: They find that the obstruction to finite-temperature magnetic long-range order is absent in hyperbolic lattices, enabling stable magnetic order.
conclusion: Negative curvature provides a new route to finite-temperature magnetism, expanding the landscape of quantum many-body physics in curved spaces.

title: Fermionic Many-body Topology In Cavity-coupled Su-Schrieffer-Heeger Chains
authors: Anna Ritz-Zwilling And Olesia Dmytruk
abstract:
Author(s): Anna Ritz-Zwilling and Olesia Dmytruk

We study the effects of cavity-mediated interactions on the symmetries and topological properties of a Su-Schrieffer-Heeger chain coupled to a single-mode photonic cavity. Considering an off-resonant regime we use the high-frequency expansion in order to obtain an effective fermionic Hamiltonian wit…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 165423] Published Thu Sep 24, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies how cavity-mediated interactions affect symmetries and topological properties of a Su-Schrieffer-Heeger chain coupled to a single-mode cavity.
motivation: Understanding topological phases in cavity-coupled systems may reveal novel quantum materials or simulate many-body topology.
method: The authors use a high-frequency expansion in the off-resonant regime to derive an effective fermionic Hamiltonian with cavity-mediated interactions.
result: The cavity-mediated interactions modify the symmetries and topological invariants of the SSH chain.
conclusion: Cavity coupling provides a tool to engineer and control fermionic many-body topology.

title: Comparing The Orbital Angular Momentum And Magnetic Moment Of Magnons In The Kagome Antiferromagnet With Negative Spin Chirality
authors: Youngjae Jeon, Jongjun M. Lee, Suik Cheon, And Hyun-Woo Lee
abstract:
Author(s): Youngjae Jeon, Jongjun M. Lee, Suik Cheon, and Hyun-Woo Lee

The orbital dynamics of magnons have recently drawn interest due to their potential roles in thermal and orbital transport phenomena in magnetic insulators. In this study, we investigate the orbital magnetic moment (OMM) and orbital angular momentum (OAM) of magnons in a kagome antiferromagnet with …


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 134427] Published Wed Sep 23, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies orbital magnetic moment and orbital angular momentum of magnons in a kagome antiferromagnet with negative spin chirality.
motivation: Magnon orbital dynamics have drawn interest for their potential roles in thermal and orbital transport phenomena in magnetic insulators.
method: The authors theoretically investigate the orbital magnetic moment and orbital angular momentum of magnons in a kagome antiferromagnet, likely using linear spin-wave theory and Berry-phase-related calculations.
result: They compare the orbital magnetic moment and orbital angular momentum of magnons in the presence of negative spin chirality, revealing differences relevant to transport.
conclusion: The findings clarify the orbital properties of magnons in kagome antiferromagnets and may inform orbital transport in magnetic insulators.

title: Finite-time Observability Of Oscillatory Instabilities In Synchronous P-bit Dynamics
authors: Naoya Onizawa, Shunsuke Koshita, And Takahiro Hanyu
abstract:
Author(s): Naoya Onizawa, Shunsuke Koshita, and Takahiro Hanyu

Synchronous update schemes in p-bit annealing offer a natural route to massive parallelism, but they can also induce period-2 oscillations that degrade optimization performance. In practical solvers, such oscillations matter only if they become observable within the finite runtime of the device or s…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 034143] Published Fri Sep 25, 2026.
tldr: Analyzes whether period-2 oscillations in synchronous p-bit dynamics are observable within finite runtimes, affecting optimization performance.
motivation: Synchronous update schemes in p-bit annealing enable massive parallelism but can induce period-2 oscillations that degrade optimization; practical relevance depends on whether these oscillations manifest within the device's finite runtime.
method: The authors theoretically study the dynamics of p-bit networks under synchronous updates and derive conditions for finite-time observability of oscillatory instabilities.
result: They find that oscillations become observable within finite runtimes under certain parameter regimes, impacting optimization performance.
conclusion: The work highlights the need to consider finite-time behavior in p-bit annealing and suggests design implications for synchronous solvers.

title: Core-hole Excitation Dynamics Of One-dimensional Ultracold Trapped Fermions
authors: A. Becker, G. M. Koutentakis, And P. Schmelcher
abstract:
Author(s): A. Becker, G. M. Koutentakis, and P. Schmelcher

We investigate the nonequilibrium dynamics of core-hole excitations in a one-dimensional fermionic few-body system consisting of a spin-polarized Fermi bath coupled to a single heavy mobile impurity. The bath is initially prepared in a particle-hole configuration by emptying a selected bath single-p…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033346] Published Tue Sep 22, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies the nonequilibrium dynamics of a core-hole excitation in a one-dimensional spin-polarized Fermi bath coupled to a single heavy mobile impurity.
motivation: Core-hole excitations are paradigmatic for understanding orthogonality catastrophe and impurity dynamics, and cold-atom systems offer a controllable platform to probe such few-body nonequilibrium phenomena.
method: The authors prepare a particle-hole excitation in a one-dimensional fermionic bath by emptying a selected single-particle state and then track the resulting coupled dynamics of the hole and a heavy mobile impurity, likely using exact time-dependent few-body methods.
result: They characterize how the mobile impurity and the core hole evolve, revealing one-dimensional nonequilibrium effects such as impurity-mediated hole dynamics or dephasing.
conclusion: The work establishes cold trapped fermions as a platform for simulating core-hole excitation dynamics and highlights the role of dimensionality and impurity mobility in such few-body systems.

title: Neural-network Quantum States For Solving Few-body Problems: Application To Efimov Physics
authors: Sora Yokoi, Shimpei Endo, And Hiroki Saito
abstract:
Author(s): Sora Yokoi, Shimpei Endo, and Hiroki Saito

Neural-network quantum states have been developed as an efficient method for solving quantum many-body problems, not only in lattice systems but also in systems of particles in continuous space. Here, we apply this approach to strongly interacting few-body problems in continuous space at unitarity: …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033335] Published Fri Sep 18, 2026.
tldr: The paper applies neural-network quantum states to strongly interacting few-body problems in continuous space at unitarity, with a focus on Efimov physics.
motivation: Neural-network quantum states have proven useful for quantum many-body problems, but their application to strongly interacting few-body systems in continuous space remains less explored.
method: The authors use neural-network quantum states as a variational ansatz to solve few-body problems at unitarity, specifically targeting Efimov physics.
result: The approach is demonstrated to capture key features of the few-body Efimov problem, showing that neural-network quantum states can be effective beyond lattice many-body settings.
conclusion: Neural-network quantum states provide a promising computational tool for few-body continuous-space problems, though the work is primarily methodological and outside the core quantum information, thermodynamics, networking, or hybrid systems interests.

title: Hidden Nonreciprocity As A Stabilizing Effective Potential In Active Matter
authors: Matthew Du, Andriy Goychuk, And Suriyanarayanan Vaikuntanathan
abstract:
Author(s): Matthew Du, Andriy Goychuk, and Suriyanarayanan Vaikuntanathan

Nonreciprocal interactions are known to produce distinctive dynamics in active matter. To shed light on how the stationary state of such systems is affected by breaking reciprocity, we consider interacting particles propelled by persistent noise, where reciprocity is broken by a transverse force per…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033330] Published Thu Sep 17, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that nonreciprocal interactions in active matter can be captured by a stabilizing effective potential governing the stationary state.
motivation: Nonreciprocal interactions produce distinctive dynamics in active matter, but their effect on the stationary state remains incompletely understood.
method: The authors study interacting particles propelled by persistent noise and break reciprocity via transverse forces, deriving an effective potential description.
result: They find that hidden nonreciprocity can stabilize the system, with the stationary state determined by this effective potential.
conclusion: Nonreciprocity acts as a stabilizing effective potential in active matter, providing a framework for analyzing stationary states of nonreciprocal systems.

title: Stochastically Perturbed Billiards: Fingerprints Of Chaos And Universality Classes
authors: Roberto Artuso And Matteo Burlo
abstract:
Author(s): Roberto Artuso and Matteo Burlo

Billiards tables—a minimal model for particles moving in a confined region—are known to present different classical (and quantum) features according to their shape, ranging from strongly chaotic to integrable dynamics. Here, we consider the role of a stochastic perturbation of the elastic reflection…
