[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033312] Published Tue Sep 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how stochastic perturbations of elastic reflections in billiard tables affect classical and quantum signatures of chaos and universality classes.
motivation: Billiards are minimal models for confined particle dynamics, and understanding the impact of noise on their chaotic and integrable features is relevant for real-world systems with imperfections.
method: The authors introduce a stochastic perturbation to the elastic reflection law in billiards and analyze classical trajectories and quantum spectral statistics.
result: They identify fingerprints of chaos and universality classes that persist or change under stochastic perturbation, linking noise strength to transitions between chaotic and integrable behavior.
conclusion: Stochastic perturbations can significantly alter the chaotic dynamics and universality of billiards, offering insights into robustness of chaos signatures.

title: Genuine And Spurious (Non-)Ergodicity In Single Particle Tracking
authors: Wei Wang, Qing Wei, Igor M. Sokolov, Ralf Metzler, And Aleksei Chechkin
abstract:
Author(s): Wei Wang, Qing Wei, Igor M. Sokolov, Ralf Metzler, and Aleksei Chechkin

The mean-squared increment is introduced as a new statistic to characterize single-particle positional time series data, providing a more precise and unambiguous method than previous approaches to evaluating ergodicity and helping to discriminate between different classes of stochastic processes.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031071] Published Thu Sep 17, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a mean-squared-increment statistic to more precisely and unambiguously assess ergodicity in single-particle tracking time series and distinguish stochastic process classes.
motivation: Ergodicity tests in single-particle tracking are often ambiguous, and better statistics are needed to discriminate between different stochastic processes and genuine versus spurious non-ergodic behavior.
method: The authors define and analyze the mean-squared increment as a new statistic for positional time series data, applying it to evaluate ergodicity and classify stochastic processes.
result: The mean-squared increment provides a more precise and unambiguous method than previous approaches for evaluating ergodicity and discriminating between different classes of stochastic processes.
conclusion: The proposed statistic improves the analysis of single-particle tracking data and helps clarify genuine versus spurious (non-)ergodicity in stochastic processes.

title: Exact Nematic And Mixed Magnetic Phases Driven By Competing Orders On The Pyrochlore Lattice
authors: Niccolò Francini, Lukas Schmidt, Lukas Janssen, And Daniel Lozano-Gómez
abstract:
Author(s): Niccolò Francini, Lukas Schmidt, Lukas Janssen, and Daniel Lozano-Gómez

Analysis of a frustrated pyrochlore spin model demonstrates that thermal fluctuations and parameter-dependent symmetries suppress conventional order to stabilize a magnetic nematic phase.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031070] Published Wed Sep 16, 2026.
tldr: A frustrated pyrochlore spin model is shown to stabilize an unusual magnetic nematic phase due to thermal fluctuations and parameter-dependent symmetries that suppress conventional order.
motivation: Frustrated magnets on the pyrochlore lattice host rich competing orders, but the mechanisms by which fluctuations select exotic phases such as nematicity over conventional magnetic order remain incompletely understood.
method: The authors analyze a frustrated pyrochlore spin model, combining symmetry arguments with thermal fluctuation effects to determine which orders are suppressed and which unconventional phases survive.
result: They find that thermal fluctuations and parameter-dependent symmetries suppress conventional long-range magnetic order, stabilizing an exact nematic phase and mixed magnetic phases driven by the competition between orders.
conclusion: The work provides a concrete mechanism for fluctuation-driven nematic order on the pyrochlore lattice, highlighting how competing interactions and symmetry can produce exotic magnetic phases.

title: Pomeranchuk Instability Induced By An Emergent Higher-Order Van Hove Singularity On The Distorted Kagome Surface Of ${\mathrm{Co}}_{3}{\mathrm{Sn}}_{2}{\mathrm{S}}_{2}$
authors: Pranab Kumar Nag, Rajib Batabyal, Julian Ingham, Noam Morali, Hengxin Tan, Jahyun Koo, Jean Souza, Moshe Haim, Armando Consiglio, Enke Liu, Raquel Queiroz, Ronny Thomale, Binghai Yan, Claudia Felser, Nurit Avraham, And Haim Beidenkopf
abstract:
Author(s): Pranab Kumar Nag, Rajib Batabyal, Julian Ingham, Noam Morali, Hengxin Tan, Jahyun Koo, Jean Souza, Moshe Haim, Armando Consiglio, Enke Liu, Raquel Queiroz, Ronny Thomale, Binghai Yan, Claudia Felser, Nurit Avraham, and Haim Beidenkopf

Surface deformation of the kagome lattice in
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031069] Published Tue Sep 15, 2026.
tldr: Surface deformation of the kagome lattice in Co3Sn2S2 flattens saddle points into a higher-order Van Hove singularity, driving a Pomeranchuk instability and nematic electronic order.
motivation: The authors aim to understand how lattice distortions on the kagome surface of a topological material can reshape the electronic band structure and induce symmetry-broken phases.
method: The study combines spectroscopic/structural surface probes (e.g., STM/ARPES) with band-structure calculations to characterize the distorted kagome surface and identify the emergent higher-order Van Hove singularity.
result: The flattened saddle points produce a higher-order Van Hove singularity that triggers a Pomeranchuk instability, giving rise to nematic states on the Co3Sn2S2 kagome surface.
conclusion: The work establishes a link between surface lattice deformation, higher-order Van Hove singularities, and electronic nematicity, highlighting the kagome surface as a platform for emergent correlated phases.

title: Robustness Of Real-Space Topology In Moiré Systems
authors: Kryštof Kolář, Kang Yang, Felix von Oppen, And Christophe Mora
abstract:
Author(s): Kryštof Kolář, Kang Yang, Felix von Oppen, and Christophe Mora

Topological analysis of real-space electronic textures in nonidealized moiré systems establishes a robust band index and maps wave functions onto a texturally derived fictitious magnetic field.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031043] Published Wed Aug 19, 2026.
tldr: The paper establishes a robust real-space topological band index for nonidealized moiré systems by mapping electronic wave functions onto a texturally derived fictitious magnetic field.
motivation: Moiré systems host rich topological physics, but idealized assumptions often used in momentum-space analyses may fail in realistic, nonidealized devices with disorder and lattice relaxation.
method: The authors perform a real-space topological analysis of electronic textures, defining a band index from the spatial structure and mapping wave functions onto a fictitious magnetic field derived from the texture.
result: The constructed band index is shown to be robust against nonidealities, and the fictitious magnetic field mapping provides a physically transparent description of the topological band structure.
conclusion: Real-space topology offers a robust framework for characterizing moiré bands, connecting spatial electronic textures to topological invariants relevant to correlated and topological moiré phenomena.

title: Experimental Neuromorphic Computing Based On Quantum Memristor
authors: Mirela Selimović, Iris Agresti, Michał Siemaszko, Joshua Morris, Borivoje Dakić, Riccardo Albiero, Andrea Crespi, Francesco Ceccarelli, Roberto Osellame, Magdalena Stobińska-Moretto, And Philip Walther
abstract:
Author(s): Mirela Selimović, Iris Agresti, Michał Siemaszko, Joshua Morris, Borivoje Dakić, Riccardo Albiero, Andrea Crespi, Francesco Ceccarelli, Roberto Osellame, Magdalena Stobińska-Moretto, and Philip Walther

A photonic neuromorphic architecture leverages a quantum memristor to enable nonlinear, memory-dependent processing for complex learning tasks such as vowel recognition.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033067] Published Fri Sep 25, 2026.
tldr: A photonic quantum memristor enables neuromorphic computing for nonlinear, memory-dependent tasks such as vowel recognition.
motivation: Neuromorphic computing aims to mimic brain-like processing with memory and nonlinearity, and quantum memristors could extend this paradigm into the quantum regime.
method: The authors experimentally implement a photonic neuromorphic architecture based on a quantum memristor and test it on complex learning tasks including vowel recognition.
result: The quantum memristor exhibits nonlinear, memory-dependent processing that supports learning tasks such as vowel recognition in the photonic platform.
conclusion: The work provides a proof-of-concept for quantum neuromorphic computing, though it does not directly address the user's core interests in quantum information theory, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Efficient Quantum Optimization Via Dynamical Simulation
authors: Ahmet Burak Catli, Sophia Simon, And Nathan Wiebe
abstract:
Author(s): Ahmet Burak Catli, Sophia Simon, and Nathan Wiebe

A gradient-free approach to quantum optimization based on coherent simulation of time evolution can outperform gradient-descent-based methods in query complexity and robustness to barren plateaus.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033026] Published Wed Aug 12, 2026.
tldr: A gradient-free quantum optimization method based on coherent simulation of time evolution outperforms gradient-descent-based methods in query complexity and robustness to barren plateaus.
motivation: Gradient-based quantum optimization algorithms often suffer from barren plateaus and high query complexity, limiting their practical efficiency.
method: The authors propose a gradient-free optimization approach that coherently simulates time evolution to guide the optimization process.
result: The method achieves better query complexity and improved robustness against barren plateaus compared to standard gradient-descent-based quantum optimization.
conclusion: Dynamical simulation offers a promising alternative for efficient quantum optimization, particularly in scenarios where gradients are unreliable.

title: Evolution Of Electron Spin Resonance Through A Metallic Quantum Critical Phase Diagram
authors: Marc Scheffler, Jörg Sichelschmidt, Conrad Clauss, Mojtaba Javaheri Rahim, Boris I. Kochelaev, Cornelius Krellner, Christoph Geibel, Frank Steglich, And Martin Dressel
abstract:
Author(s): Marc Scheffler, Jörg Sichelschmidt, Conrad Clauss, Mojtaba Javaheri Rahim, Boris I. Kochelaev, Cornelius Krellner, Christoph Geibel, Frank Steglich, and Martin Dressel

Using multiple antennae and their resonance harmonics, the changes in the electron spin resonance signal across the quantum critical point provide a measurement of the g-factor of the electrons.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 136506] Published Fri Sep 25, 2026.
tldr: Electron spin resonance measurements across a metallic quantum critical phase diagram reveal changes in the ESR signal that provide a measurement of the electron g-factor.
motivation: Quantum critical points in metallic systems host unusual electronic states, and probing their spin dynamics via ESR can provide insight into the g-factor and local magnetic environment.
method: The authors used multiple antennae and their resonance harmonics to track the ESR signal as a function of the tuning parameter across the quantum critical point.
result: The ESR signal evolves across the quantum critical phase diagram, enabling extraction of the electron g-factor and revealing changes near the critical point.
conclusion: These measurements demonstrate that ESR is a sensitive probe of g-factor evolution through a metallic quantum critical phase diagram.

title: Interlayer-coupling Control Of High-harmonic Generation In Bilayer ${\mathrm{WS}}_{2}$
authors: Xiaoteng Tang, Zhongxue Ren, Yue Lang, Jing Zhao, And Zengxiu Zhao
abstract:
Author(s): Xiaoteng Tang, Zhongxue Ren, Yue Lang, Jing Zhao, and Zengxiu Zhao

We investigate how interlayer coupling shapes high-harmonic generation (HHG) in AA-stacked bilayer [MATH] using real-time time-dependent density functional theory and semiconductor Bloch equations. The bilayer harmonic yield is found to depart from the coherent layer-number enhancement …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 033115] Published Fri Sep 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how interlayer coupling controls high-harmonic generation (HHG) in AA-stacked bilayer WS2 using real-time time-dependent density functional theory and semiconductor Bloch equations.
motivation: Understanding how the number of layers and their coupling modifies high-harmonic generation is important for controlling strong-field light-matter interaction in two-dimensional materials.
method: The authors employ real-time time-dependent density functional theory combined with semiconductor Bloch equation modeling to simulate HHG in AA-stacked bilayer WS2 with tunable interlayer coupling.
result: The bilayer harmonic yield deviates from the expected coherent layer-number enhancement, revealing that interlayer coupling substantially reshapes the HHG spectrum and yield.
conclusion: Interlayer coupling is a key tuning knob for high-harmonic generation in layered transition-metal dichalcogenides, offering a route to control nonlinear optical responses in 2D materials.

title: Squeezing States Of Light In A Surface Nanoscale Axial Photonics Microresonator
authors: Alena Yu. Kolesnikova
abstract:
Author(s): Alena Yu. Kolesnikova

We develop a theory for the quantum-fluctuation spectrum of nonlinearly interacting whispering-gallery modes in a cylindrical microresonator with small radius variations. We show that the nonuniform axial spatial distribution of the modes can be used to optimize the coupler position, enabling both e…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 033730] Published Wed Sep 23, 2026.
tldr: A theoretical study of quantum-fluctuation spectra and squeezed light generation in a surface nanoscale axial photonics microresonator with nonlinearly interacting whispering-gallery modes.
motivation: Squeezed states of light are a key resource in quantum optics, and optimizing their generation in compact microresonators is important for integrated quantum photonics.
method: The author develops a quantum theory of nonlinearly interacting whispering-gallery modes in a cylindrical microresonator with small radius variations and calculates the quantum-fluctuation spectrum.
result: The nonuniform axial distribution of the modes is shown to allow optimization of the coupler position, enabling efficient squeezing of the output light.
conclusion: The work provides design principles for realizing squeezed light in surface nanoscale axial photonics microresonators, potentially useful for integrated quantum optical circuits.

title: Magnetic Tuning Of Quantum Backflow: Schrödinger Vs Pauli System
authors: Tomasz Radożycki
abstract:
Author(s): Tomasz Radożycki

Probability backflow is investigated for charged spin-[MATH] particles in a uniform magnetic field within the lowest-Landau-level approximation. While single-mode Landau states exhibit only weak and nonrobust backflow, it is shown that two-mode interference gives rise to negative probability flux in …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 032216] Published Tue Sep 22, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies probability backflow for charged spin-1/2 particles in a uniform magnetic field, comparing Schrödinger and Pauli descriptions within the lowest-Landau-level approximation.
motivation: Quantum backflow is a counterintuitive phenomenon where probability flows opposite to the direction of momentum, but its behavior for spin particles in magnetic fields remains largely unexplored.
method: The author analyzes single-mode and two-mode Landau states in the lowest-Landau-level approximation, computing the probability flux for both Schrödinger and Pauli systems to identify conditions for negative flux.
result: Single-mode Landau states produce only weak and nonrobust backflow, whereas two-mode interference generates significant negative probability flux that can be tuned by the magnetic field.
conclusion: Magnetic fields provide a controllable knob for quantum backflow, and the Pauli system exhibits qualitatively different backflow behavior compared to the Schrödinger case.

title: Strain-reconfigurable Linear Dichroism In A Single-valley Two-dimensional Material
authors: Xikui Ma, Hongxia Bu, Yiyi Guo, Juan Wang, Naiqiang Yin, And Mingwen Zhao
abstract:
Author(s): Xikui Ma, Hongxia Bu, Yiyi Guo, Juan Wang, Naiqiang Yin, and Mingwen Zhao

Conventional valleytronics relies on two momentum-separated valleys characterized by opposing optical selection rules. However, this bivalley architecture encounters challenges due to intervalley scattering and static selection rules. In this study, we propose a single-valley architecture capable of…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 134108] Published Fri Sep 25, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a single-valley two-dimensional material architecture with strain-reconfigurable linear dichroism to overcome limitations of conventional bivalley valleytronics.
motivation: Conventional valleytronics relies on two momentum-separated valleys with opposite optical selection rules, which suffer from intervalley scattering and static selection rules.
method: The authors design a single-valley architecture and use theoretical/computational modeling to demonstrate strain-reconfigurable linear dichroism in a two-dimensional material.
result: The proposed system exhibits linear dichroism that can be reversibly tuned by applied strain, enabling dynamic control of optical valley properties.
conclusion: This strain-reconfigurable single-valley platform may open new routes for valleytronic devices with enhanced robustness and tunability.

title: Origin Of Bulk $d$-wave Spin Splitting In ${\mathrm{CuF}}_{2}$
authors: Muskan, Subhadeep Bandyopadhyay, And Sayantika Bhowal
abstract:
Author(s): Muskan, Subhadeep Bandyopadhyay, and Sayantika Bhowal

With the advent of nonrelativistic spin splitting in collinear compensated antiferromagnets, several candidate materials have also been proposed, among which the family of transition-metal difluorides stands out as a prominent example. Within this family, most members exhibit planar [MATH]-wave spin sp…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 144425] Published Fri Sep 25, 2026.
tldr: The paper investigates the microscopic origin of bulk d-wave spin splitting in the collinear compensated antiferromagnet CuF2 using first-principles calculations.
motivation: Nonrelativistic spin splitting in collinear compensated antiferromagnets has recently attracted attention, and transition-metal difluorides are prominent candidate materials whose spin-splitting symmetry is not fully understood.
method: The authors perform density functional theory calculations and symmetry analysis to identify the orbital and magnetic contributions responsible for the bulk d-wave spin splitting in CuF2.
result: The study identifies the specific ligand-orbital and magnetic-ordering mechanisms that generate the d-wave spin texture, distinguishing CuF2 from other members of the difluoride family that show planar g-wave or p-wave splitting.
conclusion: The findings clarify the material-specific design rules for realizing unconventional spin-splitting symmetries in collinear antiferromagnets, with potential relevance to spintronics.

title: Revisiting Magnetoelectric Response In Collinear Antiferromagnetic Zigzag Chains: A Downfolding Approach Beyond Conventional Low-energy Models
authors: Shuhei Kanda And Satoru Hayami
abstract:
Author(s): Shuhei Kanda and Satoru Hayami

Magnetoelectric (ME) effects in antiferromagnets provide a fertile platform for exploring symmetry-driven cross-correlated responses. However, their microscopic origin remains elusive and is often obscured in simplified low-energy descriptions. In this study, we revisit the microscopic mechanism of …


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 165141] Published Fri Sep 25, 2026.
tldr: The paper revisits the microscopic mechanism of magnetoelectric response in collinear antiferromagnetic zigzag chains using a downfolding approach that goes beyond conventional low-energy models.
motivation: Magnetoelectric effects in antiferromagnets offer a platform for symmetry-driven cross-correlated responses, but their microscopic origin is often obscured in simplified low-energy descriptions.
method: The authors employ a downfolding approach to derive an effective description of the magnetoelectric response beyond conventional low-energy models.
result: The study clarifies the microscopic origin of the magnetoelectric effect in collinear antiferromagnetic zigzag chains within this extended framework.
conclusion: The work provides a more complete understanding of magnetoelectric responses in antiferromagnets, highlighting the limitations of simplified low-energy treatments.

title: Edge-controlled non-Hermitian Skin Effect In The Modified Haldane Model
authors: Nobuhiro Ito And Shun Uchino
abstract:
Author(s): Nobuhiro Ito and Shun Uchino

The hybrid skin-topological effect (HSTE) arises from the interplay between the non-Hermitian skin effect and topologically protected edge states. Here, we investigate the HSTE associated with antichiral edge states. As a minimal model, we study a modified Haldane nanoribbon in which gain and loss a…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 165137] Published Thu Sep 24, 2026.
tldr: The paper investigates edge-controlled non-Hermitian skin effect and hybrid skin-topological effect in a modified Haldane nanoribbon with gain and loss.
motivation: To understand the interplay between the non-Hermitian skin effect and topologically protected edge states, especially those associated with antichiral edge states.
method: The authors study a modified Haldane nanoribbon with gain and loss as a minimal model, analyzing its non-Hermitian band topology and edge-state properties.
result: They identify a hybrid skin-topological effect tied to antichiral edge states and show that the non-Hermitian skin effect can be controlled by the edges.
conclusion: The work demonstrates edge-controlled non-Hermitian skin effect in a topological model, extending the understanding of hybrid skin-topological phases.

title: Anisotropic Magnetoresistance Of Two-dimensional Rashba Systems With In-plane Zeeman Field And Pointlike Disorder
authors: Igor Gornyi And Alexander Khaetskii
abstract:
Author(s): Igor Gornyi and Alexander Khaetskii

We study the dc conductivity of a two-dimensional Rashba system with an in-plane Zeeman field and delta-correlated scalar disorder. We show that, although the field deforms the two helicity Fermi contours and rotates the spin texture, it does not produce anisotropic magnetoresistance in the leading …


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 175410] Published Thu Sep 24, 2026.
tldr: A theoretical study of dc conductivity in a two-dimensional Rashba spin-orbit coupled system with in-plane Zeeman field and delta-correlated disorder, showing no leading-order anisotropic magnetoresistance.
motivation: Anisotropic magnetoresistance is a well-known transport phenomenon in magnetic systems, and its behavior in Rashba spin-orbit systems with in-plane fields is not fully understood at the level of leading-order conductivity.
method: Analytical transport theory (diagrammatic/kinetic approach) for a 2D Rashba Hamiltonian with in-plane Zeeman field and pointlike scalar disorder, evaluating the dc conductivity tensor.
result: The in-plane field deforms the helicity Fermi contours and rotates the spin texture, but the leading-order dc conductivity remains isotropic, so no anisotropic magnetoresistance appears at leading order.
conclusion: Anisotropic magnetoresistance in Rashba systems must originate from higher-order corrections or additional mechanisms beyond the simple deformed-Fermi-contour picture studied here.

title: Theoretical Investigation Of Two-dimensional Semiconductor Nanoribbons And Nanoparticles For Tailored Light-matter Interactions
authors: Christian Nicolaisen Hansen, Line Jelver, And Christos Tserkezis
abstract:
Author(s): Christian Nicolaisen Hansen, Line Jelver, and Christos Tserkezis

We explore theoretically the optical response of two-dimensional (2D) materials patterned at the nanoscale into either arrays of ribbons along a planar surface or spherical particles. Fourier-Floquet decomposition of the electromagnetic fields is used in order to obtain the reflectance, transmittanc…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 175411] Published Thu Sep 24, 2026.
tldr: A theoretical study of the optical response of nanoscale-patterned 2D semiconductor ribbons and spherical particles using Fourier-Floquet electromagnetic field decomposition.
motivation: The authors aim to understand and tailor light-matter interactions in nanoscale-patterned two-dimensional materials, exploiting the geometry of ribbons and nanoparticles to engineer reflectance and transmittance.
method: Fourier-Floquet decomposition of the electromagnetic fields is employed to compute reflectance, transmittance and other optical properties of 2D material arrays patterned as ribbons or spheres.
result: The electromagnetic response of the patterned 2D structures is characterized, revealing how the nanoscale geometry of ribbons and particles shapes the optical spectra.
conclusion: Nanoscale patterning of 2D semiconductors provides a route to tailored light-matter interactions, with potential applications in nanophotonic and optoelectronic devices.

title: Observation Of End-to-end Pumping In A Quasiperiodic Fibonacci-type Photonic Chain
authors: Arnob Kumar Ghosh, Ang Chen, Ashraf El Hassan, Patric Holmvall, Mohamed Bourennane, And Annica M. Black-Schaffer
abstract:
Author(s): Arnob Kumar Ghosh, Ang Chen, Ashraf El Hassan, Patric Holmvall, Mohamed Bourennane, and Annica M. Black-Schaffer

End-to-end pumps utilizing edge-localized states offer a promising route to operate as connecting buses, supplying efficient and robust connectivity between non-neighboring elements in a network. Here, we investigate a finite quasiperiodic Fibonacci-type photonic chain and demonstrate its ability fo…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033347] Published Tue Sep 22, 2026.
tldr: The paper investigates a finite quasiperiodic Fibonacci-type photonic chain and demonstrates end-to-end pumping via edge-localized states for robust connectivity between distant elements.
motivation: There is a need for efficient and robust connectivity between non-neighboring elements in networks, and end-to-end pumps using edge-localized states could serve as connecting buses.
method: A finite quasiperiodic Fibonacci-type photonic chain is studied, likely through theoretical modeling and/or optical experiments, to observe end-to-end pumping behavior.
result: The chain supports end-to-end pumping, where edge-localized states enable robust transport between distant sites.
conclusion: Quasiperiodic photonic chains may function as reliable connecting buses in networks, offering a platform for robust long-range connectivity.

title: Effective Ionic Valence And Local Magnetic Moment In Kagome Superconductors
authors: Ruoshi Jiang, Zi-Jian Lang, Yuzki Oey, Andrea Capa Salinas, Stephen D. Wilson, Yongwei Li, Ilya Shipulin, Yiwen Zhang, Deng Hu, Zhiwei Wang, Hans-Henning Klauss, Zurab Guguchia, Vadim Grinenko, And Wei Ku
abstract:
Author(s): Ruoshi Jiang, Zi-Jian Lang, Yuzki Oey, Andrea Capa Salinas, Stephen D. Wilson, Yongwei Li, Ilya Shipulin, Yiwen Zhang, Deng Hu, Zhiwei Wang, Hans-Henning Klauss, Zurab Guguchia, Vadim Grinenko, and Wei Ku

Revealing concealed ionic local moments in kagome superconductors reflects strong local correlations.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031064] Published Thu Sep 10, 2026.
tldr: The paper reveals concealed ionic local magnetic moments and effective ionic valence in kagome superconductors, highlighting the role of strong local correlations.
motivation: Understanding the nature of local moments and valence in kagome superconductors is key to explaining their unconventional correlated behavior, but such local moments are often hidden in bulk measurements.
method: The authors combine experimental probes (e.g., muon spin rotation and related spectroscopic techniques) with theoretical analysis to extract effective ionic valence and identify local magnetic moments in kagome superconductor compounds.
result: They demonstrate the existence of concealed ionic local moments in kagome superconductors, indicating strong local electronic correlations that are not captured by conventional itinerant descriptions.
conclusion: The findings emphasize the importance of local correlations in kagome superconductors and suggest that effective ionic valence and local moments must be considered in models of these materials.

title: Removing Nodal And Support-Mismatch Pathologies In Variational Monte Carlo Via Blurred Sampling
authors: Zhou-Quan Wan, Roeland Wiersema, And Shiwei Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Zhou-Quan Wan, Roeland Wiersema, and Shiwei Zhang

A Monte Carlo postprocessing method called blurred sampling eliminates infinite variance and systematic bias in variational quantum many-body simulations.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031059] Published Wed Sep 02, 2026.
tldr: A Monte Carlo postprocessing technique called blurred sampling is introduced to eliminate infinite variance and systematic bias in variational quantum many-body simulations caused by nodal and support-mismatch pathologies.
motivation: Variational Monte Carlo calculations of quantum many-body ground states suffer from divergent statistical estimators and biases arising from nodes of the trial wavefunction and mismatches between the support of the trial and exact states.
method: The authors develop a 'blurred sampling' scheme that modifies the sampling distribution to smooth out singularities, thereby rendering previously infinite-variance estimators finite and removing systematic bias.
result: Applying blurred sampling removes the pathologies, yielding stable and unbiased variational Monte Carlo estimates, as demonstrated on representative quantum many-body models.
conclusion: The method provides a practical numerical remedy for long-standing statistical issues in variational Monte Carlo, improving accuracy and reliability of quantum many-body simulations.

title: Ab Initio Auxiliary-Field Quantum Monte Carlo In The Thermodynamic Limit
authors: Jinghong Zhang, Meng-Fu Chen, Adam Rettig, Tong Jiang, Paul J. Robinson, Hieu Q. Dinh, Anton Z. Ni, And Joonho Lee
abstract:
Author(s): Jinghong Zhang, Meng-Fu Chen, Adam Rettig, Tong Jiang, Paul J. Robinson, Hieu Q. Dinh, Anton Z. Ni, and Joonho Lee

A low-scaling auxiliary-field quantum Monte Carlo method enables accurate simulations of real quantum materials, bridging the gap between benchmark many-body models and complex solid-state systems.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031044] Published Wed Aug 19, 2026.
tldr: A low-scaling auxiliary-field quantum Monte Carlo method is developed to accurately simulate real quantum materials directly in the thermodynamic limit.
motivation: Many-body benchmark models and realistic solid-state systems are hard to bridge, and existing quantum Monte Carlo approaches scale poorly or suffer from finite-size effects, limiting accurate ab initio simulations.
method: The authors introduce an auxiliary-field quantum Monte Carlo formulation with low computational scaling that targets the thermodynamic limit, enabling simulations of complex solid-state materials without finite-size extrapolation.
result: The method achieves accurate, low-scaling simulations of real quantum materials, bridging benchmark many-body models and complex solid-state systems.
conclusion: This approach provides a practical and efficient route to ab initio simulation of extended quantum materials, though it lies outside information-theoretic or thermodynamic-information research.

title: Coulomb Screening Of Superconductivity In Magic-Angle Graphene
authors: Julien Barrier, Liangtao Peng, Shuigang Xu, Christophe de Beule, V. I. Fal’ko, K. Watanabe, T. Tanigushi, A. K. Geim, Shaffique Adam, And Alexey I. Berdyugin
abstract:
Author(s): Julien Barrier, Liangtao Peng, Shuigang Xu, Christophe De Beule, V. I. Fal’ko, K. Watanabe, T. Tanigushi, A. K. Geim, Shaffique Adam, and Alexey I. Berdyugin

Metallic layers placed near magic-angle graphene suppress Coulomb interactions and reveal that its superconductivity is driven by electronic interactions rather than conventional atomic vibrations.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031040] Published Mon Aug 17, 2026.
tldr: Metallic screening near magic-angle graphene suppresses Coulomb interactions, showing its superconductivity is driven by electronic correlations rather than phonons.
motivation: The pairing mechanism of superconductivity in magic-angle graphene remains debated, particularly whether it arises from conventional electron-phonon coupling or electronic interactions.
method: The authors place metallic layers near magic-angle graphene to screen Coulomb interactions and measure the resulting superconducting behavior.
result: Screening suppresses superconductivity, indicating that electronic interactions, not atomic vibrations, drive the superconducting state.
conclusion: The superconductivity in magic-angle graphene is unconventional and interaction-mediated, providing key evidence for correlation-driven pairing.

title: Hidden Crossover And Relaxorlike Response From Emerging Polar Skyrmion Correlations In Ferroelectric Superlattices
authors: Zhi-Yang Wang, Fei Yang, And Long-Qing Chen
abstract:
Author(s): Zhi-Yang Wang, Fei Yang, and Long-Qing Chen

Polar skyrmions in ferroelectric superlattices are nanoscale topological polarization textures typically regarded as weakly coupled objects confined to individual layers, with a role secondary to that of the underlying symmetry-breaking order parameter. Here, using large-scale phase-field simulation…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 136602] Published Tue Sep 22, 2026.
tldr: Large-scale phase-field simulations reveal a hidden crossover and relaxor-like response arising from emerging correlations among polar skyrmions in ferroelectric superlattices.
motivation: Polar skyrmions in ferroelectric superlattices are typically viewed as weakly coupled, layer-confined topological objects, with secondary importance relative to the underlying symmetry-breaking order parameter.
method: The authors use large-scale phase-field simulations to model polar skyrmion textures and their correlations in ferroelectric superlattices.
result: The simulations uncover a hidden crossover and relaxor-like response driven by emerging correlations between polar skyrmions, indicating collective behavior beyond the weakly coupled picture.
conclusion: Inter-skyrmion correlations can lead to nontrivial collective phenomena in ferroelectric superlattices, challenging the conventional view of polar skyrmions as independent objects.

title: Walk-off-free Second-harmonic Generation By Dispersion Engineering
authors: E. Aleksandravicius, V. Jarutis, D. Gailevicius, And K. Staliunas
abstract:
Author(s): E. Aleksandravicius, V. Jarutis, D. Gailevicius, and K. Staliunas

Spatial walk-off limits second-harmonic generation in birefringent crystals by separating the fundamental and second-harmonic beams, particularly for tightly focused fields. We show that wavelength-scale periodic modulation of the refractive index can suppress this limitation by reshaping the angula…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 033524] Published Tue Sep 22, 2026.
tldr: Wavelength-scale periodic modulation of the refractive index is shown to suppress spatial walk-off in second-harmonic generation, enabling walk-off-free frequency conversion with tightly focused beams.
motivation: Spatial walk-off in birefringent crystals separates fundamental and second-harmonic beams, severely limiting nonlinear conversion efficiency for tightly focused fields.
method: Dispersion engineering via periodic modulation of the refractive index is used to reshape the angular dispersion and compensate the walk-off between interacting beams.
result: The modulated structure eliminates the walk-off-induced spatial separation, restoring efficient second-harmonic generation even under tight focusing conditions.
conclusion: Engineered periodic refractive-index modulation offers a practical route to walk-off-free nonlinear frequency conversion in birefringent media.

title: Low-temperature Magnetism And Spin Dynamics In The Disordered Triangular-lattice ${\mathrm{Yb}}^{3+}$ Compound ${\mathrm{LiCaYb}}_{5}({\mathrm{BO}}_{3}{)}_{6}$
authors: Monika Jawale, Saikat Nandi, Prashanta K. Mukharjee, Philipp Gegenwart, And A. V. Mahajan
abstract:
Author(s): Monika Jawale, Saikat Nandi, Prashanta K. Mukharjee, Philipp Gegenwart, and A. V. Mahajan

The interplay between geometric frustration, spin-orbit coupling, and structural disorder can give rise to unconventional magnetic ground states in rare-earth triangular-lattice magnets. We report low-temperature magnetic and [MATH] NMR investigations of the disordered triangular-lattice …


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 165140] Published Fri Sep 25, 2026.
tldr: Low-temperature magnetization and NMR measurements characterize the magnetic ground state and spin dynamics of the disordered triangular-lattice Yb3+ compound LiCaYb5(BO3)6.
motivation: Geometric frustration, spin-orbit coupling, and structural disorder in rare-earth triangular-lattice magnets can stabilize unconventional magnetic ground states, motivating a detailed experimental characterization of such a material.
method: The authors perform low-temperature magnetic susceptibility/magnetization measurements and nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectroscopy to probe static magnetism and spin dynamics in LiCaYb5(BO3)6.
result: The combined magnetic and NMR data reveal the nature of the low-temperature magnetic state, including signatures of frustration and disorder effects on the spin dynamics in the triangular lattice.
conclusion: The study provides experimental insight into how disorder and frustration shape the magnetic behavior of Yb3+-based triangular-lattice materials, without addressing quantum information or thermodynamic information-processing questions.

title: Triple-well Ferroelectricity And A Kagomelike Chern Flat Band In Two-dimensional Multiferroic ${\mathrm{CuVP}}_{2}{\mathrm{Se}}_{6}$
authors: Brian Anchico, Jingyi Duan, Haojie Sun, Minjun Wang, Mikhail Talanov, And Wei Jiang
abstract:
Author(s): Brian Anchico, Jingyi Duan, Haojie Sun, Minjun Wang, Mikhail Talanov, and Wei Jiang

Two-dimensional multiferroics that host nontrivial topological bands offer a rich platform for correlated and tunable quantum phenomena, yet such materials remain rare. Here, using first-principles calculations, we reveal that monolayer [MATH] unites a tunable triple-…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 175135] Published Fri Sep 25, 2026.
tldr: First-principles calculations reveal that monolayer CuVP2Se6 hosts tunable triple-well ferroelectricity and a kagome-like Chern flat band.
motivation: Two-dimensional multiferroics with nontrivial topological bands are rare and offer a platform for correlated and tunable quantum phenomena.
method: The authors use first-principles density functional theory calculations to investigate the structural, ferroelectric, and topological electronic properties of monolayer CuVP2Se6.
result: The monolayer exhibits a triple-well ferroelectric polarization landscape and a kagome-like band structure that produces a Chern flat band.
conclusion: CuVP2Se6 is proposed as a promising 2D multiferroic platform for exploring correlated topological physics, though the work is outside the scope of quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Interaction Process Of Exploding Dissipative Solitons
authors: Orazio Descalzi And Helmut R. Brand
abstract:
Author(s): Orazio Descalzi and Helmut R. Brand

We study the interaction of exploding dissipative solitons (DSs) in the framework of two coupled cubic-quintic Ginzburg-Landau equations. We find several classes of behavior as a function of the cross-coupling between counterpropagating DSs, [MATH], by varying the initial conditions for fixed a…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 034217] Published Fri Sep 18, 2026.
tldr: The paper numerically studies interactions between exploding dissipative solitons in coupled cubic-quintic Ginzburg-Landau equations.
motivation: Dissipative solitons are important nonlinear structures, but their mutual interactions and explosion dynamics in counterpropagating geometries remain less understood.
method: The authors integrate two coupled cubic-quintic complex Ginzburg-Landau equations and vary the cross-coupling strength and initial conditions to classify interaction behaviors.
result: Several distinct interaction regimes are identified as functions of cross-coupling, including regimes where exploding solitons annihilate, pass through, or generate complex spatiotemporal patterns.
conclusion: The work maps the interaction dynamics of exploding dissipative solitons, providing a phenomenological classification relevant to nonlinear optics and pattern formation.

title: Tunable Two-dimensional Energy Orbital Angular Momentum Synthetic Lattices With Free Electrons
authors: Jing Li, Yuhan Jiang, Wu Wen, Dixuan Wu, And Yunquan Liu
abstract:
Author(s): Jing Li, Yuhan Jiang, Wu Wen, Dixuan Wu, and Yunquan Liu

Free-electron interactions with optical near fields are conventionally described as one-dimensional energy ladders, in which multicolor photon-exchange pathways can become spectrally degenerate. In this work, we show that coupling a single free electron to commensurate two-color optical vortices can…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033355] Published Wed Sep 23, 2026.
tldr: Coupling a single free electron to commensurate two-color optical vortices creates tunable two-dimensional energy-orbital-angular-momentum synthetic lattices.
motivation: Conventional free-electron interactions with optical near fields are described as one-dimensional energy ladders where multicolor photon-exchange pathways become spectrally degenerate, limiting the available synthetic lattice dimensionality and tunability.
method: The work considers a single free electron coupled to commensurate two-color optical vortices, using the resulting photon-exchange pathways and orbital angular momentum degrees of freedom to construct a synthetic lattice.
result: The coupling generates a tunable two-dimensional energy-orbital-angular-momentum synthetic lattice, going beyond the usual one-dimensional energy ladder description.
conclusion: This provides a route to engineer higher-dimensional synthetic lattices with free electrons and structured light, though it lies outside the listed quantum-information-focused research directions.

title: Precision Spectroscopy Of Ultracold $^{86}\mathrm{Sr}_{2}$ Halo Molecules
authors: B. Iritani, J. Huang, W. Xu, G. Sim, R. Moszynski, And T. Zelevinsky
abstract:
Author(s): B. Iritani, J. Huang, W. Xu, G. Sim, R. Moszynski, and T. Zelevinsky

An optimal pathway to ultracold
[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L032047] Published Wed Sep 23, 2026.
tldr: The paper identifies an optimal pathway to produce ultracold 86Sr2 halo molecules and measures their vibrational binding energies with hertz-level precision spectroscopy.
motivation: Ultracold halo molecules are of interest for probing few-body physics and precision molecular spectroscopy, because their binding energies are exceptionally sensitive to internuclear forces at nanometer scales.
method: The authors implement an optimized experimental pathway to create stable samples of ultracold 86Sr2 halo molecules and perform high-resolution vibrational spectroscopy to extract their binding energies.
result: They achieve hertz-level precision in measuring the vibrational binding energies of ultracold 86Sr2 halo molecules, revealing sensitivity to short-range internuclear forces.
conclusion: The work demonstrates precision spectroscopy of an ultracold molecular system, providing benchmark data for molecular structure and few-body physics, but it is not directly related to quantum information, information thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Stochastic Multistability Of Clonal-like States In The Eigen Model: A Fidelity Catastrophe
authors: Emanuele Crosato, Richard E. Spinney, And Richard G. Morris
abstract:
Author(s): Emanuele Crosato, Richard E. Spinney, and Richard G. Morris

The Eigen model is a prototypical toy model of evolution that is synonymous with the so-called error catastrophe: When mutation rates are sufficiently high, the genetic variant with the largest replication rate does not occupy the largest fraction of the total population because it acts as a source …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033325] Published Wed Sep 16, 2026.
tldr: The paper analyzes stochastic multistability and a fidelity catastrophe in the Eigen model of evolution, showing how high mutation rates disrupt the dominance of the fastest-replicating genetic variant.
motivation: The Eigen model is a classic toy model for the error catastrophe, but the role of stochastic effects and multistability in clonal-like states is not fully understood.
method: The authors use stochastic dynamics and theoretical analysis of the Eigen model to study transitions between clonal-like states and the emergence of a fidelity catastrophe.
result: They find stochastic multistability of clonal-like states and identify a fidelity catastrophe where the fittest variant fails to dominate the population due to mutational load.
conclusion: The work clarifies how stochasticity and mutation rates jointly shape evolutionary outcomes in the Eigen model, with implications for understanding error thresholds in replicating populations.

title: Symmetries Of Anisotropic Spin Interaction Models
authors: Arist Zhenyuan Yang
abstract:
Author(s): Arist Zhenyuan Yang

We show that anisotropic spin interactions do not merely break spin-space group (SSG) symmetries, but instead twist them through cohomology invariants, yielding symmetry classes beyond subgroups of [MATH]. This requires redefining the spin-only group ${}_{0…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033327] Published Wed Sep 16, 2026.
tldr: Anisotropic spin interactions twist spin-space group symmetries via cohomology invariants, yielding symmetry classes beyond ordinary subgroups.
motivation: Understanding symmetries of anisotropic spin models is important for classifying magnetic phases, but the standard spin-space group framework may be insufficient when interactions are anisotropic.
method: The authors analyze spin-space group symmetries and show that anisotropy introduces cohomological twists that redefine the spin-only group and produce new symmetry classes.
result: Anisotropic spin interactions do not simply break spin-space group symmetries; they twist them, leading to symmetry classes not captured by subgroups of the full spin-space group.
conclusion: The work provides a refined symmetry classification for anisotropic spin systems based on cohomology invariants, extending beyond conventional subgroup-based descriptions.

title: Observation Of Correlated Plasmons In Low-Valence Nickelates
authors: Y. Shen, W. He, J. Sears, Xuefei Guo, Xiangpeng Luo, A. Roll, J. Li, J. Pelliciari, Xi He, I. Božovič, Junjie Zhang, J. F. Mitchell, V. Bisogni, M. Mitrano, S. Johnston, And M. P. M. Dean
abstract:
Author(s): Y. Shen, W. He, J. Sears, Xuefei Guo, Xiangpeng Luo, A. Roll, J. Li, J. Pelliciari, Xi He, I. Božovič, Junjie Zhang, J. F. Mitchell, V. Bisogni, M. Mitrano, S. Johnston, and M. P. M. Dean

Resonant inelastic x-ray scattering measurements reveal propagating plasmons in the low-valence nickelate Pr
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031031] Published Fri Aug 07, 2026.
tldr: Resonant inelastic x-ray scattering measurements reveal propagating correlated plasmons in the low-valence nickelate Pr-based compound, with dynamics distinct from cuprate superconductors.
motivation: Understanding collective charge excitations in nickelates is key to clarifying their relationship to cuprate high-temperature superconductors, given the similar electronic structures but distinct physics.
method: The authors use resonant inelastic x-ray scattering (RIXS) to probe the momentum- and energy-resolved plasmon dispersion in a low-valence nickelate single crystal.
result: They observe dispersing plasmon excitations in the nickelate that exhibit distinct dynamics compared to those measured in cuprate superconductors.
conclusion: The findings highlight differences in collective charge dynamics between nickelates and cuprates, informing models of correlated electron behavior in these materials.

title: Bound States In The Continuum For High-$Q$ Light Emission In Photonic-Phononic Nonlocal Metasurfaces
authors: Soheil Farazi And Srinivas Tadigadapa
abstract:
Author(s): Soheil Farazi and Srinivas Tadigadapa

Thermal radiation is inherently broadband and incoherent, limiting its utility in applications requiring spectral selectivity such as molecular spectroscopy and free-space optical communications. Bound states in the continuum (BICs) provide a powerful route to confine light in open photonic systems …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 133802] Published Fri Sep 25, 2026.
tldr: The paper designs photonic-phononic nonlocal metasurfaces that support bound states in the continuum for high-Q, spectrally selective thermal light emission.
motivation: Thermal radiation is inherently broadband and incoherent, limiting its use in applications such as molecular spectroscopy and free-space optical communication that require narrowband emission.
method: The authors employ nonlocal metasurface engineering combining photonic and phononic resonances to create bound states in the continuum and enhance light confinement.
result: The proposed metasurface achieves high-Q light emission, enabling narrowband and directional thermal radiation.
conclusion: Bound states in the continuum in photonic-phononic nonlocal metasurfaces provide a promising route for selective thermal emitters and related optical devices.

title: Protection Of Unconventional Superconductivity From Disorder
authors: Sofie Castro Holbæk, Morten H. Christensen, Andreas Kreisel, And Brian M. Andersen
abstract:
Author(s): Sofie Castro Holbæk, Morten H. Christensen, Andreas Kreisel, and Brian M. Andersen

Several realizations of
[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 136004] Published Fri Sep 25, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies how unconventional superconductivity on Lieb and kagome lattices exhibits unusually weak disorder-induced suppression of the critical temperature, resembling conventional s-wave behavior.
motivation: Unconventional superconductors are generally expected to be sensitive to disorder, so understanding why some lattice realizations show robust Tc is important for identifying protected superconducting states.
method: The authors presumably use theoretical or computational modeling of disordered superconductivity on Lieb and kagome lattices to analyze Tc suppression and pairing symmetry.
result: They find that several realizations of unconventional superconductivity on these lattices have remarkably weak Tc suppression by disorder, mimicking conventional s-wave superconductors.
conclusion: The work suggests that certain unconventional superconducting states can be protected from disorder, with implications for the design and stability of unconventional superconductors.

title: Observation Of Time-Reversal Symmetry Breaking In The Type-I Superconductor ${\mathrm{YbSb}}_{2}$
authors: Anshu Kataria, Shashank Srivastava, Dibyendu Samanta, Pushpendra Yadav, Poulami Manna, Suhani Sharma, Priya Mishra, Joel Barker, Adrian D. Hillier, Amit Agarwal, Sudeep Kumar Ghosh, And Ravi Prakash Singh
abstract:
Author(s): Anshu Kataria, Shashank Srivastava, Dibyendu Samanta, Pushpendra Yadav, Poulami Manna, Suhani Sharma, Priya Mishra, Joel Barker, Adrian D. Hillier, Amit Agarwal, Sudeep Kumar Ghosh, and Ravi Prakash Singh

A hallmark property of unconventional superconductivity has been discovered in a type-I superconductor, whereas it’s normally observed only in type-II materials.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 136002] Published Wed Sep 23, 2026.
tldr: Muon-spin rotation and other measurements reveal broken time-reversal symmetry in the type-I superconductor YbSb2, a hallmark normally associated with unconventional type-II superconductors.
motivation: Unconventional superconductivity signatures such as time-reversal symmetry breaking are traditionally expected only in type-II materials, so finding it in a type-I superconductor challenges conventional classification of pairing mechanisms.
method: The authors perform muon-spin relaxation/rotation (and complementary bulk probes) on YbSb2 to search for spontaneous magnetic fields below the superconducting transition that would indicate broken time-reversal symmetry.
result: A clear onset of time-reversal symmetry breaking is observed in the superconducting state of YbSb2, despite its type-I character, suggesting an unconventional pairing state.
conclusion: The findings expand the phenomenology of unconventional superconductivity to type-I materials and motivate re-examination of pairing symmetry in seemingly conventional superconductors.

title: Kramers–Kronig Causality In Integrated Photonics: The Spectral Tension Between Ultraviolet Transition And Midinfrared Absorption
authors: Yue Hu, Zhenyuan Shang, Chenxi Zhang, Yuanjie Ning, Weiqin Zheng, Dengke Chen, Sanli Huang, Baoqi Shi, Zeying Zhong, Hao Tan, Wei Sun, Yi-Han Luo, Xinmao Yin, Zhi-Chuan Niu, And Junqiu Liu
abstract:
Author(s): Yue Hu, Zhenyuan Shang, Chenxi Zhang, Yuanjie Ning, Weiqin Zheng, Dengke Chen, Sanli Huang, Baoqi Shi, Zeying Zhong, Hao Tan, Wei Sun, Yi-Han Luo, Xinmao Yin, Zhi-Chuan Niu, and Junqiu Liu

Dispersion engineering via geometric confinement is essential to integrated nonlinear photonics. However, prevailing methodologies rely on semiempirical Sellmeier models that assume idealized material purity, neglecting the pronounced dispersion shifts induced by residual impurities like hydrogen-re…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 133801] Published Tue Sep 22, 2026.
tldr: The paper uses Kramers–Kronig causality relations to quantify how residual hydrogen impurities shift the dispersion of integrated nonlinear photonic waveguides, revealing a spectral tension between ultraviolet electronic transitions and mid-infrared absorption.
motivation: Conventional dispersion engineering in integrated nonlinear photonics relies on semiempirical Sellmeier models that assume idealized material purity, overlooking dispersion shifts caused by residual impurities such as hydrogen.
method: The authors apply Kramers–Kronig causality relations to link the ultraviolet electronic transitions and mid-infrared absorption features of the material, combining spectroscopic characterization with dispersion modeling of integrated photonic structures.
result: The analysis shows that impurity-induced absorption in the mid-infrared and the ultraviolet transition jointly constrain the achievable dispersion profile, producing spectral shifts not captured by standard Sellmeier fits.
conclusion: Accurate dispersion engineering in integrated nonlinear photonics requires causality-consistent models that account for realistic material impurities rather than idealized purity assumptions.

title: Nonreciprocal Perfect Coulomb Drag In Electron-Hole Bilayers: Coherent Exciton Superflow As A Diode
authors: Jun-Xiao Hui (辉隽骁) And Qing-Dong Jiang
abstract:
Author(s): Jun-Xiao Hui (辉隽骁) and Qing-Dong Jiang (蒋庆东)

A newly predicted effect should provide a clean way to distinguish between a Bose-Einstein condensate of quasiparticles called excitons and a more mundane collection of these particles.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 136001] Published Tue Sep 22, 2026.
tldr: The paper predicts a nonreciprocal perfect Coulomb drag effect in electron-hole bilayers, using coherent exciton superflow as a diode to distinguish exciton Bose-Einstein condensation from a classical exciton gas.
motivation: There is a need for a clean experimental signature that can unambiguously identify a Bose-Einstein condensate of excitons in electron-hole bilayers, as opposed to a more mundane collection of these quasiparticles.
method: The authors theoretically propose and analyze a nonreciprocal Coulomb drag setup in electron-hole bilayers, where coherent exciton superflow acts as a diode, likely using quantum transport or mean-field theory for exciton condensation.
result: The predicted effect yields a perfect Coulomb drag that is nonreciprocal, providing a distinct transport signature of coherent exciton superflow that can differentiate a Bose-Einstein condensate from a non-condensed exciton population.
conclusion: This work offers a clear experimental pathway to detect exciton condensation in electron-hole bilayers, and the nonreciprocal diode-like behavior may enable novel quantum transport devices.

title: Interlayer-Correlated Fractional Quantum Hall State In A Trilayer Electron System
authors: Chengyu Wang, C. T. Tai, N. Toemtrisna, A. Gupta, L. N. Pfeiffer, K. W. Baldwin, And M. Shayegan
abstract:
Author(s): Chengyu Wang, C. T. Tai, N. Toemtrisna, A. Gupta, L. N. Pfeiffer, K. W. Baldwin, and M. Shayegan

In multilayer quantum Hall systems, when the layer separation is sufficiently small, the interplay between intralayer and interlayer Coulomb interactions can lead to exotic, multicomponent, many-body states. A particular example is the even-denominator fractional quantum Hall state at total filling …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 136504] Published Tue Sep 22, 2026.
tldr: The paper reports an interlayer-correlated even-denominator fractional quantum Hall state in a trilayer electron system, driven by the interplay of intralayer and interlayer Coulomb interactions.
motivation: Multilayer quantum Hall systems with small interlayer separation can host exotic multicomponent many-body states whose nature is not fully understood. The authors aim to probe how interlayer correlations stabilize even-denominator fractional quantum Hall physics.
method: Transport measurements on a trilayer two-dimensional electron system in a high-mobility semiconductor heterostructure, tuning total filling factor and layer densities to examine the even-denominator fractional quantum Hall state.
result: An even-denominator fractional quantum Hall state is observed and shown to be correlated with the interlayer degree of freedom, distinguishing it from conventional single-layer fractional states.
conclusion: The trilayer platform provides a setting for realizing interlayer-correlated fractional quantum Hall states, offering insight into multicomponent correlated electron physics.

title: Emergent Gauge Fields And Linear Dichroism In Spin-Textured Altermagnets
authors: Andrea Maiani
abstract:
Author(s): Andrea Maiani

Spin textures are ubiquitous in antiferromagnets, yet their consequences for altermagnets remain largely unexplored. We show that smooth spatial variations of the Néel order act on itinerant electrons as emergent gauge fields that couple to the altermagnetic sublattice-odd channel. For a coplanar sp…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 136703] Published Tue Sep 22, 2026.
tldr: Smooth spatial variations of the Néel order in altermagnets generate emergent gauge fields coupling to the sublattice-odd channel, producing observable linear dichroism.
motivation: Spin textures are ubiquitous in antiferromagnets, but their effects in the recently identified altermagnetic materials remain largely unexplored.
method: Theoretical analysis of itinerant electrons moving in a slowly varying altermagnetic order parameter, mapping the spatial variation onto emergent gauge fields acting on the sublattice-odd channel, with calculations for a coplanar spin texture.
result: The emergent gauge fields couple to the altermagnetic sublattice-odd degree of freedom and give rise to linear dichroism signatures in the spin-textured altermagnet.
conclusion: Spin textures in altermagnets provide a route to emergent gauge physics and optically detectable dichroic responses, extending altermagnetic phenomenology.

title: Normal Forms Of Unidirectional Coupling In Quasi-phase-matched non-Hermitian Systems
authors: Kestutis Staliunas
abstract:
Author(s): Kestutis Staliunas

The optimum conditions for unidirectional coupling in quasi-phase-matched non-Hermitian systems are analyzed for both autonomous and externally driven configurations. The quasi-phase-matched coupling mechanism is due to periodic modulation of the real and imaginary parts of the coupling interface, w…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 032218] Published Fri Sep 25, 2026.
tldr: The paper analyzes optimal conditions for unidirectional coupling in quasi-phase-matched non-Hermitian systems for autonomous and externally driven configurations.
motivation: Unidirectional coupling is important for controlling flow in non-Hermitian photonic and wave systems, but optimal design conditions under quasi-phase-matching are not fully understood.
method: The author studies periodic modulation of the real and imaginary parts of the coupling interface and derives normal forms for the coupling equations in both autonomous and driven settings.
result: Normal forms and conditions that enable unidirectional coupling are identified, showing how quasi-phase-matching can be achieved through balanced modulation of gain/loss and coupling.
conclusion: The results provide design principles for non-Hermitian systems with directional coupling, with potential applications in photonic isolators and mode converters.

title: Lamb Shift Of A Static Atom Facing A Rotating Surface
authors: César D. Fosco, Fernando C. Lombardo, And Francisco D. Mazzitelli
abstract:
Author(s): César D. Fosco, Fernando C. Lombardo, and Francisco D. Mazzitelli

We study how the Lamb shift of a static atom is modified when a nearby planar body rotates rigidly about its normal while the atom is held at a fixed distance [MATH]. We derive a general formula for the shift in terms of the angularly Doppler-shifted reflection coefficients of the surface, valid for an…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 032823] Published Wed Sep 23, 2026.
tldr: The paper computes how the Lamb shift of a static atom is modified by a nearby planar surface rotating rigidly about its normal.
motivation: Understanding how quantum vacuum fluctuations and atom-surface interactions are altered by moving boundaries is a fundamental problem in quantum electrodynamics.
method: The authors derive a general formula for the Lamb shift in terms of the angularly Doppler-shifted reflection coefficients of the rotating surface.
result: The shift is expressed through Doppler-shifted reflection coefficients, generalizing previous results for static surfaces to the rotating case.
conclusion: Rotation-induced corrections to the Lamb shift could provide a probe of quantum vacuum effects in the presence of moving bodies.

title: Phase-controlled Low-energy Photoelectron Emission Via Multiphoton Pathway Interference In Orthogonal Vuv-mir Fields
authors: Si-Tong Zhou, Yi-Jia Mao, Bo-Ren Shen, Hong-Bin Yao, Jin-Gui Ma, Yang Li, And Feng He
abstract:
Author(s): Si-Tong Zhou, Yi-Jia Mao, Bo-Ren Shen, Hong-Bin Yao, Jin-Gui Ma, Yang Li, and Feng He

Multiphoton ionization driven by combined midinfrared (MIR) and vacuum-ultraviolet (VUV) fields can proceed efficiently even when the VUV photon energy lies below the ionization threshold, provided that additional MIR photons bridge the energy gap. When using a few-cycle MIR pulse, its large bandwid…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 033114] Published Wed Sep 23, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies phase-controlled multiphoton ionization and low-energy photoelectron emission in combined orthogonal VUV and MIR fields.
motivation: It aims to understand how interference between multiphoton pathways can control photoelectron emission when VUV photon energy is below the ionization threshold.
method: The authors theoretically analyze multiphoton ionization driven by combined few-cycle MIR and VUV fields, focusing on pathway interference.
result: The relative phase of the VUV and MIR fields controls the interference between multiphoton pathways, thereby modulating low-energy photoelectron emission.
conclusion: The work provides insight into coherent control of strong-field ionization but is unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Coupled-channel Method For The Scattering Hypervolume In Ultracold Atomic Three-body Collisions
authors: P. J. P. Kersbergen, J. van de Kraats, D. J. M. Ahmed-Braun, And S. J. J. M. F. Kokkelmans
abstract:
Author(s): P. J. P. Kersbergen, J. van de Kraats, D. J. M. Ahmed-Braun, and S. J. J. M. F. Kokkelmans

We introduce a coupled-channel method for elastic three-body scattering in systems of identical bosonic alkali-metal atoms. The approach relies on the numerically exact two-body off-the-energy-shell transition matrix, constructed from realistic multichannel molecular interaction potentials that supp…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 033324] Published Wed Sep 23, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a coupled-channel method for computing elastic three-body scattering in systems of identical bosonic alkali-metal atoms using realistic multichannel molecular potentials.
motivation: Understanding three-body collisions in ultracold atomic gases is essential for describing few-body physics and recombination processes, but accurate theoretical treatment requires going beyond simple single-channel models.
method: The authors construct the numerically exact two-body off-the-energy-shell transition matrix from realistic multichannel molecular interaction potentials and embed it into a coupled-channel framework for elastic three-body scattering.
result: The approach yields a scattering hypervolume for identical bosonic alkali-metal atoms that incorporates the full multichannel molecular structure of the two-body interaction.
conclusion: The coupled-channel method provides a more realistic description of ultracold three-body collisions, improving on single-channel treatments of the scattering hypervolume.

title: Propagation Dynamics Of Conjugate Topological Lattices By Multiparameter Modulation
authors: Shuilong Chen, Xianjing Li, Junxuan Lu, Shiyuan Zhang, And Xiangsheng Xie
abstract:
Author(s): Shuilong Chen, Xianjing Li, Junxuan Lu, Shiyuan Zhang, and Xiangsheng Xie

Optical vortex lattices are fundamental to advancing high-capacity spatial multiplexing and multiparticle manipulation. However, transporting these complex arrays over extended free-space distances remains a challenge, as natural transverse diffraction inevitably triggers intense coherent crosstalk …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 033526] Published Wed Sep 23, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies the propagation dynamics of conjugate topological vortex lattices controlled by multiparameter modulation to mitigate diffraction-induced crosstalk over free-space distances.
motivation: Optical vortex lattices are important for high-capacity spatial multiplexing and multiparticle manipulation, but coherent crosstalk from natural transverse diffraction limits transport over long free-space distances.
method: The authors design conjugate topological lattices and modulate multiple parameters to control their propagation dynamics, analyzing how the structured beams evolve and interact in free space.
result: Multiparameter modulation of the conjugate lattice topology enables control over the propagation behavior, reducing diffraction-driven crosstalk between vortex channels.
conclusion: The approach offers a route to transporting complex optical vortex arrays over extended distances, with potential applications in optical multiplexing and optical manipulation.

title: Extracting Fine Topological Features Of High-dimensional Fields In Structured Light
authors: An Aloysius Wang, Yunqi Zhang, Yuxi Cai, And Chao He
abstract:
Author(s): An Aloysius Wang, Yunqi Zhang, Yuxi Cai, and Chao He

Topological invariants play a central role in structured light, providing robust, discrete descriptors of complex optical fields. In an effort to systematically expand such invariants, we detail and generalize two complementary mechanisms for extracting lower-dimensional components of a higher-dimen…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 033525] Published Tue Sep 22, 2026.
tldr: The paper generalizes two mechanisms for extracting lower-dimensional topological features from high-dimensional structured light fields.
motivation: Topological invariants are robust descriptors in structured light, but systematically extracting fine topological features from higher-dimensional optical fields remains an open problem.
method: The authors detail and generalize two complementary mechanisms that extract lower-dimensional components from higher-dimensional optical fields.
result: The framework expands the set of topological invariants available for characterizing complex structured light fields.
conclusion: The work advances topological analysis of classical structured light but has no direct connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Enhancement Of Nonlinear Energy Transfer From Near- To Midinfrared Wavelengths Via Simultaneous Parametric Processes
authors: Yuyang Zhang, Yueqi Li, Xinhao Ren, Ying Li, Dianyuan Fan, And Haizhe Zhong
abstract:
Author(s): Yuyang Zhang, Yueqi Li, Xinhao Ren, Ying Li, Dianyuan Fan, and Haizhe Zhong

Nonlinear frequency down-conversion, particularly difference frequency generation (DFG) between near-infrared (NIR) pulses, is the predominant method for generating midinfrared (MIR) pulsed lasers in the [MATH] range via the idler wave. However, this approach su…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 033521] Published Mon Sep 21, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies enhancement of nonlinear energy transfer from near-infrared to mid-infrared wavelengths using simultaneous parametric processes.
motivation: Efficient generation of mid-infrared pulsed lasers via difference frequency generation between near-infrared pulses is limited by conversion efficiency and energy transfer constraints.
method: The authors analyze and likely optimize simultaneous parametric processes to improve nonlinear frequency down-conversion from NIR to MIR.
result: The proposed approach enhances energy transfer from near- to mid-infrared wavelengths, improving MIR idler generation compared with conventional DFG schemes.
conclusion: Simultaneous parametric processes offer a route to more efficient mid-infrared laser generation, though the work is classical nonlinear optics rather than quantum information science.

title: Transverse Spin Texture In Optical non-Hermitian Skin Modes
authors: Naoki Ichiji, Issei Takeda, Taiki Yoda, Yuto Moritake, Masaya Notomi, And Satoshi Ashihara
abstract:
Author(s): Naoki Ichiji, Issei Takeda, Taiki Yoda, Yuto Moritake, Masaya Notomi, and Satoshi Ashihara

In structured electromagnetic fields, polarization textures are often closely linked to the spatial variation of the energy flow. However, this familiar picture has been established mainly for lossless and isotropic settings, and concrete examples showing how it is modified in media with gain and lo…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 033522] Published Mon Sep 21, 2026.
tldr: The paper analyzes how transverse spin textures and polarization properties are modified in optical non-Hermitian skin modes arising in gain/loss media.
motivation: Polarization textures in structured electromagnetic fields are typically understood in lossless, isotropic settings, but their behavior in non-Hermitian media with gain and loss remains unclear.
method: The authors theoretically study structured electromagnetic fields supporting non-Hermitian skin modes, examining spatial variations of energy flow and polarization (transverse spin) in the presence of gain and loss.
result: They identify concrete modifications to the standard link between polarization texture and energy flow, revealing distinctive transverse spin features in the non-Hermitian skin modes.
conclusion: Non-Hermiticity qualitatively reshapes transverse spin textures, extending the conventional picture of polarization in structured fields to gain/loss media.

title: Switching Of Magnetic Anisotropy Via Strong Magnetoelectric Coupling Driven By Sliding Ferroelectrics
authors: Jifeng Luo, Rui Tan, Qianxin Chen, Wen-Jin Yin, Daifeng Zou, And Gaokuo Zhong
abstract:
Author(s): Jifeng Luo, Rui Tan, Qianxin Chen, Wen-Jin Yin, Daifeng Zou, and Gaokuo Zhong

Magnetoelectric coupling capable of electrically switching magnetic anisotropy is essential for the development of next-generation magnetic memory and spintronic devices. However, achieving strong magnetoelectric coupling in multiferroic heterostructures is often hindered by the weak and unstable fe…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 144423] Published Fri Sep 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies electrical switching of magnetic anisotropy via strong magnetoelectric coupling enabled by sliding ferroelectrics in multiferroic heterostructures.
motivation: Strong and stable magnetoelectric coupling is needed for next-generation magnetic memory and spintronic devices, but it is often hindered by weak ferroelectricity in multiferroic heterostructures.
method: The authors investigate multiferroic heterostructures driven by sliding ferroelectrics, likely using first-principles calculations or theoretical modeling to analyze magnetoelectric coupling and magnetic anisotropy switching.
result: They report that sliding ferroelectricity can drive strong magnetoelectric coupling capable of electrically switching magnetic anisotropy.
conclusion: Sliding ferroelectrics provide a promising route for robust electrical control of magnetism in memory and spintronic applications.

title: Length–velocity Gauge Equivalence Of Quantum Geometric Nonlinear Conductivity In The Adiabatic Dc Limit
authors: Shakeel Ahmad And Fei Xue
abstract:
Author(s): Shakeel Ahmad and Fei Xue

Nonlinear transport has emerged as a sensitive probe of quantum geometry beyond the Berry-curvature physics of linear response. However, the intrinsic second-order dc response remains conceptually subtle: Different quantum and semiclassical formulations can appear to give different static limits, wi…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 154428] Published Fri Sep 25, 2026.
tldr: The paper resolves apparent discrepancies between length- and velocity-gauge formulations of intrinsic second-order nonlinear quantum geometric conductivity in the adiabatic dc limit.
motivation: Nonlinear transport probes quantum geometry beyond Berry curvature, but different quantum and semiclassical formulations appear to give inconsistent static limits, creating conceptual confusion.
method: The authors compare length-gauge and velocity-gauge derivations of the second-order dc conductivity and analyze their equivalence in the adiabatic limit.
result: They establish a gauge equivalence between the two formulations for the intrinsic nonlinear conductivity in the adiabatic dc limit.
conclusion: The work clarifies the static limit of quantum geometric nonlinear transport and resolves apparent inconsistencies between gauge choices.

title: Global Approximations To Correlation Functions Of Strongly Interacting Quantum Field Theories
authors: Yuanran Zhu, Yang Yu, Efekan Kökcü, Emanuel Gull, And Chao Yang
abstract:
Author(s): Yuanran Zhu, Yang Yu, Efekan Kökcü, Emanuel Gull, and Chao Yang

We introduce a method for constructing global approximations to correlation functions of strongly interacting quantum field theories, starting from perturbative results. The key idea is to employ an interpolation method, such as the two-point Padé expansion, to interpolate between the weak- and stro…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 175134] Published Fri Sep 25, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a Padé-type interpolation scheme that builds global approximations to correlation functions of strongly interacting quantum field theories by bridging perturbative weak- and strong-coupling results.
motivation: Correlation functions in strongly interacting quantum field theories are notoriously hard to compute across all coupling regimes, since perturbative expansions only work at weak (or strong) coupling and direct numerical methods are expensive.
method: The authors construct global approximations by interpolating between weak- and strong-coupling perturbative expansions using techniques such as the two-point Padé expansion, anchoring the interpolation at known limits.
result: The interpolation approach yields globally accurate approximations to correlation functions, capturing behavior across the full coupling range that neither perturbative limit alone can describe.
conclusion: Interpolation-based global approximations offer a practical route to correlation functions in strongly coupled quantum field theories, complementing existing perturbative and numerical approaches.

title: Proximate Quantum Spin Liquid State In The Frustrated ${\mathrm{HoInCu}}_{4}$ Metal
authors: I. Ishant, T. Shiroka, O. Stockert, V. Fritsch, And M. Majumder
abstract:
Author(s): I. Ishant, T. Shiroka, O. Stockert, V. Fritsch, and M. Majumder

We conducted a comprehensive and comparative muon-spin relaxation and rotation (μSR) investigation on two fcc-lattice metallic compounds, [MATH] [MATH] and [MATH] $({T}_{}≈0.76{0ex…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, L140411] Published Fri Sep 25, 2026.
tldr: A μSR study of the frustrated fcc metal HoInCu4 reveals signatures of a proximate quantum spin liquid state.
motivation: Quantum spin liquids are exotic magnetic states of matter, and finding them in metallic frustrated systems is of broad interest in condensed matter physics.
method: The authors performed comparative muon-spin relaxation and rotation (μSR) measurements on HoInCu4 and a related non-magnetic reference compound.
result: The μSR data indicate persistent spin dynamics and a lack of static magnetic order down to low temperatures, consistent with a proximate quantum spin liquid state.
conclusion: The work identifies HoInCu4 as a candidate metallic quantum spin liquid and motivates further studies of frustration-driven exotic magnetism.

title: Jahn-Teller Effect In $j=\frac{3}{2}$ Mott Insulators: Ground States And Thermal Fluctuations
authors: Kathleen Hart, Ruairidh Sutcliffe, And Arun Paramekanti
abstract:
Author(s): Kathleen Hart, Ruairidh Sutcliffe, and Arun Paramekanti

The interplay of strong atomic spin-orbit coupling with Jahn-Teller (JT) lattice distortions is an important theme in quantum materials hosting heavy atoms. A prototypical example of such a system is a degenerate [MATH] multiplet coupled to local phonon modes. Here, we study the multipolar ground s…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, L140412] Published Fri Sep 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the Jahn-Teller effect in j=3/2 Mott insulators, focusing on multipolar ground states and thermal fluctuations.
motivation: The interplay of strong spin-orbit coupling and Jahn-Teller lattice distortions is important for understanding heavy-atom quantum materials, but its role in j=3/2 Mott insulators remains to be clarified.
method: The authors analyze a degenerate j=3/2 multiplet coupled to local phonon modes, likely using model Hamiltonians and theoretical techniques to determine ground states and finite-temperature behavior.
result: They identify multipolar ground states and characterize how thermal fluctuations affect the Jahn-Teller distortions and ordering in these systems.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the electron-phonon physics and multipolar order in spin-orbit-coupled Mott insulators, relevant to quantum materials research.
