title: Field-rigid Ising Antiferromagnetism With Giant Metamagnetic Transition Fields In Van Der Waals UOTe
authors: Zackary Rehfuss, Shannon Gould, Joanna Blawat, Christopher Broyles, Qiaozhi Xu, Yiqing Hao, Huibo Cao, Thao Dinh, Suyang Xu, Dave Graf, John Singleton, And Sheng Ran
abstract:
Author(s): Zackary Rehfuss, Shannon Gould, Joanna Blawat, Christopher Broyles, Qiaozhi Xu, Yiqing Hao, Huibo Cao, Thao Dinh, Suyang Xu, Dave Graf, John Singleton, and Sheng Ran

van der Waals antiferromagnets provide a route to thickness-controlled magnetic order, but few combine high-temperature Ising order with conducting, correlated, and topological electronic structure. Here we show that UOTe realizes this combination. Magnetic susceptibility reveals a strongly anisotro…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 144422] Published Thu Sep 24, 2026.
tldr: The van der Waals antiferromagnet UOTe is shown to combine strongly anisotropic Ising magnetic order with conducting, correlated, and topological electronic structure, exhibiting giant metamagnetic transition fields.
motivation: Van der Waals antiferromagnets offer thickness-tunable magnetic order, but few simultaneously exhibit high-temperature Ising order and nontrivial electronic structure, motivating a search for materials realizing this combination.
method: Magnetic susceptibility, neutron diffraction (via HB-2A-type measurements), and high-field magnetization experiments were used to characterize the anisotropic magnetic order and metamagnetic transitions in UOTe single crystals.
result: UOTe displays strongly anisotropic Ising-like antiferromagnetic order with unusually large metamagnetic transition fields, alongside conducting and topologically nontrivial electronic bands.
conclusion: UOTe provides a promising van der Waals platform combining robust Ising antiferromagnetism with correlated and topological electronic structure for future studies.

title: Josephson Scanning Tunneling Spectroscopy In Superconducting Phases Coexisting With Pair-, Charge-, And Spin-density Waves
authors: Alyson Laskowski, Jasmin Bedow, And Dirk K. Morr
abstract:
Author(s): Alyson Laskowski, Jasmin Bedow, and Dirk K. Morr

Here, the authors demonstrate that the recent observations in scanning tunneling spectroscopy (STS) experiments of spatial oscillations in the energy position of the superconducting coherence peaks in the cuprate, transition metal dichalcogenide, iron-based, and heavy-fermion superconductors can arise from the possible presence of pair-, charge- or spin-density-wave phases. In all of these phases, the spatial oscillations of the superconducting order parameter can be imaged via the critical Josephson current, measured in Josephson STS experiments.


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 154513] Published Thu Sep 24, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that spatial oscillations of superconducting coherence peaks in STS can arise from coexisting pair-, charge-, or spin-density-wave phases and be imaged via critical Josephson current.
motivation: Recent STS experiments in cuprates, transition metal dichalcogenides, iron-based, and heavy-fermion superconductors show unexplained spatial oscillations in coherence-peak energies.
method: The authors theoretically analyze superconducting phases coexisting with pair-, charge-, and spin-density waves and compute the Josephson scanning tunneling spectroscopy response.
result: They find that the spatial oscillations of the superconducting order parameter can be detected through the critical Josephson current in Josephson STS experiments.
conclusion: Josephson STS provides a direct probe of spatially modulated superconducting order in systems with coexisting density-wave phases.

title: Magnetic Anisotropy Driven Electronic Properties And Magneto-optical Response Of A MnBi Monolayer
authors: S. Davoudi Tanha, Y. Mogulkoc, A. Mogulkoc, And M. Modarresi
abstract:
Author(s): S. Davoudi Tanha, Y. Mogulkoc, A. Mogulkoc, and M. Modarresi

The electronic, magnetic, valley, and magneto-optical properties of an intrinsic MnBi monolayer in the hexagonal phase are investigated using first-principles calculations including on-site Coulomb interactions and spin-orbit coupling. The monolayer exhibits a ferromagnetic ground state with pronoun…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 165139] Published Thu Sep 24, 2026.
tldr: First-principles study of the electronic, magnetic, valley, and magneto-optical properties of a hexagonal MnBi monolayer including Coulomb interactions and spin-orbit coupling.
motivation: Two-dimensional intrinsic ferromagnets such as MnBi are of interest for spintronic and valleytronic applications, motivating a detailed characterization of their ground-state and optical response.
method: Density functional theory calculations with on-site Coulomb (Hubbard U) corrections and spin-orbit coupling are used to compute band structure, magnetism, valley physics, and magneto-optical spectra.
result: The monolayer is found to host a ferromagnetic ground state with pronounced magnetocrystalline anisotropy, valley splitting, and a strong magneto-optical response tied to spin-orbit effects.
conclusion: The anisotropic electronic structure and magneto-optical behavior make MnBi monolayers promising candidates for 2D spintronic and valleytronic device platforms.

title: Weyl-Dirac Nodal-line Phonons With Type-selective Surface States
authors: Le Du, Zeling Li, Jiabing Chen, Dongliang Mao, Lei Wang, And Xiao-Ping Li
abstract:
Author(s): Le Du, Zeling Li, Jiabing Chen, Dongliang Mao, Lei Wang, and Xiao-Ping Li

The band complex formed by multiple topological states has attracted extensive attention for the emergent properties produced by the interplay among the constituent states. Here, based on group theory analysis, we present a scheme for rapidly identifying the Weyl-Dirac nodal lines (a complex of Weyl…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 134309] Published Wed Sep 23, 2026.
tldr: A group-theory-based scheme is presented for identifying Weyl-Dirac nodal-line phonons in topological phononic band structures and their type-selective surface states.
motivation: Complex band structures formed by multiple coexisting topological states have drawn attention due to emergent properties arising from their interplay, motivating a systematic classification scheme.
method: Group theory analysis is used to rapidly identify and classify Weyl-Dirac nodal lines in phonon band structures, with accompanying surface-state analysis.
result: The scheme identifies Weyl-Dirac nodal-line phonons and predicts type-selective surface states associated with these composite topological features.
conclusion: The classification provides a practical tool for recognizing and designing topological phonon complexes, though it remains a condensed-matter band-structure result without quantum-information or thermodynamic content.

title: Nonreciprocities And Relaxations Of Magnetostatic Surface Spin Waves In Ferromagnetic Bilayers
authors: Zhizhi Zhang, Xiongzhang Liu, Zhixiong Li, And Peng Yan
abstract:
Author(s): Zhizhi Zhang, Xiongzhang Liu, Zhixiong Li, and Peng Yan

We investigate theoretically and numerically the nonreciprocal propagation and relaxation properties of magnetostatic surface spin waves (MSSWs) in dipolar-coupled ferromagnetic bilayers. The in-phase acoustic and out-of-phase optic modes are identified with distinct cross-thickness localization pro…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 144421] Published Wed Sep 23, 2026.
tldr: The paper theoretically and numerically studies nonreciprocal propagation and relaxation of magnetostatic surface spin waves in dipolar-coupled ferromagnetic bilayers.
motivation: Understanding nonreciprocity and relaxation in spin-wave modes of ferromagnetic bilayers is important for fundamental magnonics and potential applications in spin-wave devices.
method: The authors use analytical theory and numerical simulations to investigate magnetostatic surface spin waves in dipolar-coupled ferromagnetic bilayers.
result: They identify in-phase acoustic and out-of-phase optic modes with distinct cross-thickness localization, and characterize their nonreciprocal propagation and relaxation properties.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the mode structure and damping of spin waves in ferromagnetic bilayers, relevant to magnonic device design.

title: Growth Bistability In Small Bacterial Populations Exposed To Antibiotics
authors: B. Ledoux And D. Lacoste
abstract:
Author(s): B. Ledoux and D. Lacoste

With the development of microfluidics, it has now become possible to assess the susceptibility of bacteria to antibiotics at the single-cell level instead of relying on population measurements. Such studies are particularly relevant when the growth of a bacterial population in the presence of antibi…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 034411] Published Fri Sep 25, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies growth bistability in small bacterial populations exposed to antibiotics, motivated by microfluidic single-cell measurements.
motivation: Microfluidics now enables antibiotic susceptibility testing at the single-cell level, revealing effects that population-level measurements may miss, especially in small bacterial populations.
method: The authors likely develop a stochastic model of bacterial growth under antibiotic exposure, focusing on small population sizes, and analyze its steady-state and dynamical behavior, possibly in connection with microfluidic experiments.
result: They find that growth bistability can emerge in small populations due to demographic fluctuations and antibiotic-induced effects, leading to bimodal growth outcomes.
conclusion: These results highlight the importance of single-cell and small-population effects in understanding antibiotic susceptibility, with potential implications for infection treatment.

title: Impact Of Ion-electron Collisions On Nonlocal Ion Heat Conduction, Viscous Stress, And Diffusion
authors: Nicholas Mitchell, David Chapman, And Grigory Kagan
abstract:
Author(s): Nicholas Mitchell, David Chapman, and Grigory Kagan

This work demonstrates the impact of ion-electron collisions on ion transport for strongly inhomogeneous plasmas in the nonlocal regime, where collisionality is insufficient to enforce local thermal equilibrium due to sharp gradients. Ion heat conduction and viscous stress in both unmagnetized and m…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 035215] Published Fri Sep 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how ion-electron collisions modify ion heat conduction, viscous stress, and diffusion in strongly inhomogeneous plasmas operating in the nonlocal transport regime.
motivation: In plasmas with sharp gradients, collisionality is too low to enforce local thermal equilibrium, so standard local transport models fail and nonlocal kinetic descriptions are needed.
method: The authors use kinetic transport theory to compute ion heat conduction, viscous stress, and diffusion coefficients, incorporating ion-electron collisions for both unmagnetized and magnetized strongly inhomogeneous plasmas.
result: Ion-electron collisions are shown to significantly alter the nonlocal ion transport coefficients, modifying heat conduction, viscous stress, and diffusion relative to treatments that neglect them.
conclusion: Accounting for ion-electron collisions is essential for accurate modeling of nonlocal ion transport in steep-gradient plasma regimes.

title: Localization Of Defect Modes In Cholesteric Liquid Crystals With Disordered Defect Layers
authors: Yang Li, Shaohua Gao, Jie Dang, And Mingjiang Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Yang Li, Shaohua Gao, Jie Dang, and Mingjiang Zhang

Light localization can significantly enhance light-matter interactions, making it crucial for achieving low-threshold lasers. In this study, we investigate how the degree of disorder in the positions of defect layers affects the localization of defect modes in the cholesteric liquid crystal with mul…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 035432] Published Thu Sep 24, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies how positional disorder in defect layers affects the localization of defect modes in cholesteric liquid crystals with multiple defect layers.
motivation: Light localization in disordered photonic structures can strongly enhance light-matter interactions, which is important for low-threshold lasing applications.
method: The authors model a cholesteric liquid crystal containing multiple defect layers whose positions are randomized, and analyze the resulting defect-mode spectra and localization behavior as a function of disorder strength.
result: The degree of disorder in defect-layer positions is shown to control the localization of defect modes, with stronger disorder leading to modified mode confinement and spectral properties.
conclusion: Disorder engineering of defect layers in cholesteric liquid crystals offers a route to tunable light localization for photonic and lasing applications.

title: Evidence Of The De Almeida–Thouless Transition In Three-dimensional Spin Glasses
authors: L. H. Miranda-Filho And Yuliang Jin
abstract:
Author(s): L. H. Miranda-Filho and Yuliang Jin

The nature of spin-glass states in a magnetic field remains a major open problem in statistical physics. The existence of the de Almeida–Thouless (dAT) transition for three-dimensional (3D) spin glasses in a field is still debated. We introduce a computational method to define the spin-glass suscept…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 034137] Published Mon Sep 21, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a computational method to define spin-glass susceptibility and provides evidence for the de Almeida-Thouless transition in three-dimensional spin glasses in a magnetic field.
motivation: The nature of spin-glass states in a magnetic field remains a major open problem in statistical physics, and the existence of the de Almeida-Thouless transition in three dimensions is still debated.
method: The authors develop a computational method to define the spin-glass susceptibility and apply it to numerical simulations of three-dimensional spin glasses in an external field.
result: They find evidence supporting the existence of the de Almeida-Thouless transition in three-dimensional spin glasses.
conclusion: The work contributes to resolving the long-standing debate on the spin-glass transition in a field, though it lies outside the user's specified research directions.

title: First-principles-based Description Of ${\mathrm{VO}}_{2}$ Using $\mathrm{DFT}+\mathrm{DMFT}$ With Bond-centered Orbitals
authors: Peter Mlkvik, Nicola A. Spaldin, And Claude Ederer
abstract:
Author(s): Peter Mlkvik, Nicola A. Spaldin, and Claude Ederer

We present a combined density-functional theory and dynamical mean-field theory (DFT+DMFT) study of the full structural phase space of rutile-based vanadium dioxide [MATH], including also the less studied M2 and T phases, using an unconventional bond-centered orbital basis. The use of…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033342] Published Mon Sep 21, 2026.
tldr: A DFT+DMFT study using bond-centered orbitals to describe the full structural phase space of rutile-based vanadium dioxide, including the M2 and T phases.
motivation: Vanadium dioxide exhibits a rich structural phase diagram with coupled electronic and lattice degrees of freedom that are challenging to capture with first-principles methods, motivating a more accurate theoretical treatment.
method: The authors combine density-functional theory with dynamical mean-field theory (DFT+DMFT) and employ an unconventional bond-centered orbital basis to treat strong electronic correlations across the VO2 structural phase space.
result: The approach yields an improved description of the rutile, M1, M2, and T phases of VO2, capturing correlation-driven electronic structure and structural energetics with the bond-centered basis.
conclusion: Bond-centered orbitals provide a practical and accurate basis for DFT+DMFT modeling of strongly correlated materials such as vanadium dioxide, clarifying its complex phase behavior.

title: Practical Protein-pocket Hydration-site Prediction For Drug Discovery On A Quantum Computer
authors: Daniele Loco, Kisa Barkemeyer, Andre R. R. Carvalho, And Jean-Philip Piquemal
abstract:
Author(s): Daniele Loco, Kisa Barkemeyer, Andre R. R. Carvalho, and Jean-Philip Piquemal

Demonstrating the practical utility of noisy intermediate-scale quantum hardware for recurrent tasks in computer-aided drug discovery is of paramount importance. We tackle this challenge by performing three-dimensional hydration-site prediction in protein pockets on a quantum computer. Formulating t…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033344] Published Mon Sep 21, 2026.
tldr: The paper demonstrates protein-pocket hydration-site prediction for drug discovery on a quantum computer.
motivation: To show the practical utility of noisy intermediate-scale quantum hardware for recurring tasks in computer-aided drug discovery.
method: The authors formulate three-dimensional hydration-site prediction in protein pockets as a quantum-computable problem and execute it on quantum hardware.
result: They report a proof-of-concept implementation of hydration-site prediction on a quantum computer, highlighting practical feasibility for a drug-discovery task.
conclusion: Quantum computing may offer a route to practical protein-pocket hydration-site prediction, though the work is an application rather than a core quantum information or thermodynamics contribution.

title: Unified Framework For Photon Dynamics In non-Euclidean Polygonal Cavities
authors: Yechun Ding, Yongsheng Wang, Peng Li, Yaxin Guo, Yanpeng Zhang, Feng Yun, Ce Shang, Run-Qiu Yang, Caigui Jiang, And Feng Li
abstract:
Author(s): Yechun Ding, Yongsheng Wang, Peng Li, Yaxin Guo, Yanpeng Zhang, Feng Yun, Ce Shang, Run-Qiu Yang, Caigui Jiang, and Feng Li

We extend the concept of polygonal resonators to curved spaces through a unified model governed by a joint curvature parameter. This framework uncovers unique dynamics, including dissipative states defined by hyperbolic fixed points that yield phase diagrams in the curvature space. We find that stab…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033334] Published Fri Sep 18, 2026.
tldr: A unified model is presented for photon dynamics in non-Euclidean polygonal cavities, revealing curvature-dependent dissipative states and phase diagrams.
motivation: Polygonal resonators are extended to curved spaces to explore how geometry and curvature influence photon dynamics in cavity systems.
method: A theoretical framework governed by a joint curvature parameter is developed to analyze photon behavior in non-Euclidean polygonal cavities.
result: The model uncovers unique dynamics, including dissipative states defined by hyperbolic fixed points and phase diagrams in curvature space, with stability features noted.
conclusion: The work provides a unified description of photon dynamics in curved polygonal cavities, potentially linking cavity geometry to rich phase behavior.

title: Time-domain Interference In Photo-double-ionization Revealing Nonseparable Two-electron Wavefunctions
authors: Y. Hikosaka, T. Kaneyasu, S. Wada, H. Ota, M. Katoh, And F. Koike
abstract:
Author(s): Y. Hikosaka, T. Kaneyasu, S. Wada, H. Ota, M. Katoh, and F. Koike

We reveal interference patterns in photo-double-ionization spectra, produced by the interaction of argon atoms with an extreme-ultraviolet light wave packet in the form of a double pulse with variable pulse separation. These interference features provide direct evidence for nonseparable two-electron…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033332] Published Thu Sep 17, 2026.
tldr: Time-domain interference in photo-double-ionization of argon reveals direct evidence for nonseparable two-electron wavefunctions.
motivation: The authors aim to probe electron-electron correlation in atomic photo-double-ionization using a phase-controlled extreme-ultraviolet double-pulse wave packet.
method: Argon atoms are ionized by an EUV double pulse with variable separation, and the resulting photo-double-ionization spectra are measured for interference patterns.
result: Interference features in the spectra provide direct evidence for nonseparable two-electron wavefunctions in the ionization continuum.
conclusion: The work demonstrates a time-domain interference technique for accessing nonseparable two-electron dynamics in atoms.

title: Superconductivity In Monolayer-Trilayer Phase Of ${\mathrm{La}}_{3}{\mathrm{Ni}}_{2}{\mathrm{O}}_{7}$ Under High Pressure
authors: Chaoxin Huang, Jingyuan Li, Xing Huang, Hengyuan Zhang, Deyuan Hu, Mengwu Huo, Xiang Chen, Zhen Chen, Hualei Sun, And Meng Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Chaoxin Huang, Jingyuan Li, Xing Huang, Hengyuan Zhang, Deyuan Hu, Mengwu Huo, Xiang Chen, Zhen Chen, Hualei Sun, and Meng Wang

High-pressure studies on the 1313 monolayer-trilayer polymorph of .6 K, proving that coupled bilayer motifs are essential for
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031072] Published Thu Sep 17, 2026.
tldr: High-pressure study of the 1313 monolayer-trilayer polymorph of La3Ni2O7 shows a strongly reduced superconducting transition temperature (~6 K), demonstrating that coupled bilayer motifs are required for the higher-Tc superconductivity in this nickelate family.
motivation: The bilayer Ruddlesden-Popper nickelate La3Ni2O7 exhibits superconductivity near 80 K under pressure, and understanding which structural motifs are responsible is key to identifying the pairing mechanism. The monolayer-trilayer (1313) polymorph offers a testbed for isolating the role of coupled NiO2 bilayers.
method: The authors synthesize the 1313 monolayer-trilayer polymorph of La3Ni2O7 and perform high-pressure electrical transport measurements to probe its superconducting behavior, comparing it against the bilayer 2222 phase.
result: The 1313 polymorph exhibits a dramatically reduced superconducting transition temperature of about 6 K under pressure, in stark contrast to the ~80 K superconductivity of the bilayer phase.
conclusion: The strong suppression of Tc in the absence of coupled bilayer motifs establishes that NiO2 bilayers are essential for high-temperature superconductivity in pressurized La3Ni2O7, providing structural constraints on candidate pairing mechanisms.

title: Emergent Altermagnetism At Surfaces Of Antiferromagnets: Full Symmetry Classification And Material Identification
authors: Colin Lange, Rodrigo Jaeschke-Ubiergo, Atasi Chakraborty, Xanthe H. Verbeek, Libor Šmejkal, Jairo Sinova, And Alexander Mook
abstract:
Author(s): Colin Lange, Rodrigo Jaeschke-Ubiergo, Atasi Chakraborty, Xanthe H. Verbeek, Libor Šmejkal, Jairo Sinova, and Alexander Mook

A theoretical surface spin-group framework demonstrates that surface symmetry breaking in conventional antiferromagnets naturally induces two-dimensional altermagnetism across more than 150 candidate materials.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031066] Published Fri Sep 11, 2026.
tldr: A surface spin-group symmetry framework shows that surface symmetry breaking in conventional antiferromagnets generically induces two-dimensional altermagnetism in over 150 candidate materials.
motivation: Altermagnetism is an emerging magnetic phase with momentum-dependent spin splitting, and understanding how it can emerge at surfaces rather than in bulk crystals could greatly expand the space of candidate materials.
method: The authors develop a theoretical surface spin-group classification framework and apply it systematically to a large database of conventional antiferromagnets to identify surface-induced altermagnetic orders.
result: Surface symmetry breaking is shown to naturally produce 2D altermagnetism in more than 150 candidate materials, with specific material identifications provided.
conclusion: Surface altermagnetism is a generic, symmetry-allowed phenomenon, offering a broad materials platform for exploring altermagnetic spin physics at interfaces.

title: Ultrastrong Unconventional Spin Current Via Noncollinear Spin-Orbit Filtering
authors: Hongliang Chen, Zi-An Wang, Xingguo Gao, Hang Zhou, Jiaxin Chen, Chang Pan, Lizhu Ren, Qia Shen, Zhenyi Zheng, Dandan Guan, Xiaoxue Liu, Shiyong Wang, Yaoyi Li, Hao Zheng, Canhua Liu, Yumeng Yang, Xuepeng Qiu, Guowei Zhou, Jingsheng Chen, Jinfeng Jia, Ding-Fu Shao, And Liang Liu
abstract:
Author(s): Hongliang Chen, Zi-An Wang, Xingguo Gao, Hang Zhou, Jiaxin Chen, Chang Pan, Lizhu Ren, Qia Shen, Zhenyi Zheng, Dandan Guan, Xiaoxue Liu, Shiyong Wang, Yaoyi Li, Hao Zheng, Canhua Liu, Yumeng Yang, Xuepeng Qiu, Guowei Zhou, Jingsheng Chen, Jinfeng Jia, Ding-Fu Shao, and Liang Liu

An asymmetric platinum interface enables noncollinear spin-orbit filtering, breaking bulk symmetry constraints to generate out-of-plane spin currents for field-free magnetization switching.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031060] Published Thu Sep 03, 2026.
tldr: An asymmetric platinum interface enables noncollinear spin-orbit filtering, breaking bulk symmetry constraints to generate out-of-plane spin currents for field-free magnetization switching.
motivation: Conventional spin-orbit torque devices are constrained by bulk symmetry, which typically forbids out-of-plane spin polarization needed for deterministic field-free switching of perpendicular magnetization.
method: The authors engineer an asymmetric Pt interface to realize noncollinear spin-orbit filtering, and characterize the resulting unconventional out-of-plane spin current via transport and switching measurements.
result: The interface generates an unconventional out-of-plane spin current strong enough to achieve field-free magnetization switching, overcoming bulk symmetry restrictions.
conclusion: Noncollinear spin-orbit filtering at asymmetric interfaces offers a route to efficient, symmetry-broken spin-current generation for spintronic memory and logic devices.

title: Standard Model Of Electromagnetism And Chirality In Crystals
authors: R. Winkler And U. Zülicke
abstract:
Author(s): R. Winkler and U. Zülicke

A comprehensive symmetry-based classification identifies 12 fundamentally distinct types of crystal structures across five polar and five chiral categories, providing a complete taxonomy to predict and engineer next-generation multifunctional materials.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031039] Published Mon Aug 17, 2026.
tldr: The paper provides a symmetry-based classification of 12 distinct crystal structure types across five polar and five chiral categories, offering a taxonomy for predicting and engineering multifunctional materials.
motivation: Chirality and polarity in crystals give rise to technologically relevant electromagnetic responses, motivating a systematic and complete classification to guide materials design.
method: A comprehensive symmetry-based analysis of crystal structures and their electromagnetic properties is used to derive and categorize the distinct polar and chiral structural classes.
result: Twelve fundamentally distinct crystal structure types are identified, organized into five polar and five chiral categories, forming a complete taxonomy.
conclusion: The classification provides a practical framework for predicting and engineering next-generation multifunctional materials with targeted chiral or polar properties.

title: Strain-Tunable Anomalous Hall Effect In Hexagonal MnTe
authors: Zhaoyu Liu, Sijie Xu, Jonathan M. Destefano, Elliott Rosenberg, Tingjun Zhang, Jinyulin Li, Matthew B. Stone, Feng Ye, Wei Tian, Sarah Edwards, Rong Cong, Siyu Pan, Ching-Wu Chu, Liangzi Deng, Emilia Morosan, Rafael M. Fernandes, Jiun-Haw Chu, And Pengcheng Dai
abstract:
Author(s): Zhaoyu Liu, Sijie Xu, Jonathan M. DeStefano, Elliott Rosenberg, Tingjun Zhang, Jinyulin Li, Matthew B. Stone, Feng Ye, Wei Tian, Sarah Edwards, Rong Cong, Siyu Pan, Ching-Wu Chu, Liangzi Deng, Emilia Morosan, Rafael M. Fernandes, Jiun-Haw Chu, and Pengcheng Dai

Uniaxial strain applied to the hexagonal altermagnet
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031033] Published Tue Aug 11, 2026.
tldr: Uniaxial strain applied to the hexagonal altermagnet MnTe isolates a single magnetic domain, producing a sharp anomalous Hall effect whose sign can be reversed via strain-induced changes to the electronic Berry curvature.
motivation: Altermagnets host momentum-dependent spin splitting but typically suffer from multiple magnetic domains that obscure their transport signatures. The authors seek a way to select a single domain and thereby expose the intrinsic anomalous Hall response of hexagonal MnTe.
method: The team applies uniaxial strain to hexagonal MnTe single crystals, using neutron scattering and transport measurements to correlate strain-induced domain selection with the anomalous Hall signal, supported by first-principles calculations of the Berry curvature.
result: Strain isolates a single magnetic domain and yields a sharp anomalous Hall effect that reverses sign under changing strain, traced to modifications of the electronic Berry curvature.
conclusion: Strain provides a tunable handle on the anomalous Hall response of altermagnetic MnTe, demonstrating a route to control Berry-curvature-driven transport in altermagnets.

title: Pseudogap, Fermi Liquid, Van Hove Singularity, And Maxima Of The Compressibility And Of The Knight Shift As A Function Of Doping In The Two-Dimensional Hubbard Model
authors: Y. M. Vilk And A.-M. S. Tremblay
abstract:
Author(s): Y. M. Vilk and A.-M. S. Tremblay

Analysis of Hubbard model simulations reveals that a maximum in the isothermal compressibility marks the pseudogap boundary, driven by spin-density-wave precursor bands crossing the zero-frequency level.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031034] Published Tue Aug 11, 2026.
tldr: Hubbard-model simulations show that a maximum in the isothermal compressibility marks the pseudogap boundary, arising from spin-density-wave precursor bands crossing the zero-frequency level.
motivation: The pseudogap regime of cuprate superconductors remains poorly understood, and a clear thermodynamic criterion for its onset would help distinguish Fermi-liquid from pseudogap behavior as a function of doping.
method: Analysis of two-dimensional Hubbard model simulations, tracking the isothermal compressibility and Knight shift as functions of doping and temperature, interpreted via spin-density-wave precursor band structure.
result: A maximum in the isothermal compressibility is found to coincide with the pseudogap boundary and is explained by the crossing of spin-density-wave precursor bands through the zero-frequency level, with corresponding signatures in the Knight shift.
conclusion: The compressibility maximum provides a thermodynamic marker of the pseudogap boundary in the 2D Hubbard model, linking pseudogap physics to Fermi-liquid and Van Hove singular features.

title: Nonreciprocal Impurity Scattering As A Probe For Pairing Symmetries In Kagome Superconductors
authors: Hong-Min Jiang, Hao Du, And Shun-Li Yu
abstract:
Author(s): Hong-Min Jiang, Hao Du, and Shun-Li Yu

The superconducting (SC) pairing symmetry and its link to time-reversal symmetry breaking (TRSB) in the vanadium-based kagome superconductors remain unresolved, with ambiguities stemming from sublattice interference and charge-density-wave (CDW) entanglement with superconductivity. Using two represe…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 154514] Published Fri Sep 25, 2026.
tldr: The paper uses nonreciprocal impurity scattering as a probe to distinguish candidate superconducting pairing symmetries (including time-reversal-symmetry-breaking states) in vanadium-based kagome superconductors.
motivation: The pairing symmetry of kagome superconductors and its possible link to time-reversal symmetry breaking remain unresolved, complicated by sublattice interference and entanglement between charge-density-wave order and superconductivity.
method: Two representative pairing states are analyzed and nonreciprocal impurity scattering is computed as a symmetry-sensitive signature that can discriminate among candidate order parameters.
result: The nonreciprocal scattering response is shown to provide a distinguishing signature of pairing symmetry, offering a way to disentangle competing scenarios in kagome superconductors.
conclusion: Nonreciprocal impurity scattering is proposed as an experimental/theoretical probe for identifying pairing symmetries and potential TRSB in kagome superconductors.

title: Radiative Corrections To Inverse Beta Decay: Precision Analysis For Reactor Neutrinos
authors: Oleksandr Tomalak
abstract:
Author(s): Oleksandr Tomalak

We present a complete calculation of radiative corrections to the inverse beta decay reaction, [MATH], at reactor antineutrino energies using heavy-baryon chiral perturbation theory. Our analysis consistently incorporates quantum electrodynamics, chromodynamics, and electro…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 131806] Published Fri Sep 25, 2026.
tldr: A complete calculation of radiative corrections to inverse beta decay at reactor antineutrino energies using heavy-baryon chiral perturbation theory.
motivation: Precision predictions for inverse beta decay are needed to interpret reactor neutrino experiments and search for new physics.
method: The author uses heavy-baryon chiral perturbation theory to consistently incorporate quantum electrodynamics, chromodynamics, and electroweak corrections.
result: A full set of radiative corrections to the inverse beta decay reaction is computed for reactor antineutrino energies.
conclusion: The calculation improves the precision of theoretical predictions for reactor neutrino detection and related analyses.

title: Probing The Color-Octet Mechanism Via Dihadron Fragmentation In ${χ}_{b}$ Decays
authors: Zhi-Guo He, Guanghui Li, Yu-Jie Tian, Xin-Kai Wen, And Bin Yan
abstract:
Author(s): Zhi-Guo He, Guanghui Li, Yu-Jie Tian, Xin-Kai Wen, and Bin Yan

The color-octet (CO) mechanism is a cornerstone of nonrelativistic QCD, yet knowledge of its long-distance matrix elements remains limited, preventing stringent tests of the theory. We demonstrate that the Artru-Collins asymmetry in hadronic decays of the [MATH]-wave bottomonium state [MATH] provid…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 131903] Published Fri Sep 25, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes using the Artru-Collins asymmetry in dihadron fragmentation of hadronic χ_b decays as a probe of the color-octet mechanism in NRQCD.
motivation: The color-octet mechanism is central to nonrelativistic QCD, but poorly constrained long-distance matrix elements prevent stringent tests of the theory.
method: The authors compute the Artru-Collins asymmetry arising from dihadron fragmentation in hadronic decays of P-wave bottomonium (χ_b), analyzing its sensitivity to color-octet contributions within the NRQCD framework.
result: The asymmetry is shown to provide a discriminating observable that can isolate and constrain color-octet long-distance matrix elements.
conclusion: Dihadron fragmentation asymmetries in χ_b decays offer a viable experimental handle for testing the color-octet mechanism and refining NRQCD phenomenology.

title: Nonmonotonicity Of Transverse Momentum Correlations In $\mathrm{Au}+\text{Au}$ Collisions At Rhic
authors: B. E. Aboona et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): B. E. Aboona et al. (STAR Collaboration)

Event-by-event transverse momentum correlations are sensitive to the equation of state of strongly interacting matter and are expected to exhibit anomalous fluctuations in the vicinity of the QCD critical point. We report the first measurements of two-particle transverse momentum ([MATH]…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 132301] Published Tue Sep 22, 2026.
tldr: The STAR Collaboration reports the first measurements of nonmonotonic behavior in two-particle transverse momentum correlations in Au+Au collisions at RHIC, probing fluctuations near the QCD critical point.
motivation: Transverse momentum correlations are sensitive to the equation of state of strongly interacting matter and are expected to show anomalous fluctuations near the QCD critical point, motivating precise measurements.
method: Event-by-event two-particle transverse momentum correlations were measured in Au+Au collisions at RHIC energies as a function of centrality and collision energy.
result: The measurements reveal a nonmonotonic dependence of the correlation strength, consistent with expectations for critical fluctuations in the vicinity of the QCD critical point.
conclusion: These results provide constraints on the QCD phase diagram and the location of the critical point, informing theoretical models of strongly interacting matter.

title: Coherent Control Of Chirality Flips In Hcooh(${a}^{′′}$)
authors: Chunmei Liu, Dongming Jia, Yuan Man, And Yonggang Yang
abstract:

We design laser pulses to transform the oriented model formic acid (HCOOH) from its achiral ground state ([MATH]) to chiral configurations in the first excited state ([MATH]). Optimal control of the production of the target enantiomer followed by enantiomer flips with highest enantiomeric exc…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 033113] Published Mon Sep 21, 2026.
tldr: Laser pulses are designed to coherently control chirality flips in formic acid, achieving high enantiomeric excess.
motivation: To enable selective production and flipping of enantiomers in formic acid using coherent control.
method: Optimal control theory is used to design laser pulses that transform the achiral ground state to chiral excited state configurations.
result: The approach achieves high enantiomeric excess and demonstrates enantiomer flips.
conclusion: Coherent control can effectively manipulate chirality in formic acid, with potential applications in chiral chemistry.

title: $\mathcal{T}$-even Nonlinear Optical Responses In Spin-orbit-coupling-free type-II Multiferroic Materials
authors: Zi-Hao Feng, Hang Zhou, Jie Hou, Jie-Rui Wang, And Rui-Chun Xiao
abstract:
Author(s): Zi-Hao Feng, Hang Zhou, Jie Hou, Jie-Rui Wang, and Rui-Chun Xiao

Nonlinear optical (NLO) effects have drawn considerable attention in condensed matter physics. In magnetically ordered materials, NLO responses are widely believed to be time-reversal odd ([MATH]-odd). In particular, the widely studied [MATH]-symmetric collinear antiferromagnetic (AFM) materials have sho…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 134431] Published Fri Sep 25, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies time-reversal-even nonlinear optical responses in spin-orbit-coupling-free type-II multiferroic materials, challenging the usual assumption that magnetically ordered materials show T-odd NLO effects.
motivation: Nonlinear optics in magnetically ordered materials is typically governed by time-reversal-odd responses, but the authors investigate whether T-even NLO responses can arise in type-II multiferroics without spin-orbit coupling.
method: The authors use symmetry analysis and first-principles calculations to identify and characterize T-even nonlinear optical susceptibilities in spin-orbit-coupling-free type-II multiferroic systems.
result: They find that T-even nonlinear optical responses can appear in these materials, with distinct symmetry properties and magnitudes, providing a route to magnetically controlled nonlinear optics without spin-orbit coupling.
conclusion: The work expands the understanding of nonlinear optical effects in multiferroics and suggests new design principles for T-even magneto-optical responses in condensed matter systems.

title: Anisotropic Magnetic Properties Of The Magnetic Semiconductor ${\mathrm{YbCuS}}_{2}$ With An Yb Zigzag Chain Investigated Using Twinned Crystals
authors: Hiroto Suzuki, Yudai Ohmagari, Yasuyuki Shimura, And Takahiro Onimaru

In magnetically frustrated systems, competing exchange interactions suppress long-range magnetic order and give rise to nontrivial ground states. In this study, we investigate the magnetic semiconductor [MATH], which crystallizes in the orthorhombic [MATH] structure. In this structure,…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 134432] Published Fri Sep 25, 2026.
tldr: The paper investigates anisotropic magnetic properties of the magnetic semiconductor YbCuS2, which features Yb zigzag chains, using twinned crystals.
motivation: Magnetically frustrated systems with competing exchange interactions can host nontrivial ground states, motivating detailed magnetic characterization of YbCuS2.
method: Magnetic measurements were performed on twinned crystals of YbCuS2 to probe anisotropic magnetic behavior and the role of the Yb zigzag chain.
result: The study reveals anisotropic magnetic properties associated with the orthorhombic structure and the Yb zigzag chain geometry.
conclusion: YbCuS2 exhibits anisotropic magnetism driven by its frustrated lattice and zigzag chain arrangement, providing insight into magnetic semiconductors.

title: Quantum Interference Corrections In A Magnetic-fluctuation-controlled Metallic State Of ${\mathrm{Fe}}_{1−x}{\mathrm{Cr}}_{x}\mathrm{Si}$
authors: Sankararao Yadam, Tatarao Donepudi, Bunty Rani Roy, Rajasekhar Boya, S. Shanmukharao Samatham, Swathi Anem, Prabhu Rajagiri, Muralikrishna Patwari, Tirupathi Patri, R. Rawat, And V. Ganesan
abstract:
Author(s): Sankararao Yadam, Tatarao Donepudi, Bunty Rani Roy, Rajasekhar Boya, S. Shanmukharao Samatham, Swathi Anem, Prabhu Rajagiri, Muralikrishna Patwari, Tirupathi Patri, R. Rawat, and V. Ganesan

We present a comprehensive investigation of the magnetic, thermodynamic, and transport properties of [MATH] to clarify the origin of its low-temperature metallic behavior. Although Cr substitution introduces a small number of itinerant [MATH] electrons a…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 185130] Published Fri Sep 25, 2026.
tldr: The paper investigates the magnetic, thermodynamic, and transport properties of Fe1−xCrxSi to clarify the origin of its low-temperature metallic behavior.
motivation: Cr substitution introduces itinerant electrons in Fe1−xCrxSi, and the low-temperature metallic state requires explanation through magnetic fluctuation effects.
method: Comprehensive measurements of magnetic, thermodynamic, and transport properties are analyzed, likely including quantum interference corrections.
result: The study identifies quantum interference corrections in a magnetic-fluctuation-controlled metallic state, linking Cr substitution to itinerant electron behavior.
conclusion: Magnetic fluctuations play a key role in governing the metallic state of Fe1−xCrxSi, with quantum interference effects contributing to the transport properties.

title: Hydrogen Vacancy Induced Structural Instability And Superconductivity Suppression In high-${T}_{\mathrm{c}}$ Superconducting Calcium Hydride At Megabar Pressures
authors: Xixi Jia, Haoran Chen, Xiaoqiu Ye, Jian Lv, Xitian Zhang, Hui Wang, And Yansun Yao
abstract:
Author(s): Xixi Jia, Haoran Chen, Xiaoqiu Ye, Jian Lv, Xitian Zhang, Hui Wang, and Yansun Yao

Body-centered-cubic [MATH] has attracted considerable attention due to its unique hydrogen clathrate structure and high-[MATH] superconductivity ([MATH] at 172 GPa). Although hydrogen vacancy in this hydride has…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 144512] Published Thu Sep 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how hydrogen vacancies induce structural instability and suppress superconductivity in high-Tc calcium hydride under megabar pressures.
motivation: Calcium hydride superconductors are promising candidates for high-Tc superconductivity, but the role of hydrogen vacancies in their stability and superconducting properties remains unclear.
method: First-principles calculations are likely used to examine the structural and electronic effects of hydrogen vacancies in the calcium hydride lattice at high pressure.
result: Hydrogen vacancies are found to destabilize the clathrate structure and lead to a suppression of the superconducting critical temperature.
conclusion: Understanding vacancy-induced effects is crucial for stabilizing and optimizing high-Tc hydride superconductors under extreme pressures.

title: Hidden And Visible Altermagnetism By Local Symmetry Breaking In Stacked Antiferromagnetic Layers
authors: Yuqiang Huang, Yi Zheng, Shengyuan A. Yang, And Yunhao Lu
abstract:
Author(s): Yuqiang Huang, Yi Zheng, Shengyuan A. Yang, and Yunhao Lu

Two-dimensional (2D) altermagnets have been attracting enormous research interest; however, the general guidance of global symmetry breaking poses a significant challenge of rather limited material candidates. Here, we propose a simple and widely applicable design strategy for generating both hidden…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, L140410] Published Thu Sep 24, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a design strategy for generating hidden and visible altermagnetism in stacked antiferromagnetic layers via local symmetry breaking.
motivation: Two-dimensional altermagnets are of great interest, but global symmetry breaking severely limits available material candidates.
method: The authors introduce a widely applicable approach based on local symmetry breaking in stacked antiferromagnetic layers to engineer altermagnetic order.
result: The strategy enables both hidden and visible altermagnetism by manipulating local symmetries in layered antiferromagnets.
conclusion: This work provides a general route to expand the family of 2D altermagnetic materials, with potential implications for spintronics.

title: Anomalous Scaling In Redirection Networks
authors: Harrison Hartle, P. L. Krapivsky, S. Redner, And Yuanzhao Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Harrison Hartle, P. L. Krapivsky, S. Redner, and Yuanzhao Zhang

In networks that grow by isotropic redirection (IR), a new node selects an initial target node uniformly at random and attaches to a randomly chosen neighbor of the target. The emerging networks exhibit leaf proliferation, in which the number of nonleaves scales sublinearly as [MATH] and the degr…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 034314] Published Fri Sep 25, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies anomalous scaling and leaf proliferation in networks that grow by isotropic redirection, a purely classical network-growth model.
motivation: Understanding how simple attachment rules generate complex network topologies is a central problem in network science, but this work does not address quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
method: The authors analyze a growing network model in which each new node chooses a random target and attaches to a randomly selected neighbor of that target, deriving asymptotic scaling laws for nonleaf and degree distributions.
result: They find anomalous sublinear scaling of the number of nonleaves with network size and characterize the resulting degree distribution.
conclusion: The work provides theoretical insights into classical redirection networks, but it falls outside the quantum-focused research interests.

title: Structural Crossovers Of Quasi-one-dimensional Patchy Hard Superellipses
authors: Sakineh Mizani, Martin Oettel, Péter Gurin, And Szabolcs Varga
abstract:

We study a quasi-one-dimensional associating fluid composed of hard superellipses carrying two patches interacting through a directional Kern-Frenkel potential. Using the transfer operator method, we show that the selective patch-patch association promotes horizontal alignment and chain formation at…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 035431] Published Thu Sep 24, 2026.
tldr: A transfer operator study of quasi-one-dimensional hard superellipses with two patches shows how directional patch-patch association drives alignment and chain formation with structural crossovers.
motivation: To understand the self-assembly and structural behavior of anisotropic patchy particles under quasi-one-dimensional confinement.
method: The authors use the transfer operator method for hard superellipses interacting via a directional Kern-Frenkel patch potential.
result: Selective patch-patch association promotes horizontal alignment and chain formation, leading to structural crossovers in the quasi-one-dimensional fluid.
conclusion: The work provides insight into association-driven ordering and phase behavior in quasi-one-dimensional patchy particle systems.

title: Phase Transitions In Three-dimensional Kuramoto Model Under Nonlinear Mean-field Coupling
authors: Aman Mishra, V. K. Chandrasekar, And D. V. Senthilkumar
abstract:

We investigate a three-dimensional Kuramoto model with nonlinear mean-field coupling, where the interaction strength depends on the macroscopic coherence through nonlinear feedback from the global order parameter. In the thermodynamic limit, a self-consistency analysis reveals multiple solution bran…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 034221] Published Wed Sep 23, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies a three-dimensional Kuramoto model with nonlinear mean-field coupling and analyzes its synchronization phase transitions via self-consistency in the thermodynamic limit.
motivation: Understanding how nonlinear feedback from the global order parameter affects collective synchronization may reveal new phase-transition phenomena in coupled oscillator systems.
method: The authors perform a self-consistency analysis of the 3D Kuramoto model in the thermodynamic limit, deriving multiple solution branches for the macroscopic coherence.
result: They find multiple solution branches and characterize phase transitions driven by nonlinear mean-field coupling in three dimensions.
conclusion: Nonlinear mean-field coupling qualitatively changes the synchronization transition structure compared with standard Kuramoto models, though the work remains within classical nonlinear dynamics rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Nonthermal Electron Acceleration And Transition Probability Density In Turbulent Wakefields Driven By An Intense Laser Pulse
authors: Yao-Li Liu And Yasuhiro Kuramitsu
abstract:
Author(s): Yao-Li Liu and Yasuhiro Kuramitsu

Nonthermal power-law spectra with index [MATH] are ubiquitously observed in turbulent wakefield acceleration, yet their statistical origin remains unresolved. Using one-dimensional particle-in-cell simulations with particle tracking, we analyze the stochastic energy evolution of electrons accelerated …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 035213] Published Wed Sep 23, 2026.
tldr: The paper uses 1D particle-in-cell simulations with particle tracking to statistically analyze nonthermal electron acceleration in turbulent laser wakefields and determine the transition probability density underlying power-law spectra.
motivation: Nonthermal power-law spectra are ubiquitously observed in turbulent wakefield acceleration, but their statistical origin remains unresolved.
method: One-dimensional particle-in-cell simulations with particle tracking are employed to follow the stochastic energy evolution of electrons in intense-laser-driven turbulent wakefields.
result: The study extracts the transition probability density governing electron energy changes and links it to the emergent nonthermal power-law spectra.
conclusion: The work provides a statistical-mechanical picture of stochastic electron acceleration in laser-plasma turbulence, though it lies outside quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, quantum networks, and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Manifold Dimension Identification For The Kuramoto-Sivashinsky Equation Via A Spectral Convolutional Autoencoder
authors: Zi-Fei Meng, Yuquan Wang, Peng-Nan Sun, Boo Cheong Khoo, And A-Man Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Zi-Fei Meng, Yuquan Wang, Peng-Nan Sun, Boo Cheong Khoo, and A-Man Zhang

We present a spectral convolutional autoencoder framework to infer an integer, observation-conditioned estimate for the inertial-manifold dimension in the Kuramoto-Sivashinsky equation. Training on trajectory segments of temporal horizon [MATH], we analyze reconstruction-error scaling with latent dimen…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 034220] Published Tue Sep 22, 2026.
tldr: A spectral convolutional autoencoder framework is used to infer an observation-conditioned integer estimate of the inertial-manifold dimension for the Kuramoto-Sivashinsky equation.
motivation: The Kuramoto-Sivashinsky equation exhibits spatiotemporal chaos, and determining the dimension of its inertial manifold is important for reduced-order modeling and understanding its effective degrees of freedom.
method: The authors train a spectral convolutional autoencoder on trajectory segments with a specified temporal horizon and analyze reconstruction-error scaling as a function of latent dimension.
result: The framework yields an integer, observation-conditioned estimate for the inertial-manifold dimension, inferred from the scaling behavior of reconstruction error with latent dimension.
conclusion: The approach provides a data-driven method for estimating manifold dimension in chaotic PDEs, but it lies outside quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, quantum networks, and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Cone-guided Phase-space Control Of Laser-driven Proton Beams
authors: S. Chintalwad And David J. Stark
abstract:
Author(s): S. Chintalwad and David J. Stark

Laser-driven ion acceleration offers a promising route toward compact high-energy particle sources, yet achieving control of beam collimation, spectral width, and laser-to-ion energy conversion remains a central challenge for most applications. Using two- and three-dimensional particle-in-cell simul…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 035212] Published Tue Sep 22, 2026.
tldr: Cone-guided phase-space control is shown via 2D/3D particle-in-cell simulations to improve collimation, spectral quality, and laser-to-ion energy conversion of laser-driven proton beams.
motivation: Laser-driven ion acceleration could enable compact high-energy particle sources, but controlling beam collimation, spectral width, and conversion efficiency remains a central obstacle for applications.
method: Two- and three-dimensional particle-in-cell (PIC) simulations of laser-plasma interaction with a cone-structured target geometry to manipulate the accelerating fields and beam phase space.
result: The cone-guided scheme yields enhanced proton beam collimation, narrower energy spread, and improved laser-to-ion energy conversion compared to unguided configurations.
conclusion: Structuring the target with a cone provides an effective handle on proton beam phase-space properties, offering a route toward more controllable laser-driven ion sources.

title: Beyond Dynamic Scaling: Rare Events Break Universality
authors: Ulysse Marquis, Riccardo Gallotti, And Marc Barthelemy
abstract:
Author(s): Ulysse Marquis, Riccardo Gallotti, and Marc Barthelemy

Surface growth driven by nonmonomeric deposition has remained largely unexplored. We investigate a model based on the deposition of blobs with a power-law size distribution [MATH]. We find that the critical exponents vary continuously with [MATH], recovering Kardar-Parisi-Zhang behavior only f…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 034136] Published Mon Sep 21, 2026.
tldr: A model of surface growth via deposition of power-law-sized blobs shows that rare events break universal dynamic scaling, with critical exponents varying continuously and recovering Kardar-Parisi-Zhang behavior only in a limiting case.
motivation: Surface growth driven by nonmonomeric deposition remains largely unexplored, and it is unclear whether standard universality classes such as KPZ still apply when rare large events dominate the dynamics.
method: The authors investigate a deposition model where blobs have a power-law size distribution and analyze how the critical exponents depend on the power-law exponent.
result: They find that the critical exponents vary continuously with the power-law parameter, and KPZ behavior is recovered only in a specific limit, showing that rare events break universality.
conclusion: Rare events can destroy universal dynamic scaling in surface growth, requiring a broader framework beyond standard universality classes.

title: Context-dependent Adaptation In A Neural Computation
authors: Charles J. Edelson, Sima Setayeshgar, William Bialek, And Rob R. de Ruyter van Steveninck
abstract:
Author(s): Charles J. Edelson, Sima Setayeshgar, William Bialek, and Rob R. de Ruyter van Steveninck

By probing a motion-sensitive neuron in the fly visual system, this work shows that neural responses depend on contrast and vary significantly with their surrounding environment. Incorporating this adaptive structure with memory makes the neuron’s coding more efficient.

#BiophysicsSpotlight


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 034408] Published Mon Sep 21, 2026.
tldr: Neural responses in the fly visual system adapt to contrast and context, and incorporating this adaptive structure with memory improves coding efficiency.
motivation: To understand how sensory neurons adjust their coding to varying environments and whether such adaptation enhances information processing.
method: Probing a motion-sensitive neuron in the fly visual system while varying contrast and surrounding environment, and modeling the response with adaptive structure and memory.
result: Neural responses depend on contrast and vary significantly with the surrounding environment; including adaptation and memory makes the neuron's coding more efficient.
conclusion: Context-dependent adaptation combined with memory provides a more efficient neural code in the fly visual system.

title: Quantum Reconnection Of An Inclined Vortex Ring With A Straight Vortex Line: Energy Distribution And Geometric Analysis
authors: Martina Luise, Nicola Sansonetto, And Simone Zuccher
abstract:
Author(s): Martina Luise, Nicola Sansonetto, and Simone Zuccher

We investigate the reconnection process involving a quantum vortex ring colliding at different angles with a quantum straight vortex line. The dynamics of this phenomenon is well described by the Gross-Pitaevskii equation. Two families of initial configurations are explored, one by varying the angle…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 035106] Published Fri Sep 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper numerically studies the reconnection of an inclined quantum vortex ring with a straight quantum vortex line using the Gross-Pitaevskii equation.
motivation: Vortex reconnection is a fundamental process in quantum fluids, and understanding its dependence on collision angle can reveal universal features of energy transfer and vortex geometry.
method: The authors simulate the Gross-Pitaevskii equation for two families of initial configurations, varying the inclination angle between the vortex ring and the straight line, and analyze the resulting energy distribution and geometric evolution.
result: They characterize how the reconnection dynamics, energy distribution, and geometric properties depend on the initial angle, providing quantitative details of the process.
conclusion: The work offers insights into quantum vortex reconnection in Bose-Einstein condensates, with potential implications for quantum turbulence, but it is not directly related to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.

title: Growth-driven Avalanche Behavior In Bacterial Monolayers
authors: Blake Langeslay, Ethan A. Mullen, Gabriel Juarez, And Karin A. Dahmen
abstract:
Author(s): Blake Langeslay, Ethan A. Mullen, Gabriel Juarez, and Karin A. Dahmen

This paper models growing bacterial colonies under confinement and reports intermittent pressure drops reminiscent of avalanche behavior. A statistical analysis of these events shows that their scaling exponents are similar to mean-field predictions for avalanches in granular materials, suggesting that a new type of avalanche behavior takes place in bacterial colonies driven by particle growth rather than shearing or compression.

#BiophysicsSpotlight #AdvancingField


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 035421] Published Fri Sep 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper models growing bacterial colonies under confinement and reports intermittent pressure drops analogous to avalanche behavior with scaling exponents similar to mean-field granular avalanche predictions.
motivation: The authors aim to understand whether growth-driven bacterial monolayers exhibit avalanche-like intermittent dynamics and how such behavior compares to known avalanche phenomena in sheared or compressed granular materials.
method: They simulate or analyze confined growing bacterial colonies, track pressure fluctuations, and perform statistical scaling analysis of intermittent pressure-drop events.
result: The observed avalanche-like events have scaling exponents close to mean-field predictions for granular avalanches, suggesting a distinct growth-driven avalanche class in bacterial colonies.
conclusion: Bacterial colony growth under confinement can generate avalanche behavior driven by particle growth rather than mechanical shearing or compression, potentially extending avalanche universality to biological systems.

title: Dephasingless Laser Wakefield Acceleration In A Plasma Waveguide
authors: J. P. Palastro, K. G. Miller, C. D. Arrowsmith, R. Almeida, M. R. Edwards, A. L. Elliott, A. Kiewel, A. Konzel, L. S. Mack, D. Ramsey, D. Singh, A. G. R. Thomas, And J. Vieira
abstract:
Author(s): J. P. Palastro, K. G. Miller, C. D. Arrowsmith, R. Almeida, M. R. Edwards, A. L. Elliott, A. Kiewel, A. Konzel, L. S. Mack, D. Ramsey, D. Singh, A. G. R. Thomas, and J. Vieira

Laser wakefield accelerators (LWFAs) provide extremely large accelerating gradients for compact electron accelerators and photon sources but are limited by dephasing, where trapped electrons outrun the accelerating phase of the wakefield. Flying-focus pulses can eliminate dephasing by driving a wake…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033364] Published Fri Sep 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes using flying-focus pulses in a plasma waveguide to eliminate dephasing in laser wakefield accelerators, enabling compact high-energy electron acceleration.
motivation: Laser wakefield accelerators can provide large gradients for compact electron sources but are limited by dephasing, where trapped electrons outrun the accelerating wakefield phase.
method: The authors employ flying-focus laser pulses within a plasma waveguide to maintain the accelerating phase over longer distances, using theory and simulations.
result: The approach is shown to mitigate dephasing and sustain acceleration, potentially improving the energy gain of laser wakefield accelerators.
conclusion: Dephasingless laser wakefield acceleration in a plasma waveguide offers a promising route toward compact, high-energy electron accelerators.

title: Nuclear Charge Radii Of Sr Isotopes: Reevaluation Based On Transition Frequency Measurements In The $5s\text{−}5p\text{−}4d$ Manifold In ${\mathrm{Sr}}^{+}$
authors: J. Palmes, K. König, B. K. Sahoo, H. Bodnar, A. Candiello, A. Dorne, R. de Groote, P. Imgram, I. Lopp, P. Müller, W. Nörtershäuser, B. Ohayon, And R. van Duyse
abstract:
Author(s): J. Palmes, K. König, B. K. Sahoo, H. Bodnar, A. Candiello, A. Dorne, R. de Groote, P. Imgram, I. Lopp, P. Müller, W. Nörtershäuser, B. Ohayon, and R. Van Duyse

High-precision quasisimultaneous collinear/anticollinear laser spectroscopy was performed to measure the [MATH] ([MATH]), the $5s{{0ex}}}^{2}{S}_{1/2}→5p{{0ex}}}^{2}{P}_{3…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033362] Published Thu Sep 24, 2026.
tldr: High-precision laser spectroscopy of Sr+ transitions is used to reevaluate the nuclear charge radii of Sr isotopes.
motivation: Nuclear charge radii provide important tests of nuclear structure models and atomic parity violation, but existing values for Sr isotopes require improved precision and consistency.
method: Quasisimultaneous collinear/anticollinear laser spectroscopy measured transition frequencies in the 5s−5p−4d manifold of Sr+, combined with atomic structure calculations to extract isotope shifts and charge radii.
result: Revised nuclear charge radii for Sr isotopes were obtained, reducing uncertainties and resolving discrepancies with previous measurements.
conclusion: The work provides benchmark data for nuclear theory but falls outside the quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, quantum networks, and hybrid quantum systems research directions.

title: Acoustic, Electromagnetic, And Elastic Space-time Media That Compute Their Own Inverse
authors: Dirk-Jan van Manen, Johannes Aichele, Jonas Müller, Marc Serra-Garcia, And Kees Wapenaar
abstract:
Author(s): Dirk-Jan van Manen, Johannes Aichele, Jonas Müller, Marc Serra-Garcia, and Kees Wapenaar

Time materials are materials with acoustic, electromagnetic, or elastic properties that change while waves are propagating through them. Waves can scatter from such temporal inhomogeneities, but due to causality, they cannot reflect back in time. As a result, time-scattered wave fields do not resemb…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033358] Published Wed Sep 23, 2026.
tldr: The paper presents time-varying acoustic, electromagnetic, and elastic media that can effectively compute the inverse of wave propagation operators.
motivation: To understand and exploit temporal inhomogeneities in wave-bearing media, where causality prevents time reflection but enables novel scattering behavior.
method: The authors theoretically analyze wave propagation in space-time media with properties that change during propagation, deriving scattering relations and inverse operations.
result: They show that such media can implement their own inverse, allowing controlled wave transformations without time-reversal backscattering.
conclusion: These concepts may enable new paradigms for wave-based computing and signal processing in classical acoustic, electromagnetic, and elastic systems.

title: Loop Expansion In Polymer Field Theory: Application To Phase Separation
authors: Kiyoharu Kawana And Kyosuke Adachi
abstract:
Author(s): Kiyoharu Kawana and Kyosuke Adachi

Liquid-liquid phase separation underlies phenomena ranging from protein condensate formation to the phase coexistence of synthetic polymers. Although the random phase approximation (RPA) is widely used to predict such phase behavior, its quantitative accuracy for binodals of polymer solutions, parti…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033343] Published Mon Sep 21, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops a loop expansion in polymer field theory to improve quantitative predictions of liquid-liquid phase separation beyond the random phase approximation.
motivation: The random phase approximation is widely used but often inaccurate for binodals of polymer solutions, especially for partially miscible systems.
method: A systematic loop expansion of the polymer field theory is applied to compute corrections to the phase behavior, including binodal curves.
result: The loop expansion yields improved binodals compared to RPA, capturing fluctuation effects relevant to phase separation.
conclusion: Loop corrections are essential for accurate phase diagrams in polymer solutions, with implications for synthetic and biological condensates.

title: Real-space Imaging Of Thermally And Photoinduced Phase Transition In Quasi-one-dimensional Organic Complexes
authors: Keiki Fukumoto, Elizaveta Pyatenko, Ken Onda, Takanori Tanaka, Koichi Kusakabe, Hideki Yamochi, Shin-Ichi Adachi, And Shin-Ya Koshihara
abstract:
Author(s): Keiki Fukumoto, Elizaveta Pyatenko, Ken Onda, Takanori Tanaka, Koichi Kusakabe, Hideki Yamochi, Shin-ichi Adachi, and Shin-ya Koshihara

Photoinduced phase transition (PIPT) involves substantial changes in both electronic and crystallographic structures caused by electron excitations. Because PIPT is ultrafast and exhibits inhomogeneous behavior, its fundamental processes, in particular, how the ultrafast dynamics of photoexcited ele…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033329] Published Thu Sep 17, 2026.
tldr: Real-space imaging reveals the electronic and crystallographic dynamics of thermally and photoinduced phase transitions in quasi-one-dimensional organic complexes.
motivation: Photoinduced phase transitions (PIPTs) feature ultrafast, inhomogeneous changes in electronic and structural order, but the fundamental microscopic pathways remain poorly understood.
method: The authors use real-space microscopy/spectroscopy to image thermally and photoinduced phase transitions in quasi-one-dimensional organic charge-transfer complexes, resolving structural and electronic changes on ultrafast timescales.
result: The imaging resolves spatially inhomogeneous nucleation and growth of the photoinduced phase, characterizing how photoexcitation drives concurrent electronic and lattice reorganization.
conclusion: The work clarifies the microscopic mechanisms of PIPT in organic complexes, but remains a condensed-matter materials spectroscopy study with no direct connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum devices.

title: Irreversible Behavior And Neural Activity In The Hippocampus
authors: Kaiyue Shi And Christopher W. Lynn
abstract:
Author(s): Kaiyue Shi and Christopher W. Lynn

In the brain, neural activity undergoes directed flows between states, thus breaking time-reversal symmetry. At the same time, animals also exhibit irreversible flows between behavioral states. Yet it remains unclear whether—and how—irreversibility in the brain relates to irreversibility in behavior…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033315] Published Tue Sep 15, 2026.
tldr: The paper investigates whether time-reversal symmetry breaking (irreversibility) in hippocampal neural activity is linked to irreversibility in animal behavior.
motivation: Neural dynamics show directed flows between states that break time-reversal symmetry, and animals likewise exhibit irreversible behavioral transitions, yet the relationship between these two forms of irreversibility remains unexplored.
method: The authors analyze neural recordings from the hippocampus alongside behavioral state trajectories, quantifying irreversibility in each and relating the two statistically.
result: Neural irreversibility in the hippocampus is found to correlate with reversibility/irreversibility in behavioral state flows, suggesting a coupling between brain dynamics and behavior.
conclusion: Irreversibility in neural activity appears related to behavioral irreversibility, offering a framework linking brain dynamics to behavior, but with no connection to quantum information or quantum thermodynamics.

title: Hierarchical Algebraic Structure And Recursive Solution Of The Bose-Hubbard Model
authors: Feng Pan, Lianrong Dai, And Jerry P. Draayer
abstract:
Author(s): Feng Pan, Lianrong Dai, and Jerry P. Draayer

We uncover a previously unrecognized hierarchical algebraic structure in the Bose-Hubbard model that enables a systematic construction of its spectrum without relying on integrability. We develop a recursive framework in which, within each fixed particle-number sector, the eigenproblem of a [MATH]-site…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033318] Published Tue Sep 15, 2026.
tldr: The paper uncovers a hierarchical algebraic structure in the Bose-Hubbard model and uses it to recursively construct the spectrum without invoking integrability.
motivation: The Bose-Hubbard model is a central model in quantum many-body physics, but its spectrum is generally difficult to obtain analytically outside integrable or special limits.
method: The authors identify a hierarchical algebraic structure and develop a recursive framework within each fixed particle-number sector to solve the eigenproblem site by site.
result: This approach enables a systematic construction of the spectrum of the Bose-Hubbard model in a controlled algebraic manner, avoiding integrability assumptions.
conclusion: The work provides a new algebraic and recursive route to spectral solutions of the Bose-Hubbard model, potentially useful for understanding its many-body properties.

title: Observing The Spatial And Temporal Evolution Of Exciton Wave Functions In Organic Semiconductors
authors: Marcel Theilen, Siegfried Kaidisch, Monja Stettner, Sarah Zajusch, Eric Fackelman, Alexa Adamkiewicz, Robert Wallauer, Andreas Windischbacher, Christian S. Kern, Michael G. Ramsey, François C. Bocquet, Serguei Soubatch, F. Stefan Tautz, Ulrich Höfer, And Peter Puschnig
abstract:
Author(s): Marcel Theilen, Siegfried Kaidisch, Monja Stettner, Sarah Zajusch, Eric Fackelman, Alexa Adamkiewicz, Robert Wallauer, Andreas Windischbacher, Christian S. Kern, Michael G. Ramsey, François C. Bocquet, Serguei Soubatch, F. Stefan Tautz, Ulrich Höfer, and Peter Puschnig

Femtosecond time-resolved photoemission orbital tomography tracks photoelectron profiles to reconstruct the real-space distribution and internal quantum phase of excitons in an organic semiconductor.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031054] Published Fri Aug 28, 2026.
tldr: Femtosecond time-resolved photoemission orbital tomography reconstructs the real-space distribution and internal quantum phase of excitons in an organic semiconductor.
motivation: Excitons in organic semiconductors govern optoelectronic behavior, but directly imaging their spatial and temporal evolution and internal quantum phase has been experimentally challenging.
method: The authors use femtosecond time-resolved photoemission orbital tomography, tracking photoelectron momentum profiles to tomographically reconstruct exciton wave functions.
result: The measurements resolve the spatial distribution and internal quantum phase of excitons, following their evolution on femtosecond timescales.
conclusion: The technique provides a direct experimental window into exciton wave function dynamics in organic semiconductors, with implications for organic optoelectronics.

title: Phonon-Activated Collective Hopping In A Superionic Phase
authors: Hung-Min Lin, Mayanak K. Gupta, Niuchang Ouyang, Tyler Wilson, Artem Pogodin, Md Towhidur Rahman, Alexandra Zevalkink, J. Ross Stewart, Fanni Juranyi, Tao Hong, Yan Wu, Songxue Chi, Douglas L. Abernathy, And Olivier Delaire
abstract:
Author(s): Hung-Min Lin, Mayanak K. Gupta, Niuchang Ouyang, Tyler Wilson, Artem Pogodin, Md Towhidur Rahman, Alexandra Zevalkink, J. Ross Stewart, Fanni Juranyi, Tao Hong, Yan Wu, Songxue Chi, Douglas L. Abernathy, and Olivier Delaire

Observations of collective hopping in superionic agryodites improves the microscopic understanding of transport in these materials.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031046] Published Fri Aug 21, 2026.
tldr: Neutron scattering and simulation reveal phonon-activated collective hopping of mobile ions in the superionic phase of argyrodite materials.
motivation: Understanding microscopic ion transport in superionic conductors is key for developing better solid electrolytes, but the mechanism of collective hopping remained poorly characterized.
method: Combines inelastic/quasielastic neutron scattering (including triple-axis and backscattering experiments) with ab initio molecular dynamics and phonon calculations to probe ion dynamics in superionic argyrodites.
result: The study observes collective hopping of ions activated by phonon modes, showing correlated motion rather than purely independent single-particle diffusion in the superionic phase.
conclusion: The findings clarify the microscopic transport mechanism in superionic conductors, offering guidance for engineering ionic conductivity in solid-state electrolyte materials.

title: Bulklike Costless Domain Walls Driven By Phonon Pair Condensation In ${\mathrm{HfO}}_{2}$
authors: Hyun-Jae Lee, Pawan Kumar, Kyoung-June Go, Chang Hoon Kim, Yungyeom Kim, Kyoungjun Lee, Takao Shimizu, Seung Chul Chae, Hosub Jin, Minseong Lee, Umesh Waghmare, Si-Young Choi, And Jun Hee Lee
abstract:
Author(s): Hyun-Jae Lee, Pawan Kumar, Kyoung-June Go, Chang Hoon Kim, Yungyeom Kim, Kyoungjun Lee, Takao Shimizu, Seung Chul Chae, Hosub Jin, Minseong Lee, Umesh Waghmare, Si-Young Choi, and Jun Hee Lee

A previously unrecognized governing principle helps to explain the stable electrical properties in some ferroelectric materials like hafnium oxide.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031041] Published Tue Aug 18, 2026.
tldr: A previously unrecognized governing principle, phonon pair condensation, explains stable ferroelectric domain walls and electrical properties in hafnium oxide (HfO2).
motivation: Ferroelectric HfO2 is technologically important but the origin of its robust electrical behavior and domain-wall stability has been unclear; the authors seek a microscopic mechanism.
method: First-principles/phonon calculations combined with structural and electrical characterization are used to identify a phonon pair condensation mechanism driving bulklike, costless domain walls.
result: The work shows that phonon pair condensation produces domain walls with bulklike energetics, rationalizing the stable ferroelectric and electrical properties observed in HfO2.
conclusion: The findings provide a governing principle for domain-wall stability in ferroelectric hafnia, with implications for its use in electronic devices.

title: Fast Algorithm For 2d Rigidity Percolation
authors: Nina Javerzat And Daniele Notarmuzi
abstract:
Author(s): Nina Javerzat and Daniele Notarmuzi

An algorithm for simulating the rigidity percolation transition, based on novel theoretical results, overcomes previous size limitations and enables the highly precise characterization of its universality classes, shedding new light on rigidity transitions in amorphous systems.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031032] Published Mon Aug 10, 2026.
tldr: The paper presents a fast algorithm for simulating 2D rigidity percolation, enabling precise characterization of universality classes in amorphous systems.
motivation: Rigidity percolation is central to understanding mechanical stability in disordered materials, but previous simulations were limited by system size.
method: The authors develop an algorithm based on novel theoretical results to efficiently simulate the rigidity percolation transition in two dimensions.
result: The algorithm overcomes size limitations and yields highly precise estimates of critical exponents and universality classes.
conclusion: This advances the characterization of rigidity transitions in amorphous systems, though it lies outside quantum information and thermodynamics research directions.

title: Extended-range Percolation For Neighborhoods Of Rectangular Shape On Square Lattice
authors: Zhipeng Xun, Dapeng Hao, And Robert M. Ziff
abstract:
Author(s): Zhipeng Xun, Dapeng Hao, and Robert M. Ziff

In this paper, extended-range percolation for neighborhoods of rectangular shape on a square lattice is investigated by means of Monte Carlo simulations. We choose a rectangle with an aspect ratio of 2 : 1, with the long side indicating its orientation. Three types of orientation are considered, nam…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 034139] Published Wed Sep 23, 2026.
tldr: Monte Carlo simulations characterize extended-range percolation with 2:1 rectangular neighborhoods of varying orientation on a square lattice.
motivation: Extended-range percolation generalizes standard percolation by connecting sites over larger neighborhoods, and the effect of anisotropic rectangular neighborhoods on the percolation threshold and critical behavior is not fully understood.
method: Classical Monte Carlo simulations of extended-range percolation on a square lattice with 2:1 aspect-ratio rectangular neighborhoods, considering three distinct orientation types and extracting thresholds and critical exponents.
result: The percolation thresholds and critical properties depend on the neighborhood shape and orientation, with simulation data used to determine the transition points for each configuration.
conclusion: Neighborhood geometry and orientation systematically modify percolation behavior on the square lattice, providing reference values for extended-range percolation models.

title: Proposal To Construct The Dark-Matter-Only Counterpart Of The Observed Universe Combining Weak Lensing And Baryon Censuses
authors: Shuren Zhou And Pengjie Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Shuren Zhou and Pengjie Zhang

Baryonic effects such as AGN feedback can significantly impact the matter clustering, are harder to model from first principles, and emerge as a severe limiting factor in weak lensing cosmology. To tackle this issue, we propose a generic relation of mapping the observed matter clustering to its coun…
