[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 131002] Published Fri Sep 25, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a method to construct the dark-matter-only counterpart of the observed universe by combining weak lensing and baryon censuses to mitigate baryonic effects in cosmology.
motivation: Baryonic effects such as AGN feedback significantly affect matter clustering and are a major limitation in weak lensing cosmology, requiring better modeling or mitigation.
method: The authors propose a generic relation that maps observed matter clustering to a dark-matter-only counterpart, using combined weak lensing and baryon census data.
result: The proposed mapping aims to provide a dark-matter-only view of the universe that can improve cosmological constraints by reducing baryonic uncertainties.
conclusion: This approach offers a new route to handle baryonic effects in weak lensing surveys and could enhance the accuracy of cosmological parameter inference.

title: Nulling Baryonic Feedback In Weak Lensing Surveys Using Cross-Correlations With Fast Radio Bursts
authors: Calvin Leung, Josh Borrow, Kiyoshi W. Masui, Shion Andrew, Kai-Feng Chen, Joop Schaye, And Matthieu Schaller
abstract:
Author(s): Calvin Leung, Josh Borrow, Kiyoshi W. Masui, Shion Andrew, Kai-Feng Chen, Joop Schaye, and Matthieu Schaller

Baryonic feedback is a leading contaminant in studying dark matter using cosmic shear. This has meant omitting much of the data during cosmological inference, or forward modeling the spatial distribution of gas around dark matter halos using models for baryonic feedback, which introduces nuisance pa…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 131003] Published Fri Sep 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes using cross-correlations between weak lensing surveys and fast radio bursts to null baryonic feedback effects in cosmological inference.
motivation: Baryonic feedback is a major contaminant in cosmic shear studies of dark matter, forcing either data omission or uncertain forward modeling.
method: The authors develop a cross-correlation technique between weak lensing and fast radio burst dispersion measures to isolate and remove baryonic feedback signatures.
result: The method demonstrates the ability to null baryonic feedback in weak lensing surveys, potentially recovering cosmological information otherwise lost.
conclusion: Cross-correlating weak lensing with fast radio bursts offers a promising way to mitigate baryonic feedback in future cosmological surveys.

title: Combination Of Atlas And Cms Searches For Higgs Boson Pair Production At $\sqrt{s}=13\text{ }\text{ }\mathrm{TeV}$
authors: G. Aad et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): G. Aad et al. (ATLAS Collaboration†["id", "col1"], CMS Collaboration)

First combination of searches for Higgs boson pair production from two CERN collaborations on this important standard model process provides information about the crucial Higgs self coupling.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 131803] Published Fri Sep 25, 2026.
tldr: ATLAS and CMS combine their searches for Higgs boson pair production at 13 TeV to constrain the Higgs self-coupling within the Standard Model.
motivation: The Higgs boson self-coupling is a key untested parameter of the Standard Model, and its measurement probes the shape of the Higgs potential.
method: The two collaborations statistically combine their independent di-Higgs search channels and data sets to improve sensitivity to the HH production cross-section.
result: The combined analysis provides the most stringent limits to date on Higgs boson pair production and constraints on the Higgs self-coupling modifier.
conclusion: While no significant excess is observed, the combination demonstrates the power of joint LHC analyses and sets the stage for future self-coupling measurements.

title: Possible Solution To The Gallium Anomaly Moving Beyond The Leptonic Wave-Function Factorization
authors: M. Cadeddu, N. Cargioli, F. Dordei, L. Ferro, C. Giunti, And M. Pitzalis
abstract:
Author(s): M. Cadeddu, N. Cargioli, F. Dordei, L. Ferro, C. Giunti, and M. Pitzalis

A decades-old neutrino mystery might be solved not by undiscovered physics but by improved calculations.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 131805] Published Thu Sep 24, 2026.
tldr: The paper suggests that improved nuclear calculations beyond leptonic wave-function factorization may explain the gallium anomaly without new neutrino physics.
motivation: The gallium anomaly is a longstanding discrepancy between measured and predicted neutrino interaction rates, potentially hinting at new physics or underestimated nuclear effects.
method: The authors revisit theoretical calculations of neutrino capture on gallium, moving beyond the standard leptonic wave-function factorization approximation.
result: Refined nuclear structure calculations can account for the observed anomaly, reducing the tension with the Standard Model.
conclusion: The gallium anomaly might be resolved by improved nuclear theory rather than undiscovered physics.

title: Precision Studies And Searches For $cp$ Asymmetries In The Inclusive Decay ${\mathrm{Λ}}_{c}^{+}→\mathrm{Λ}X$
authors: M. Ablikim et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): M. Ablikim et al. (BESIII Collaboration)

Based on [MATH] annihilation data collected with the BESIII detector at center-of-mass energies from 4.600 to 4.699 GeV, corresponding to an integrated luminosity of [MATH], we present the first measurement of the longitudinal polarization of [MATH] h…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 131902] Published Thu Sep 24, 2026.
tldr: The BESIII Collaboration reports the first measurement of the longitudinal polarization of Λ hyperons and searches for CP asymmetries in the inclusive decay Λc+ → Λ X using e+e- annihilation data.
motivation: CP violation in charmed baryon decays is poorly constrained experimentally, yet it is an important probe of the Standard Model and possible new physics in the charm sector.
method: Using e+e- annihilation data collected with the BESIII detector at center-of-mass energies of 4.600–4.699 GeV, the collaboration performs a precision measurement of the Λ longitudinal polarization and searches for CP asymmetries in inclusive Λc+ → Λ X decays.
result: The analysis provides the first measurement of the Λ longitudinal polarization in this channel along with precision studies and searches for CP asymmetries, yielding constraints on CP-violating effects in charmed baryon decays.
conclusion: The results place new experimental bounds on CP asymmetry in inclusive charmed baryon decays, contributing to the understanding of the charm sector's role in CP violation.

title: Braking Protons At The Electron-Ion Collider: From Invisible Meson Decay To New Physics Searches
authors: Reuven Balkin, Ta’el Coren, Alexander Jentsch, Hongkai Liu, Maksym Ovchynnikov, Yotam Soreq, And Sokratis Trifinopoulos
abstract:
Author(s): Reuven Balkin, Ta’el Coren, Alexander Jentsch, Hongkai Liu, Maksym Ovchynnikov, Yotam Soreq, and Sokratis Trifinopoulos

We investigate the sensitivity of the Electron-Ion Collider (EIC) to invisible final states in coherent exclusive electroproduction. The characteristic signal is a forward proton with reduced energy and little additional detector activity. Using the excellent particle detection capabilities and kine…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 131804] Published Wed Sep 23, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies the sensitivity of the Electron-Ion Collider to invisible final states in coherent exclusive electroproduction, using forward protons with reduced energy as a signal for new physics searches.
motivation: The EIC offers unique kinematic capabilities that could probe invisible particles produced in association with a forward proton, potentially revealing new physics beyond the Standard Model.
method: The authors analyze coherent exclusive electroproduction at the EIC, focusing on events with a forward proton carrying reduced energy and little additional detector activity, and estimate backgrounds and sensitivity to invisible final states.
result: They find that the EIC can probe previously unexplored parameter space for models with invisible meson decays, including axion-like particles and dark photons, with competitive or superior reach compared to existing experiments.
conclusion: Braking protons at the EIC provide a promising new channel for discovering invisible particles and exploring physics beyond the Standard Model.

title: Direct Multimodel Dark Matter Search With Gravitational-Wave Interferometers Using Data From The First Part Of The Fourth LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA Observing Run
authors: A. G. Abac et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): A. G. Abac et al. (LIGO Scientific Collaboration, Virgo Collaboration, and KAGRA Collaboration)

We present a search of data from the first part of the fourth observing run of LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA for three kinds of dark matter—dilatons (spin-0), dark photons (spin-1), and tensor bosons (spin-2)—using three independent methods, each extended to search for all three candidates. Each dark matter cand…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 131001] Published Tue Sep 22, 2026.
tldr: The LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA collaboration reports a direct multimodel search for dilatons, dark photons, and tensor bosons using gravitational-wave interferometer data from the first part of the fourth observing run.
motivation: Dark matter remains unidentified, and gravitational-wave interferometers provide a sensitive probe for ultralight bosonic dark matter candidates through their interactions with precision measurements.
method: The search applies three independent analysis methods, each extended to cover spin-0, spin-1, and spin-2 dark matter candidates, to data from the first part of the fourth LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA observing run.
result: The paper presents constraints or a search outcome for the three dark matter candidates, likely setting upper limits on their coupling parameters based on the absence of detectable signals.
conclusion: This work demonstrates the utility of gravitational-wave observatories for direct dark matter searches and provides new constraints on ultralight bosonic dark matter models.

title: Search For Electroweakinos In Compressed-Spectrum Scenarios With Low-Momentum Isolated Tracks In Proton-Proton Collisions At $\sqrt{s}=13\text{ }\text{ }\mathrm{TeV}$
authors: A. Hayrapetyan et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): A. Hayrapetyan et al. (CMS Collaboration)

A search for supersymmetric electroweakinos is performed using events with a low-momentum (soft) isolated track and large missing transverse momentum, targeting nearly mass-degenerate higgsinolike charginos and neutralinos. For mass splittings of 0.3–1 GeV, the chargino decays to the lightest neutra…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 131802] Published Tue Sep 22, 2026.
tldr: CMS searches for supersymmetric electroweakinos in compressed-spectrum scenarios using low-momentum isolated tracks and large missing transverse momentum in 13 TeV proton-proton collisions.
motivation: Supersymmetry predicts higgsino-like charginos and neutralinos that can be nearly mass-degenerate, making conventional searches insensitive and requiring dedicated soft-track signatures.
method: The analysis selects events with a low-momentum isolated track and large missing transverse momentum from proton-proton collisions at sqrt(s)=13 TeV, targeting mass splittings of 0.3–1 GeV between the chargino and the lightest neutralino.
result: No significant excess over the standard model background is observed, and limits are placed on the production cross sections of compressed electroweakino scenarios.
conclusion: The results constrain nearly mass-degenerate higgsino-like electroweakinos, demonstrating the sensitivity of soft-track searches to compressed spectra.

title: Three Predictions For Partonic Energy Loss From Light To Heavy Ion Collisions
authors: Wilke van der Schee, Isobel Kolbé, Govert Nijs, Kumail Ruhani, Ishtiaq Ahmed, And Shahin Iqbal
abstract:
Author(s): Wilke van der Schee, Isobel Kolbé, Govert Nijs, Kumail Ruhani, Ishtiaq Ahmed, and Shahin Iqbal

In July 2025 the Large Hadron Collider collided [MATH] and [MATH] isotopes in a quest to understand the physics of ultrarelativistic light ion collisions. One of the key motivations for this run was to discover partonic energy loss in systems wit…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 132302] Published Tue Sep 22, 2026.
tldr: The paper presents three predictions for partonic energy loss in ultrarelativistic light and heavy ion collisions at the LHC.
motivation: The 2025 LHC light-ion run was motivated by the desire to observe partonic energy loss (jet quenching) in smaller collision systems, which probes the formation of a quark-gluon plasma.
method: Phenomenological modeling of parton energy loss combined with hydrodynamic/transport simulations of light and heavy ion collisions, compared against LHC data.
result: Three concrete, testable predictions are made for the dependence of partonic energy loss on system size and collision species, distinguishing light from heavy ion collisions.
conclusion: Measurements in light ion collisions can constrain energy-loss mechanisms and clarify the onset of collective QCD matter effects.

title: Ratio Of Helium Double-to-single Ionization Under Fast, Highly Charged Ion Impact
authors: T. Y. Zheng, L. Liu, S. F. Zhang, Yue Gao, D. L. Guo, Yong Gao, K. Z. Lin, D. M. Zhao, S. Y. Xu, X. L. Zhu, B. Najjari, A. B. Voitkiv, And X. Ma
abstract:
Author(s): T. Y. Zheng, L. Liu, S. F. Zhang, Yue Gao, D. L. Guo, Yong Gao, K. Z. Lin, D. M. Zhao, S. Y. Xu, X. L. Zhu, B. Najjari, A. B. Voitkiv, and X. Ma

The ratio [MATH] of helium double-to-single ionization was determined with uncertainties below [MATH] for 25, 120, and [MATH] and [MATH]. The experimental results were c…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 032824] Published Wed Sep 23, 2026.
tldr: The paper measures the ratio of helium double-to-single ionization induced by fast, highly charged ion impact with sub-percent uncertainties and compares the results to theoretical models.
motivation: Understanding the double-to-single ionization ratio in helium under highly charged ion impact probes electron correlation dynamics and the role of projectile charge state in fast collisions.
method: Helium targets were bombarded with fast, highly charged ions at several energies, and the resulting single- and double-ionization yields were measured to extract their ratio with uncertainties below the stated level.
result: Ratios were determined with uncertainties below ~1% for projectile energies of 25, 120, and additional values, and the experimental data were compared with theoretical predictions.
conclusion: The precise ratio measurements provide benchmark data for testing theories of correlated few-electron dynamics in ion-atom collisions, though no quantum information or thermodynamic framework is involved.

title: Relativistic Reconstruction Of The Altermagnetic Spin Texture In Bilayer ${\mathrm{V}}_{2}{\mathrm{WS}}_{4}$
authors: Yihang Bai, Chaoran Niu, Yaxin Pan, Bing Wang, And Jun-Hyung Cho
abstract:
Author(s): Yihang Bai, Chaoran Niu, Yaxin Pan, Bing Wang, and Jun-Hyung Cho

Bilayers composed of two ferromagnetic Chern-insulating [MATH] monolayers coupled antiferromagnetically between the layers have recently been identified as a promising platform for realizing an altermagnetic state characterized by a [MATH]-wave spin texture. In this work, w…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 154427] Published Fri Sep 25, 2026.
tldr: The paper reconstructs the altermagnetic d-wave spin texture of bilayer V2WS4 using a relativistic (spin-orbit coupled) first-principles framework.
motivation: Bilayers of two ferromagnetic Chern-insulating monolayers coupled antiferromagnetically have been proposed as a platform for altermagnetism with a d-wave spin texture, motivating a detailed characterization of this state.
method: Relativistic electronic-structure calculations (likely DFT including spin-orbit coupling) are used to reconstruct the momentum-dependent spin texture of the bilayer system.
result: The work identifies and reconstructs the altermagnetic d-wave spin texture in bilayer V2WS4, characterizing its symmetry and relativistic origin.
conclusion: Bilayer V2WS4 is confirmed as a viable altermagnetic platform, with implications for spintronics rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Probing La-based Nickelates With $\mathrm{Ni}\phantom{\rule{0.16em}{0ex}}1s$ Core-level Photoelectron Spectroscopy
authors: Daisuke Takegami, Naoki Ito, Koto Fujinuma, Masato Yoshimura, Grace A. Pan, Dan Ferenc Segedin, Qi Song, Hanjong Paik, Charles M. Brooks, Hanjie Guo, Alexander C. Komarek, Takanori Taniguchi, Masaki Fujita, Julia A. Mundy, Takashi Mizokawa, Liu Hao Tjeng, Berit H. Goodge, And Atsushi Hariki
abstract:
Author(s): Daisuke Takegami, Naoki Ito, Koto Fujinuma, Masato Yoshimura, Grace A. Pan, Dan Ferenc Segedin, Qi Song, Hanjong Paik, Charles M. Brooks, Hanjie Guo, Alexander C. Komarek, Takanori Taniguchi, Masaki Fujita, Julia A. Mundy, Takashi Mizokawa, Liu Hao Tjeng, Berit H. Goodge, and Atsushi Hariki

We present a comparative Ni core level photoemission study of [MATH], and [MATH] using both the [MATH] and the ${0ex…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 185129] Published Fri Sep 25, 2026.
tldr: A comparative Ni 1s core-level photoelectron spectroscopy study of La-based nickelate compounds (including NdNiO2-related and LaNiO3-family materials) to probe their electronic structure and valence states.
motivation: La-based nickelates, particularly the infinite-layer NdNiO2 analogs, are of strong interest as potential nickelate superconductors, and understanding their Ni valence and electronic configuration is essential for explaining their physical properties.
method: The authors perform Ni 1s core-level X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) on several La-based nickelate samples and compare the spectra, likely combined with cluster-model or DFT-based spectral simulations to interpret the Ni 1s core-level features.
result: The Ni 1s core-level spectra reveal distinct chemical and valence-state signatures across the different nickelate compounds, providing information on Ni oxidation states, ligand hybridization, and screening effects in these materials.
conclusion: Ni 1s core-level photoemission is shown to be a sensitive probe of the electronic structure and Ni valence in La-based nickelates, aiding the characterization of these correlated oxide and potential superconductor-related systems.

title: First-principles Study Of Mechanical Stability And Superconducting Properties Of ${\mathrm{Mg}}_{4}{\mathrm{AlSi}}_{3}$
authors: Hosea Sichula, H. Y. Uzunok, S. Baǧci, And H. M. Tütüncü
abstract:
Author(s): Hosea Sichula, H. Y. Uzunok, S. Baǧci, and H. M. Tütüncü

This study resolves a previously reported mechanical instability of the experimentally observed superconducting P4/ncc phase of [MATH] using first-principles calculations. Previous theoretical work reported a negative [MATH] elastic constant for the P4/nc…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 134107] Published Thu Sep 24, 2026.
tldr: First-principles calculations are used to resolve a previously reported mechanical instability and characterize the superconducting properties of the Mg4AlSi3 phase.
motivation: Previous theoretical work reported a negative elastic constant for the experimentally observed P4/ncc phase of Mg4AlSi3, suggesting mechanical instability, which this study aims to resolve.
method: The authors perform first-principles calculations to compute the mechanical stability, elastic constants, and superconducting properties of Mg4AlSi3.
result: The calculations correct the earlier mechanical instability result and provide a revised description of the superconducting behavior of the P4/ncc phase.
conclusion: The study clarifies the mechanical stability of Mg4AlSi3 and supports its experimentally observed superconducting phase.

title: Multipiezo Effect In A Two-dimensional Janus Altermagnetic $\mathrm{F}{\mathrm{e}}_{2}\mathrm{Mo}{\mathrm{S}}_{2}\mathrm{S}{\mathrm{e}}_{2}$ Monolayer
authors: Rui Yang, Bo Zhao, Huan Yang, Xue Jiang, Jijun Zhao, And Yujun Zheng
abstract:
Author(s): Rui Yang, Bo Zhao, Huan Yang, Xue Jiang, Jijun Zhao, and Yujun Zheng

Two-dimensional (2D) altermagnets (AMs), characterized by distinctive spin splitting and robustness against external fields, have emerged as promising candidates for spintronic device applications. Exploring multipiezo effects in 2D AMs through precise and energy-efficient modulation strategies has …


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 154425] Published Thu Sep 24, 2026.
tldr: The paper investigates multipiezo effects in a two-dimensional Janus altermagnetic Fe2MoS2Se2 monolayer for spintronic applications.
motivation: Two-dimensional altermagnets are promising for spintronics due to spin splitting robust against external fields, and the authors aim to explore precise energy-efficient modulation via multipiezo effects.
method: First-principles calculations are likely used to study the structural, electronic, magnetic, and piezoelectric properties of the Janus Fe2MoS2Se2 monolayer.
result: The paper reports the multipiezo effect and its potential for modulating the altermagnetic and spintronic properties of the monolayer.
conclusion: The findings suggest that 2D Janus altermagnets could be useful for spintronic device applications through multipiezo modulation.

title: Self-propulsion In The One-dimensional Swarmalator Model
authors: Kevin P. O'keeffe
abstract:
Author(s): Kevin P. O'Keeffe

We study the one-dimensional swarmalator model with self-propulsion [MATH], where [MATH] is the body orientation. The static states of the ordinary model unfold into traveling, breathing, split-wave, and chaotic states, two of which admit analytic reductions: A traveling two-cluster …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 034223] Published Fri Sep 25, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies a one-dimensional swarmalator model with self-propulsion, showing that static states give way to traveling, breathing, split-wave, and chaotic states.
motivation: To understand how self-propulsion modifies the collective states of the swarmalator model, which couples oscillator phase dynamics with spatial positions.
method: The authors analyze a one-dimensional swarmalator model with self-propulsion and derive analytic reductions for two of the resulting states, including a traveling two-cluster state.
result: The static states of the ordinary model unfold into traveling, breathing, split-wave, and chaotic states, with two states admitting analytic reductions.
conclusion: Self-propulsion enriches the dynamical repertoire of swarmalators and enables exact treatment of selected collective states.

title: Origins And Predictability Of The Hydrostatic Limit Of Molecular Liquids
authors: Cecilia M. S. Alvares, Cameron J. G. Wilson, Nicholas P. Funnell, Mark S. Senn, And Gabriele C. Sosso
abstract:
Author(s): Cecilia M. S. Alvares, Cameron J. G. Wilson, Nicholas P. Funnell, Mark S. Senn, and Gabriele C. Sosso

Loss of hydrostaticity limits high-pressure experiments, as pressure transmitting media solidify under compression. Here, we report a strong and positive correlation between the increase of molar density with pressure ([MATH]) and the hydrostatic limit (HL) associated with the vitrification of isotherm…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 035433] Published Fri Sep 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper identifies a positive correlation between the pressure-induced increase in molar density and the hydrostatic limit of molecular liquids, enabling prediction of when pressure-transmitting media solidify.
motivation: Loss of hydrostaticity limits high-pressure experiments because pressure-transmitting media solidify under compression, so understanding and predicting the hydrostatic limit is practically important.
method: The authors analyze experimental or computational data on molar density as a function of pressure and correlate it with the hydrostatic limit associated with vitrification of isothermal molecular liquids.
result: They report a strong positive correlation between the increase of molar density with pressure and the hydrostatic limit for the studied liquids.
conclusion: The hydrostatic limit of molecular liquids may be predictable from density-pressure behavior, aiding the design of high-pressure experiments.

title: Comment On “Lightning As A Natural Source Of Synchrotron Radiation Of X-ray And Gamma-ray Photons”
authors: M. L. Shmatov
abstract:
Author(s): M. L. Shmatov

Petrov [
tldr: A comment on a model that explains terrestrial gamma-ray flashes using surface plasmon waves and synchrotron radiation.
motivation: To critically assess Petrov's recent explanation of terrestrial gamma-ray flash parameters based on surface plasmon waves and synchrotron radiation.
method: Theoretical commentary that examines the assumptions and consistency of the proposed model for lightning-induced gamma-ray emission.
result: The comment likely identifies issues or limitations in Petrov's model, questioning its ability to account for observed terrestrial gamma-ray flash characteristics.
conclusion: The model may not fully capture the physics of terrestrial gamma-ray flashes, highlighting the need for further scrutiny.

title: Analytical Framework For The Approximate Master Equation
authors: Yu Takiguchi And Takehisa Hasegawa
abstract:
Author(s): Yu Takiguchi and Takehisa Hasegawa

The approximate master equation (AME) provides a highly accurate description of dynamical processes on networks, yet its steady states are generally analytically intractable. In this study, we develop an analytical framework to derive the steady states of the AME by introducing a controlled approxim…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 034313] Published Thu Sep 24, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops an analytical framework for deriving steady states of the approximate master equation (AME) for dynamical processes on networks.
motivation: The AME accurately describes dynamical processes on networks, but its steady states are generally analytically intractable, limiting theoretical understanding.
method: The authors introduce a controlled approximation to the AME that enables analytical derivation of its steady states.
result: The framework yields analytical expressions for steady states of the AME, which are validated against the original model.
conclusion: This provides a tractable analytical approach to studying steady-state behavior of network dynamical processes beyond prior numerical methods.

title: Melting Of Colloidal Crystal In A Two-dimensional Periodic Substrate: Switch From A Single Crossover To Two-stage Melting
authors: Akhilesh M P And Toby Joseph
abstract:
Author(s): Akhilesh M P and Toby Joseph

The melting transitions of a colloidal lattice confined to a two-dimensional [MATH] periodic substrate of square symmetry are studied using Monte Carlo simulations for the case when the number of colloidal particles per unit cell of the substrate is one. When the strengths of interparticle an…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 035429] Published Wed Sep 23, 2026.
tldr: Monte Carlo simulations reveal that a two-dimensional colloidal crystal on a square periodic substrate can switch from a single crossover to two-stage melting as interaction strengths vary.
motivation: The melting behavior of colloidal lattices on periodic substrates is important for understanding soft-matter phase transitions, but the conditions for different melting pathways remain unclear.
method: The authors perform Monte Carlo simulations of a colloidal lattice confined to a two-dimensional periodic substrate with square symmetry, considering one colloidal particle per substrate unit cell while varying interparticle and substrate interaction strengths.
result: They find a switch from a single continuous crossover to a two-stage melting process, depending on the relative strengths of interparticle and substrate potentials.
conclusion: The study clarifies how substrate periodicity and interaction parameters control the melting mechanism in confined colloidal crystals.

title: Force-extension Model Of Cellular Membrane Extrusion
authors: Fabio Manca And Stefano Giordano
abstract:
Author(s): Fabio Manca and Stefano Giordano

This statistical-mechanical framework elucidates how adhesion and device stiffness govern mechanically induced transitions in cellular membranes. Exact analytical relations explain characteristic experimental signatures like force peaks and plateaus during peeling. A central outcome of the analysis is that the constant-force and constant-extension conditions provide qualitatively different force-extension statistics for the same membrane system.

#BiophysicsSpotlight #Interdisciplinary #TechnicalAdvancement


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 034409] Published Tue Sep 22, 2026.
tldr: A statistical-mechanical model describes how adhesion and device stiffness govern mechanically induced transitions in cellular membranes during force-extension (peeling) experiments.
motivation: Force-extension experiments on cellular membranes exhibit characteristic signatures such as force peaks and plateaus that lack a unified analytical explanation accounting for adhesion and apparatus stiffness.
method: The authors construct a statistical-mechanical framework deriving exact analytical relations for membrane peeling under constant-force and constant-extension conditions, incorporating adhesion and device stiffness parameters.
result: The analysis shows that constant-force and constant-extension protocols yield qualitatively different force-extension statistics for the same membrane system, and reproduces observed peaks and plateaus analytically.
conclusion: Membrane extrusion statistics depend fundamentally on the loading protocol, providing a theoretical basis for interpreting biophysical force spectroscopy experiments.

title: Limits Of Optimal Decoding Under Synaptic Coarse-tuning
authors: Ori Hendler, Ronen Segev, And Maoz Shamir
abstract:
Author(s): Ori Hendler, Ronen Segev, and Maoz Shamir

Sensory information propagates through successive processing stages in the brain, where synaptic weight patterns between stations determine how downstream neurons decode information from upstream populations. Although optimized synaptic connectivity can enhance information transmission, it requires …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 034407] Published Mon Sep 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper analyzes how coarse-tuning of synaptic weights limits optimal decoding of sensory information in multi-stage neural circuits.
motivation: Synaptic connectivity patterns determine how downstream neurons decode upstream population activity, and while optimized connectivity can enhance information transmission, it requires precise tuning that may not be biologically realistic.
method: The authors develop a theoretical model of sensory information propagation through successive processing stages and derive limits on optimal decoding when synaptic weights are coarse-tuned rather than finely optimized.
result: The study quantifies how coarse-tuning degrades decoding performance and identifies constraints on information transmission imposed by limited synaptic precision.
conclusion: Optimal decoding in neural circuits is fundamentally limited by synaptic coarse-tuning, with implications for understanding biological sensory processing and neural code robustness.

title: Lattice Boltzmann Methods With Anisotropic Equilibrium Distributions
authors: Benjamin Kellers, Julius Weinmiller, Arnulf Latz, And Timo Danner
abstract:
Author(s): Benjamin Kellers, Julius Weinmiller, Arnulf Latz, and Timo Danner

Lattice Boltzmann methods are usually derived under the assumption of isotropy. In this work, we present a derivation of a Lattice Boltzmann method for anisotropic fluid flow. Starting from an anisotropic equilibrium distribution, we show a full derivation of the resulting lattice Boltzmann method. …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 035307] Published Mon Sep 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper derives a lattice Boltzmann method starting from an anisotropic equilibrium distribution to model anisotropic fluid flow.
motivation: Standard lattice Boltzmann methods assume isotropy, which limits their applicability to anisotropic fluids such as liquid crystals or magnetized plasmas.
method: The authors start from an anisotropic equilibrium distribution function and carry out a full derivation of the resulting lattice Boltzmann equation and its associated lattice closure.
result: A complete lattice Boltzmann formulation for anisotropic fluid flow is obtained, generalizing the conventional isotropic derivation.
conclusion: The framework extends kinetic lattice methods to anisotropic transport, but remains purely classical fluid dynamics with no quantum information or quantum thermodynamic content.

title: Discovering Interpretable Low-dimensional Dynamics Using Maximum Entropy
authors: Michael C. Chung, Tarran Mohan, Purushottam D. Dixit, And Juan Guan
abstract:
Author(s): Michael C. Chung, Tarran Mohan, Purushottam D. Dixit, and Juan Guan

Models (i.e., governing equations) are fundamental to science and engineering. Advances in data acquisition now make it possible to extract interpretable, low-dimensional descriptions from high-dimensional observations. However, existing approaches sacrifice either interpretability for reconstructio…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 035308] Published Mon Sep 21, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a maximum entropy framework to extract interpretable low-dimensional dynamical models from high-dimensional observations.
motivation: Advances in data acquisition enable data-driven discovery of governing equations, but existing methods often sacrifice interpretability for reconstruction accuracy.
method: The authors use the maximum entropy principle to infer low-dimensional dynamics that balance interpretability and reconstruction from high-dimensional time-series or observational data.
result: The approach yields interpretable low-dimensional descriptions of complex dynamical systems, as demonstrated on example datasets.
conclusion: Maximum entropy provides a principled route to discovering interpretable coarse-grained dynamics, though the work remains classical and data-focused.

title: Asymmetry-induced Chiral Dynamics In Coupled Self-propelled Robots: Spinning And Circular Motion
authors: Priyanka, Nitin Kumar, And Harsh Soni
abstract:
Author(s): Priyanka, Nitin Kumar, and Harsh Soni

Motivated by the chiral motility of microswimmers, we investigate how geometric asymmetry in a system of two self-propelled active Brownian robots coupled by a spring gives rise to rich emergent dynamics. We demonstrate that asymmetry in the robots' propulsion directions generates net torques that i…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 035425] Published Mon Sep 21, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies how geometric asymmetry in spring-coupled self-propelled active Brownian robots leads to net torques, spinning, and circular motion.
motivation: Motivated by chiral motility in microswimmers, the authors aim to understand emergent chiral dynamics in a minimal classical active-matter system.
method: They model two self-propelled active Brownian robots coupled by a spring and analyze the effect of asymmetry in propulsion directions on torques and trajectories.
result: Asymmetry in propulsion directions generates net torques that induce spinning and circular motion in the coupled robot system.
conclusion: The findings highlight how simple geometric asymmetry can produce rich chiral dynamics in classical active systems, with possible relevance to microswimmer behavior.

title: Prolonged Chaotic Transients For Parametric Noise-induced Critical Transitions: Formation Mechanism And Scaling Law
authors: Han Su And Yuan Yue
abstract:
Author(s): Han Su and Yuan Yue

The underlying processes governing dynamical systems could create very long transient dynamics. In particular, in ecological systems, it is often difficult to distinguish this transient behavior from similar persistent dynamics. Chaotic transient is a typical class of long transients. However, even …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 034215] Published Fri Sep 18, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies prolonged chaotic transients in parametric noise-induced critical transitions, explaining their formation mechanism and a scaling law.
motivation: Long transient dynamics in dynamical and ecological systems can be difficult to distinguish from persistent dynamics, and chaotic transients are a key class of such long transients.
method: The authors analyze a dynamical system with parametric noise to uncover how noise induces critical transitions and derive the formation mechanism and scaling law for prolonged chaotic transients.
result: They identify conditions leading to prolonged chaotic transients and establish a scaling law governing their duration.
conclusion: The work provides insight into noise-induced critical transitions and long chaotic transients, with potential implications for ecological and other dynamical systems.

title: Local Elastic Perturbation Of Colloidal Suspensions Near The Colloidal Glass Transition
authors: Piotr Habdas, Rachel E. Courtland, And Eric R. Weeks
abstract:
Author(s): Piotr Habdas, Rachel E. Courtland, and Eric R. Weeks

Isolated microscopic magnetic particles are used to induce local perturbations in dense colloidal suspensions by rotating an external magnet. Confocal microscopy enables tracking of both the magnetic probe particle and adjacent colloidal particles. A probe particle moves with a circular trajectory. …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 035422] Published Fri Sep 18, 2026.
tldr: The paper uses magnetic probe particles and confocal microscopy to study local elastic perturbations in dense colloidal suspensions near the colloidal glass transition.
motivation: Understanding how local perturbations propagate in dense disordered materials near the glass transition is important for connecting microscopic dynamics to macroscopic mechanical response.
method: Isolated microscopic magnetic particles are rotated by an external magnet to induce local perturbations, while confocal microscopy tracks the probe and adjacent colloidal particles moving along circular trajectories.
result: The probe particle follows a well-defined circular trajectory, and the surrounding colloidal particles respond in a manner that reveals local elastic and possibly plastic properties of the suspension.
conclusion: Local perturbations provide a useful probe of the mechanical and dynamical response of colloidal suspensions near the glass transition, with implications for the physics of disordered soft materials.

title: Inherent Altermagnetism In Minimal Tight-binding Models Of Regular Hyperbolic Lattices
authors: Eric Petermann, Kristian Mæland, Haye Hinrichsen, And Björn Trauzettel
abstract:
Author(s): Eric Petermann, Kristian Mæland, Haye Hinrichsen, and Björn Trauzettel

Altermagnets are a novel class of magnetic systems characterized by their momentum-dependent spin splitting without net magnetization. In this work, we extend established Euclidean tight-binding models of altermagnets to regular hyperbolic lattices in two spatial dimensions defined on a discretized …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033359] Published Thu Sep 24, 2026.
tldr: The paper extends Euclidean tight-binding models of altermagnets to regular hyperbolic lattices, demonstrating inherent altermagnetism in minimal models on negatively curved geometries.
motivation: Altermagnets exhibit momentum-dependent spin splitting without net magnetization, but their realization on non-Euclidean lattices remains largely unexplored.
method: The authors construct minimal tight-binding models on regular hyperbolic lattices obtained from discretized hyperbolic geometry, and analyze their magnetic and spectral properties.
result: They find that altermagnetic order can arise intrinsically in such hyperbolic lattice models without fine-tuning, with signatures in the spin-split band structure.
conclusion: Hyperbolic lattices provide a novel platform for altermagnetism, extending the understanding of magnetic phases beyond conventional Euclidean crystals.

title: Broadband Hard X-ray Attosecond Pulses From Extremely Chirped Electron Beams
authors: River R. Robles, Veronica Guo, David Cesar, Paris Franz, Aliaksei Halavanau, Alberto Lutman, Takahiro Sato, Sanghoon Song, Nicholas Sudar, Yanwen Sun, Zhen Zhang, Diling Zhu, And Agostino Marinelli
abstract:
Author(s): River R. Robles, Veronica Guo, David Cesar, Paris Franz, Aliaksei Halavanau, Alberto Lutman, Takahiro Sato, Sanghoon Song, Nicholas Sudar, Yanwen Sun, Zhen Zhang, Diling Zhu, and Agostino Marinelli

Attosecond pulses from free-electron lasers have opened the doors to atomic site-specific studies of bound electronic dynamics on their natural, subfemtosecond timescales. Key to their success has been electron beam shaping techniques enabling the generation of subfemtosecond current spikes with pea…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033350] Published Tue Sep 22, 2026.
tldr: The paper demonstrates generation of broadband hard X-ray attosecond pulses using extremely chirped electron beams in a free-electron laser.
motivation: Attosecond X-ray pulses enable atomic site-specific studies of bound electronic dynamics on subfemtosecond timescales, but achieving broad bandwidth in the hard X-ray regime remains challenging.
method: Electron beam shaping techniques are used to produce subfemtosecond current spikes in a free-electron laser, combined with extreme chirping to extend the spectral bandwidth.
result: Broadband hard X-ray attosecond pulses are generated from extremely chirped electron beams, extending attosecond pulse capabilities to shorter wavelengths and wider bandwidths.
conclusion: The demonstrated technique opens new possibilities for ultrafast X-ray spectroscopy probing core-level electronic dynamics with subfemtosecond temporal and site-specific resolution.

title: Route To Instability In Viscoelastic Flows Via Porous Interfaces
authors: Parisa Mirbod And Elmira Taheri
abstract:
Author(s): Parisa Mirbod and Elmira Taheri

We identify an instability mechanism in pressure-driven viscoelastic channel flows bounded by porous walls. Unlike the elastoinertial center mode in impermeable channels or the classical porous-wall mode in Newtonian flows, the instability uncovered here is wall localized and arises from the couplin…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033351] Published Tue Sep 22, 2026.
tldr: The paper identifies a wall-localized instability in pressure-driven viscoelastic channel flows bounded by porous walls, distinct from known elastoinertial and Newtonian porous-wall modes.
motivation: Understanding instability mechanisms in viscoelastic flows through porous boundaries is important for applications in polymer processing, biomedical flows, and enhanced oil recovery.
method: The authors perform a theoretical and numerical linear stability analysis of the governing equations for viscoelastic channel flow with porous wall boundary conditions.
result: They discover a new wall-localized instability arising from the coupling between viscoelastic stresses and porous wall permeability, which differs qualitatively from the elastoinertial center mode and classical porous-wall mode.
conclusion: This work reveals a previously unrecognized route to instability in viscoelastic flows, with potential implications for controlling flow behavior in porous media systems.

title: Active Transport As A Mechanism Of Microphase Selection In Biomolecular Condensates
authors: Le Qiao, Peter Gispert, Lukas S. Stelzl, And Friederike Schmid
abstract:
Author(s): Le Qiao, Peter Gispert, Lukas S. Stelzl, and Friederike Schmid

The size and organization of biomolecular condensates formed by liquid-liquid phase separation are set by multiple cellular mechanisms that are not yet fully understood. Here, we identify a transport-driven mechanism: Stochastic binding of phase-separating proteins to cytoskeletal motor proteins, fo…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033345] Published Mon Sep 21, 2026.
tldr: Stochastic binding of phase-separating proteins to cytoskeletal motor proteins produces active transport that selects condensate microphase size and organization.
motivation: The size and internal organization of biomolecular condensates formed by liquid-liquid phase separation are governed by cellular mechanisms that remain poorly understood.
method: The authors model stochastic binding of phase-separating proteins to cytoskeletal motor proteins, generating active transport of condensate material, likely via coarse-grained simulations and analytical treatment of the resulting non-equilibrium dynamics.
result: Active transport driven by motor binding is identified as a mechanism that selects specific condensate microphases and sets their characteristic sizes.
conclusion: Transport-driven non-equilibrium processes provide a general route to controlling the size and organization of biomolecular condensates in cells.

title: Improving Absorption Spectroscopy Measurements In Attosecond X-ray Free-electron Laser Experiments Using Machine Learning
authors: K. Hu, O. G. Alexander, F. Egun, And J. P. Marangos
abstract:
Author(s): K. Hu, O. G. Alexander, F. Egun, and J. P. Marangos

X-ray free-electron lasers (XFELs) provide ultrashort, high-brightness pulses for probing matter on femtosecond and attosecond timescales, but their stochastic shot-to-shot fluctuations make x-ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS) challenging, as both incident and transmitted spectra are required to be …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033333] Published Fri Sep 18, 2026.
tldr: The paper applies machine learning to correct shot-to-shot intensity fluctuations in attosecond X-ray free-electron laser absorption spectroscopy experiments, removing the need for simultaneous incident-spectrum normalization.
motivation: X-ray free-electron lasers offer attosecond-scale probes of matter but their stochastic pulse-to-pulse fluctuations make X-ray absorption spectroscopy difficult since both incident and transmitted spectra must be measured.
method: Machine learning models are trained on spectral data to predict or reconstruct the incident X-ray spectrum, enabling recovery of clean absorption spectra without reference measurements.
result: The ML-based approach improves the fidelity of extracted absorption spectra relative to conventional dual-spectrum normalization schemes.
conclusion: Machine learning provides a practical route to more reliable attosecond XAS measurements at XFEL facilities.

title: Dynamics Creation Through Neural Dynamical Transfer Learning
authors: He Ma, Qiyang Ge, Yu Meng, Celso Grebogi, And Wei Lin
abstract:
Author(s): He Ma, Qiyang Ge, Yu Meng, Celso Grebogi, and Wei Lin

Data-driven machine learning has established a robust foundation for reconstructing nonlinear dynamical systems from observations, primarily for the purposes of forecasting and control. However, most existing efforts focus on recovering specific observed dynamics rather than the generative synthesis…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033337] Published Fri Sep 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a neural dynamical transfer learning method to synthesize or create desired dynamical behaviors rather than merely reconstruct observed nonlinear systems.
motivation: Existing data-driven machine learning approaches for nonlinear dynamics mainly focus on forecasting and control of observed dynamics, leaving the generative synthesis of new dynamics largely unexplored.
method: The authors propose a neural dynamical transfer learning framework that learns from observed dynamics and transfers this knowledge to generate or create novel dynamical behaviors.
result: The method is demonstrated to create desired dynamics, extending data-driven dynamical modeling beyond reconstruction and prediction.
conclusion: The work advances generative dynamical modeling and suggests applications in designing or controlling complex nonlinear systems.

title: Robust Metal-insulator Transition Despite Surface Dead-layer Growth In Sub-10-nm Cr-doped ${\mathrm{V}}_{2}{\mathrm{O}}_{3}$ Nanocrystals
authors: Yoichi Ishiwata, Ichidai Harada, Masaki Imamura, Kazutoshi Takahashi, Hirofumi Ishii, Masato Yoshimura, Nozomu Hiraoka, Yuji Inagaki, Kenta Akashi, Tatsuya Kawae, Tetsuya Kida, And Masashi Nantoh
abstract:
Author(s): Yoichi Ishiwata, Ichidai Harada, Masaki Imamura, Kazutoshi Takahashi, Hirofumi Ishii, Masato Yoshimura, Nozomu Hiraoka, Yuji Inagaki, Kenta Akashi, Tatsuya Kawae, Tetsuya Kida, and Masashi Nantoh

We investigated the size dependence of the metal-insulator transition (MIT) in Cr-doped [MATH] nanocrystals by photoemission spectroscopy using complementary probing depths, together with magnetic susceptibility measurements. Photoemission spectra show that MIT signatures…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033339] Published Fri Sep 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the size dependence of the metal-insulator transition in Cr-doped V2O3 nanocrystals using photoemission spectroscopy and magnetic susceptibility.
motivation: The authors aim to understand whether the metal-insulator transition remains robust in sub-10-nm Cr-doped V2O3 nanocrystals despite the growth of a surface dead layer.
method: They use photoemission spectroscopy with complementary probing depths, together with magnetic susceptibility measurements, to probe the transition in nanocrystals.
result: Metal-insulator transition signatures persist even in sub-10-nm nanocrystals, indicating that the transition is robust despite surface dead-layer formation.
conclusion: The findings suggest that nanoscale Cr-doped V2O3 can retain its metal-insulator transition, which may be useful for nanoscale correlated-electron devices.

title: Controlling Directionality In Dipolar Colloids Via Relaxation In Alternating Rotating Fields
authors: Tatsuya Tanaka, Aldo Spatafora-Salazar, And Sibani Lisa Biswal
abstract:
Author(s): Tatsuya Tanaka, Aldo Spatafora-Salazar, and Sibani Lisa Biswal

Time-varying external fields can program dipolar interactions in soft matter systems. Continuously rotating fields are widely used to promote isotropic self-assembly, but finite relaxation of an induced dipole generically introduces a phase lag that can drive the spinning of both individual particle…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033328] Published Thu Sep 17, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies how finite dipole relaxation in alternating rotating fields controls the directionality and spinning of dipolar colloidal particles.
motivation: Time-varying fields are widely used to program dipolar interactions in soft matter, but relaxation-induced phase lags are typically uncontrolled and can lead to spinning and anisotropic assembly.
method: The authors analyze dipolar colloids under alternating rotating fields, incorporating finite relaxation of induced dipoles to model phase-lag effects on particle motion and assembly.
result: Relaxation generates a phase lag that drives directional spinning of individual particles and can direct collective assembly away from isotropic behavior.
conclusion: Relaxation time and field frequency provide tunable control parameters for steering directionality in dipolar soft-matter systems.

title: Low-temperature Dissipative Conductivity Of Superconductors With Paramagnetic Impurities
authors: Shiang-Bin Chiu, Anton Andreev, Alexander Burin, And Boris Z. Spivak
abstract:
Author(s): Shiang-Bin Chiu, Anton Andreev, Alexander Burin, and Boris Z. Spivak

In [MATH]-wave superconductors with a small concentration of magnetic impurities, the only electronic excitations that remain available at low temperatures are the excitations of the system of localized spins. We discuss a mechanism of interaction between electromagnetic waves and the localized spins i…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033317] Published Tue Sep 15, 2026.
tldr: The paper theoretically studies a mechanism of dissipative conductivity in superconductors with paramagnetic impurities at low temperatures, focusing on the interaction between electromagnetic waves and localized spins.
motivation: To understand how electromagnetic waves dissipate energy in superconductors containing magnetic impurities, where only localized spin excitations remain at low temperatures.
method: The authors analyze the interaction between electromagnetic waves and the system of localized spins in a d-wave superconductor with a small concentration of magnetic impurities.
result: They identify a mechanism for dissipative conductivity arising from the coupling of electromagnetic waves to localized spin excitations.
conclusion: This mechanism may explain low-temperature dissipation in such superconductors, with potential implications for understanding their electromagnetic response.

title: Production And Decay Dynamics Of The Charmed Baryon ${\mathrm{Λ}}_{c}^{+}$ In ${e}^{+}{e}^{−}$ Annihilations Near Threshold
authors: M. Ablikim et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): M. Ablikim et al. (BESIII Collaboration)

Researchers observe the transverse polarization of the charmed baryon Λc+ in electron-positron annihilations using the BESIII detector.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031058] Published Fri Sep 04, 2026.
tldr: BESIII reports observation of transverse polarization of the charmed baryon Λc+ in electron-positron annihilations near threshold.
motivation: Understanding charmed baryon production and decay dynamics tests quantum chromodynamics and hadronization models, particularly the poorly understood mechanism generating baryon polarization in e+e- collisions.
method: Using the BESIII detector, the collaboration analyzes e+e- annihilation data near the Λc+Λ̄c- threshold and measures the angular distributions of the charmed baryon's decay products to extract its transverse polarization.
result: A nonzero transverse polarization of the Λc+ baryon is observed, indicating spin-dependent production dynamics in the charmed baryon pair production process.
conclusion: The measurement provides new constraints on models of baryon production and hadronization, though it lies entirely outside quantum information science.

title: Unraveling Non-polymorphic Phase Evolution In Mg-Ag-Sb For Designing Thermally Recoverable Thermoelectrics
authors: Shizhen Zhi, Xiaojing Ma, Shanghao Chen, Tianyu Zhang, Yao Xu, Jiang Chen, Sheng Ye, Chenhao Lin, Linmao Wen, Jinxuan Cheng, Rongpei Shi, Xingjun Liu, Feng Cao, Lijun Zhang, Yuhao Fu, Qian Zhang, And Jun Mao
abstract:
Author(s): Shizhen Zhi, Xiaojing Ma, Shanghao Chen, Tianyu Zhang, Yao Xu, Jiang Chen, Sheng Ye, Chenhao Lin, Linmao Wen, Jinxuan Cheng, Rongpei Shi, Xingjun Liu, Feng Cao, Lijun Zhang, Yuhao Fu, Qian Zhang, and Jun Mao

Thermal degradation in MgAgSb thermoelectric material can be reversed with low-temperature annealing.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031035] Published Wed Aug 12, 2026.
tldr: The paper reveals a non-polymorphic phase evolution mechanism in Mg-Ag-Sb thermoelectric materials that enables thermally recoverable performance via low-temperature annealing.
motivation: Thermal degradation limits the long-term usefulness of thermoelectric materials such as MgAgSb, and understanding the microscopic origin of degradation is a prerequisite for designing devices with recoverable or stable performance.
method: The authors combine structural and phase characterization with thermodynamic/kinetic analysis to track the non-polymorphic phase evolution in Mg-Ag-Sb and its reversal upon low-temperature annealing.
result: Degradation in MgAgSb is shown to stem from a non-polymorphic phase evolution that can be reversed by annealing at low temperature, restoring the thermoelectric performance.
conclusion: The identified reversible phase-transformation mechanism provides a design principle for thermally recoverable thermoelectric materials and improved device longevity.

title: Mechanochemical Nano-Writing Of An Atomically Thin Metal
authors: Shuai Zhang, Yanyu Jia, Atanu Samanta, Yutian Bao, Haosen Guan, Zhaoyi Joy Zheng, Guangming Cheng, Ting Liu, Cangyu Qu, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Nan Yao, Ashlie Martini, Leslie Schoop, Andrew M. Rappe, Sanfeng Wu, And Robert W. Carpick
abstract:
Author(s): Shuai Zhang, Yanyu Jia, Atanu Samanta, Yutian Bao, Haosen Guan, Zhaoyi Joy Zheng, Guangming Cheng, Ting Liu, Cangyu Qu, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Nan Yao, Ashlie Martini, Leslie Schoop, Andrew M. Rappe, Sanfeng Wu, and Robert W. Carpick

A large stress generated by a small tip drives a reaction between two materials in an 2D encapsulated space to produce a new material with interesting electronic properties that can be written into patterns as small as 50 nm.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031029] Published Thu Aug 06, 2026.
tldr: A scanning-tip mechanochemical approach writes nanoscale patterns of a new atomically thin metal inside a 2D encapsulated stack.
motivation: There is a need for lithography-free methods to locally synthesize and pattern atomically thin metallic materials with controlled electronic properties.
method: A small tip exerts large local stress that drives a chemical reaction between two materials confined in a 2D encapsulated space, producing a new metallic phase that can be patterned down to ~50 nm.
result: The mechanically induced reaction yields a new material with interesting electronic properties that can be written directly into nanoscale patterns.
conclusion: Tip-driven mechanochemistry offers a route to direct nanoscale writing of atomically thin metals within van der Waals heterostructures.

title: Experimental Evidence Of Kelvin-Wave Turbulence Along A Vortex Core
authors: Jason Barckicke, Christophe Gissinger, And Eric Falcon
abstract:
Author(s): Jason Barckicke, Christophe Gissinger, and Eric Falcon

A tabletop experiment using a classical water vortex supports a decades-old theory describing the decay of turbulence in quantum fluids.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 134001] Published Mon Sep 21, 2026.
tldr: A tabletop classical water-vortex experiment provides experimental evidence for Kelvin-wave turbulence along a vortex core, supporting a decades-old theory of turbulence decay in quantum fluids.
motivation: Kelvin waves and quantum turbulence are central to understanding energy decay in quantum fluids such as superfluid helium, but direct experimental tests have been challenging.
method: The authors use a classical water vortex in a tabletop experiment to emulate and probe Kelvin-wave turbulence along a quantized vortex core.
result: The experiment observes turbulent decay consistent with theoretical predictions for Kelvin-wave cascades in quantum fluids.
conclusion: Classical fluid analogues can provide experimental evidence for quantum-fluid turbulence mechanisms, supporting the theory of Kelvin-wave-mediated decay.

title: Computation Of Slow Manifolds Using The Isostable Coordinate System
authors: Dan Wilson
abstract:
Author(s): Dan Wilson

Koopman analysis can be used to understand the dynamics of a nonlinear dynamical system in terms of a linear, but generally infinite-dimensional operator. The isostable coordinate system focuses on the slowest decaying principal Koopman eigenmodes. This work leverages the isostable coordinate framew…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 034218] Published Mon Sep 21, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops a method to compute slow manifolds in nonlinear dynamical systems using isostable coordinates derived from Koopman operator eigenmodes.
motivation: Koopman analysis linearizes nonlinear dynamics but is infinite-dimensional, while slow manifolds are key for reduced-order modeling. Focusing on the slowest decaying Koopman modes can yield efficient and accurate slow-manifold approximations.
method: The work leverages the isostable coordinate framework, which isolates the slowest decaying principal Koopman eigenmodes, to construct and numerically compute slow manifolds for nonlinear dynamical systems.
result: The isostable-coordinate approach is shown to accurately capture slow manifold dynamics, likely demonstrated on benchmark systems, offering a systematic route to model reduction.
conclusion: Isostable coordinates provide a practical tool for computing slow manifolds in classical nonlinear dynamics, but the work lies outside the quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, quantum networks, and hybrid quantum systems directions.

title: Ordered Interfacial Assembly Of Rough Microellipsoids
authors: Md Anisur Rahman And Peter J. Beltramo
abstract:
Author(s): Md Anisur Rahman and Peter J. Beltramo

Dense, orientationally and translationally ordered two-dimensional (2D) monolayers of colloidal ellipsoids are fabricated at air-water interfaces. Kinetic arrest and disordered structures from long-range quadrupolar capillary attraction are overcome by synthesizing polystyrene microellipsoids with s…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 035427] Published Mon Sep 21, 2026.
tldr: The paper demonstrates ordered interfacial assembly of rough polystyrene microellipsoids into dense 2D monolayers by overcoming capillary attraction and kinetic arrest.
motivation: Dense, orientationally and translationally ordered 2D monolayers of colloidal ellipsoids are desirable for fundamental studies and applications, but long-range quadrupolar capillary attraction and kinetic arrest typically lead to disordered structures.
method: Polystyrene microellipsoids with controlled surface roughness were synthesized and assembled at air-water interfaces; the roughness is used to modify capillary interactions and enable ordering.
result: The authors fabricate dense, highly ordered 2D monolayers of ellipsoids, overcoming the usual disordered structures caused by long-range capillary attraction.
conclusion: Surface roughness provides a route to control interfacial assembly and achieve ordered colloidal monolayers, which may be useful for designing structured materials.

title: Percolation Of A Cohesive Fine Particle In A Static Bed
authors: Jizhi Zhang, Qiong Zhang, Julio M. Ottino, Paul B. Umbanhowar, And Richard M. Lueptow
abstract:
Author(s): Jizhi Zhang, Qiong Zhang, Julio M. Ottino, Paul B. Umbanhowar, and Richard M. Lueptow

Percolation of fine particles (fines) in a static bed of larger particles is central to many industrial and natural processes. Noncohesive fines either pass through the bed or become trapped depending on multiple factors including particle sizes, friction and restitution coefficients, and size polyd…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033336] Published Fri Sep 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the percolation behavior of cohesive fine particles through a static bed of larger particles in granular systems.
motivation: Fine particle percolation in static beds is important for many industrial and natural processes, and cohesion adds complexity beyond noncohesive cases.
method: The authors likely use experimental and/or computational granular dynamics methods to analyze how cohesion affects whether fines pass through or become trapped in a bed.
result: The paper characterizes the conditions under which cohesive fines percolate or remain trapped, considering particle sizes, friction, and cohesion.
conclusion: Cohesive interactions significantly alter percolation dynamics compared to noncohesive fines, providing insights for granular processing.

title: Enduring Mechanical Memory From The Constitutive Response Of Elastically Recoverable Nanostructured Materials
authors: Abhishek Gupta, Bhanugoban Maheswaran, Nicholas Jaegersberg, Komal Chawla, And Ramathasan Thevamaran
abstract:
Author(s): Abhishek Gupta, Bhanugoban Maheswaran, Nicholas Jaegersberg, Komal Chawla, and Ramathasan Thevamaran

Vertically aligned carbon nanotube foams exhibit return point memory, opening new opportunities for mechanical computing applications.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031073] Published Fri Sep 18, 2026.
tldr: Vertically aligned carbon nanotube foams exhibit return-point (mechanical) memory, which the authors propose as a basis for mechanical computing.
motivation: Conventional computing relies on electronic state, but mechanical systems could in principle store and process information through their constitutive response, motivating the search for materials with intrinsic, recoverable memory.
method: The authors measure and model the cyclic constitutive response of elastically recoverable nanostructured vertically aligned carbon nanotube foams, identifying return-point memory behavior in the loading–unloading hysteresis.
result: The nanotube foams display stable return-point memory, meaning the material 'remembers' previous strain extrema (turning points) and reproduces them under subsequent loading cycles.
conclusion: Mechanically encoded memory in nanostructured foams may enable mechanical computing and architected materials that process information without electronics, though the work remains a materials-level proof of concept.

title: Interplay Between Evolutionary And Epidemic Timescales Challenges The Outcome Of Control Policies
authors: Santiago Lamata-Otín, Alex Arenas, Jesús Gómez-Gardeñes, And David Soriano-Paños
abstract:
Author(s): Santiago Lamata-Otín, Alex Arenas, Jesús Gómez-Gardeñes, and David Soriano-Paños

The classical SIR model, assuming constant viral traits, represents the cornerstone model for computing key indicators during epidemic outbreaks, such as the expected peak of infections or the impact of control policies. Viral evolution has been reported to challenge the physics of the SIR model, ch…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 137401] Published Tue Sep 22, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies how the interplay between evolutionary and epidemic timescales alters the predictions of classical SIR-based models for outbreak peaks and control policy outcomes.
motivation: Classical SIR models assume constant viral traits, but viral evolution can reshape epidemic dynamics, potentially invalidating standard indicators used to design control policies.
method: The authors extend SIR-type epidemic modeling to incorporate viral evolutionary dynamics occurring on comparable timescales to the epidemic spread, analyzing the resulting coupled dynamics and their impact on key epidemic metrics.
result: They show that when evolutionary and epidemic timescales are comparable, predictions for infection peaks and the effectiveness of control policies deviate substantially from standard SIR expectations.
conclusion: Accounting for viral evolution is essential for reliable epidemic forecasting and for designing robust control strategies, as neglecting it can lead to misleading policy outcomes.

title: Articulation Points In Multiplex Networks
authors: Artem Vergazov, Saeed Osat, And Vladimir V. Palyulin
abstract:
Author(s): Artem Vergazov, Saeed Osat, and Vladimir V. Palyulin

Many real systems can be efficiently represented by complex networks. Recently, the robustness of these networks under random or targeted attacks has been of interest. One of the strategies to dismantle a network involves identifying and removing articulation points. These are nodes that are critica…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 034315] Published Fri Sep 25, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies articulation points in multiplex networks as critical nodes whose removal can efficiently dismantle network robustness.
motivation: Many real systems are modeled as complex networks, and understanding their robustness under random or targeted attacks is important for network dismantling strategies.
method: The authors analyze articulation points—nodes whose removal disconnects a network—in the context of multiplex networks, likely using percolation or graph-theoretic techniques.
result: The study identifies and characterizes articulation points in multiplex networks and assesses their impact on network disintegration under removal strategies.
conclusion: Articulation points play a key role in the robustness of multiplex networks, offering a targeted approach for network dismantling, though the work is purely classical network science.

title: Near-wall Pathways Of Anomalous Electron Transport In Hall Thrusters Revealed By Three-dimensional Particle-in-cell Simulations
authors: Zhe Liu, Zhongping Zhao, And Yinjian Zhao
abstract:
Author(s): Zhe Liu, Zhongping Zhao, and Yinjian Zhao

Cross-field electron transport in Hall thrusters is widely attributed to high-frequency [MATH] instabilities, yet its net spatial pathway remains poorly resolved. Here we perform instability-resolving three-dimensional particle-in-cell simulations of a Hall thruster using a boundary-faithful and high…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 035211] Published Mon Sep 21, 2026.
tldr: Three-dimensional particle-in-cell simulations reveal the near-wall spatial pathways of anomalous cross-field electron transport in Hall thrusters.
motivation: Cross-field electron transport in Hall thrusters is widely attributed to high-frequency instabilities, but its net spatial pathway remains poorly resolved.
method: The authors perform instability-resolving three-dimensional particle-in-cell simulations of a Hall thruster using a boundary-faithful and high-fidelity setup.
result: The simulations identify near-wall pathways that govern anomalous electron transport and clarify how instability-driven transport is spatially organized.
conclusion: These results provide a resolved picture of anomalous electron transport in Hall thrusters, which may inform future thruster design and modeling.

title: Periodic And Quasiperiodic Traveling Waves In Nonlinear Lattices With Odd Elasticity
authors: Andrus Giraldo, Stefan Ruschel, And Behrooz Yousefzadeh
abstract:
Author(s): Andrus Giraldo, Stefan Ruschel, and Behrooz Yousefzadeh

Discrete nonlinear systems support a rich variety of localized and extended wave phenomena, with their dynamics sensitively dependent on the symmetries of the underlying interaction forces within the lattice. Odd elasticity, emerging in effective models of active materials, breaks the action-reactio…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033357] Published Wed Sep 23, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies periodic and quasiperiodic traveling-wave solutions in discrete nonlinear lattices with odd elasticity, using bifurcation and continuation methods.
motivation: Odd elasticity arises in active materials and breaks action-reaction symmetry, motivating interest in how such nonconservative interactions affect wave propagation in nonlinear lattices.
method: The authors analyze discrete nonlinear lattice models with odd elastic couplings, employing numerical continuation and dynamical systems techniques to trace periodic and quasiperiodic traveling waves.
result: They identify parameter regimes supporting periodic and quasiperiodic traveling-wave states and characterize their stability and bifurcation structure.
conclusion: The findings highlight how odd elasticity enriches the wave phenomenology of nonlinear lattices, with potential implications for active metamaterials, but the work is not related to quantum information or quantum thermodynamics.

title: Geometric Origin Of Macroscopic Alignment In Granular Flows
authors: Christopher Harper, Eric C. P. Breard, PJ Zrelak, And George W. Bergantz
abstract:
Author(s): Christopher Harper, Eric C. P. Breard, PJ Zrelak, and George W. Bergantz

Predicting the nematic alignment of nonspherical particles in sheared granular flows is essential for understanding the rheology, packing, and constitutive response of dense particulate media. While macroscopic fabric is typically attributed to complex multibody interactions, stress transmission, an…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033331] Published Thu Sep 17, 2026.
tldr: The paper explains macroscopic nematic alignment in sheared granular flows as arising from geometric packing constraints rather than complex multibody stress transmission.
motivation: Predicting the alignment of nonspherical particles in dense granular flows is crucial for understanding their rheology, packing, and constitutive behavior, but it is usually attributed to complicated many-body interactions.
method: The authors analyze sheared granular media, likely through discrete-element simulations and geometric/statistical analysis of particle fabric and contact networks.
result: They find that macroscopic fabric alignment has a geometric origin tied to packing geometry rather than emergent from multibody force transmission alone.
conclusion: Geometric considerations provide a simpler, predictive route to describe alignment and rheology in dense particulate media.

title: Anisotropic Subdiffusion In The Cytoplasm Of Living Cells
authors: Aranyak Sarkar, Pooja Yadav, And Matthias Weiss
abstract:
Author(s): Aranyak Sarkar, Pooja Yadav, and Matthias Weiss

The cytoplasm of eukaryotic cells is a complex fluid that harbors a variety of membrane-enveloped organelles with distinct spatial distributions and duties. Peroxisomes, for example, are vesicular entities with radii in the sub-micron range, dispersed all over the cytoplasm to provide oxidative reac…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 138402] Published Thu Sep 24, 2026.
tldr: The paper investigates anisotropic subdiffusion of peroxisomes in the cytoplasm of living cells.
motivation: Understanding the diffusive behavior of organelles like peroxisomes in the complex cytoplasmic environment is crucial for cellular function and transport.
method: Likely employs advanced imaging and tracking techniques to analyze the motion of sub-micron peroxisomes in eukaryotic cells.
result: Reveals anisotropic subdiffusion, indicating direction-dependent and anomalous transport of peroxisomes within the cytoplasm.
conclusion: Provides insights into the physical constraints on intracellular transport and the role of cytoplasmic structure in organelle dynamics.

title: Search For The Nonresonant Production Of A Pair Of Additional Higgs Bosons In The Type-X Two-Higgs-Doublet Model In Proton-Proton Collisions At $\sqrt{s}=13\text{ }\text{ }\mathrm{TeV}$
authors: A. Hayrapetyan et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): A. Hayrapetyan et al. (CMS Collaboration)

A search is presented for the production of two additional Higgs bosons from an off-shell Z boson, where both additional particles decay to [MATH] lepton pairs. The search is performed with a data sample collected with the CMS detector from proton-proton collisions at the LHC at $=13\te…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 131801] Published Tue Sep 22, 2026.
tldr: A CMS search for nonresonant production of a pair of additional Higgs bosons decaying to lepton pairs in the Type-X two-Higgs-doublet model using 13 TeV proton-proton collision data.
motivation: Extensions of the Standard Model such as the Type-X two-Higgs-doublet model predict additional Higgs bosons, motivating direct searches for their nonresonant production at the LHC.
method: The analysis uses CMS data from proton-proton collisions at sqrt(s)=13 TeV, selecting events consistent with the off-shell Z boson decaying to two additional Higgs bosons that subsequently decay to lepton pairs, and compares the observed yields to background predictions.
result: No significant excess over the Standard Model background is observed, and upper limits are set on the production cross section times branching fraction in the Type-X 2HDM parameter space.
conclusion: The results constrain the allowed parameter space of the Type-X two-Higgs-doublet model, excluding or disfavoring regions that predict observable nonresonant additional Higgs boson pair production at the LHC.

title: First Measurement Of The ${k}^{−}$ Escape Cross Section In The $^{12}\mathrm{C}({K}^{−},p)$ Reaction
authors: Fumiya Oura et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): Fumiya Oura et al. (J-PARC E42 Collaboration)

We investigated the [MATH]-nucleus interaction through the simultaneous measurement of the inclusive [MATH] and exclusive [MATH] escape [MATH] reactions at [MATH] at J-PARC. The present measurem…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 132501] Published Tue Sep 22, 2026.
tldr: The J-PARC E42 collaboration reports the first measurement of the K− escape cross section in the 12C(K−,p) reaction, probing the K−-nucleus interaction via inclusive and exclusive channels.
motivation: The nature of the antikaon-nucleus interaction and possible deeply bound kaonic nuclear states remain poorly constrained, motivating precise measurements of K− absorption and escape processes.
method: Simultaneous measurement of inclusive and exclusive K− escape reactions in the 12C(K−,p) reaction at J-PARC allowed extraction of the K− escape cross section and separation of competing reaction channels.
result: The first experimental determination of the K− escape cross section in the 12C(K−,p) reaction was obtained, providing constraints on the K−-nucleus interaction strength and absorption dynamics.
conclusion: These results supply benchmark data for theoretical models of antikaon-nucleus interactions and pave the way for further studies of kaonic nuclear systems at J-PARC.

title: Contact Forces In Motility-Regulated Active Matter
authors: Manh-Quan Nguyen, Alberto Dinelli, Gianmarco Spera, And Julien Tailleur
abstract:
Author(s): Manh-Quan Nguyen, Alberto Dinelli, Gianmarco Spera, and Julien Tailleur

Long-range interactions are ubiquitous in nature, where they are mediated by diffusive fields at the cellular scale or by visual cues for groups of animals. Short-range forces, which are paradigmatic in physics, can thus often be neglected when modeling the collective behaviors of biological systems…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 138302] Published Tue Sep 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how contact forces in active matter are regulated by motility, focusing on the role of short-range interactions in collective biological behavior.
motivation: Long-range interactions often dominate models of collective behavior, but short-range contact forces may be important in active systems; the authors aim to characterize their effects when motility is regulated.
method: The authors likely use theoretical modeling and simulations of active particles with motility regulation and contact interactions, analyzing how forces modify collective states.
result: The study identifies conditions under which contact forces significantly alter the collective dynamics, showing that motility regulation can tune the impact of short-range interactions.
conclusion: The work highlights the need to include contact forces in active matter models and suggests that motility regulation provides a control mechanism for collective behavior.

title: Proof Of Conservation Laws In Gravitational Scattering: Tails And Breaking Of Peeling
authors: Geoffrey Compère And Sébastien Robert
abstract:
Author(s): Geoffrey Compère and Sébastien Robert

We propose a definition of asymptotically flat spacetimes that is consistent with both null infinities and compatible with known properties of gravitational scattering, incoming and outgoing radiation, and interactions with matter. For this class of spacetimes, we prove three antipodal matching cond…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 131401] Published Mon Sep 21, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a definition of asymptotically flat spacetimes and proves antipodal matching conditions and conservation laws in gravitational scattering, including tail effects and breaking of peeling.
motivation: Gravitational scattering in asymptotically flat spacetimes requires a precise framework that is compatible with null infinity, incoming and outgoing radiation, and matter interactions.
method: The authors introduce a class of asymptotically flat spacetimes and derive antipodal matching conditions, conservation laws, and analyze tail effects and the breaking of peeling.
result: Three antipodal matching conditions are proven for this class, with implications for gravitational scattering and radiation, and the breaking of peeling is characterized.
conclusion: The proposed definition provides a consistent setting for conservation laws in gravitational scattering, but the work lies in classical gravitational physics and general relativity.

title: Curvature In Infectious Disease Network: A Metric For Vaccination And Control
authors: Sara Najem
abstract:
Author(s): Sara Najem
