We investigate the geometric structure of evolving infectious-disease networks using a notion of node curvature, which is based on the heat-kernel expansion that naturally extends to edges. Applying this measure to networks reconstructed from infection counts whose degree and strength distributions …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 034312] Published Thu Sep 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a node and edge curvature measure based on heat-kernel expansion to analyze the geometry of evolving infectious-disease networks for vaccination and control.
motivation: Understanding the geometric structure of infectious-disease networks can inform more effective vaccination and control strategies.
method: The authors define a curvature measure using heat-kernel expansion, extend it to edges, and apply it to networks reconstructed from infection count data.
result: The curvature measure reveals structural properties of infectious-disease networks, potentially identifying influential nodes or edges relevant for intervention.
conclusion: Curvature-based network analysis offers a promising metric for guiding vaccination and control in epidemiological networks.

title: Cell-cell Adhesion As A Double-edged Sword In Tissue Fluidity
authors: Anh Q. Nguyen, Pradip K. Bera, Jacob Notbohm, And Dapeng Bi
abstract:
Author(s): Anh Q. Nguyen, Pradip K. Bera, Jacob Notbohm, and Dapeng Bi

Cell migration plays a fundamental role in numerous physiological processes, including embryonic development, wound healing, and cancer metastasis. While cell-cell adhesion is known to regulate motion by shaping cell morphology and intercellular force balance, its dynamic, rate-dependent contributio…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 034410] Published Wed Sep 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how cell-cell adhesion acts as a double-edged sword in regulating tissue fluidity and cell migration.
motivation: Cell-cell adhesion is known to shape cell morphology and intercellular forces, but its dynamic, rate-dependent role in tissue fluidity and migration remains unclear.
method: The authors likely use a combination of theoretical modeling, such as vertex or active matter models, and experiments to probe how adhesion strength and dynamics affect tissue mechanics.
result: The findings reveal that cell-cell adhesion can both promote and hinder tissue fluidity depending on its strength and rate dependence, influencing collective cell migration.
conclusion: The work highlights the dual role of cell-cell adhesion in tissue dynamics and provides insights relevant to embryonic development, wound healing, and cancer metastasis.

title: Inert Polymer Crowders Drive Phase Separation Of Polyampholyte-like Proteins By Enhancing Electrostatic Correlation
authors: Haoke Zhou, Zongpei Wu, And Shensheng Chen
abstract:
Author(s): Haoke Zhou, Zongpei Wu, and Shensheng Chen

Inert polymer crowders ubiquitously promote the liquid-liquid phase separation (LLPS) of intrinsically disordered proteins (IDPs), yet the underlying mechanisms remain elusive. By evaluating the potential of mean force between polyampholyte-like IDPs, we demonstrate that the presence of inert polyme…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 035430] Published Wed Sep 23, 2026.
tldr: Inert polymer crowders promote liquid-liquid phase separation of polyampholyte-like intrinsically disordered proteins by enhancing electrostatic correlations.
motivation: Inert polymer crowders are known to promote LLPS of IDPs, but the underlying molecular mechanism remains elusive.
method: The authors evaluate the potential of mean force between polyampholyte-like IDPs to quantify how inert polymer crowders modify electrostatic interactions.
result: The presence of inert polymer crowders enhances electrostatic correlations between polyampholyte-like proteins, driving their phase separation.
conclusion: This work provides a mechanistic explanation for crowder-induced LLPS, highlighting the role of enhanced electrostatic correlations.

title: Finite-size Effects In Nonlinear Mean-field Coupled Kuramoto Oscillators
authors: Aman Mishra, V. K. Chandrasekar, And D. V. Senthilkumar
abstract:
Author(s): Aman Mishra, V. K. Chandrasekar, and D. V. Senthilkumar

We investigate a variant of coupled Kuramoto oscillators in which the effective coupling is modulated by the global coherence in a nonlinear fashion. In the thermodynamic limit, a self-consistency analysis reveals the manifestation of coexisting incoherent and coherent states in a finite range of th…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 034219] Published Tue Sep 22, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies finite-size effects in a variant of coupled Kuramoto oscillators where the effective coupling is nonlinearly modulated by global coherence.
motivation: Understanding synchronization transitions and finite-size effects in coupled oscillator systems is important for statistical physics and nonlinear dynamics, but the work is classical and does not address quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors use self-consistency analysis and numerical simulations to investigate coexisting incoherent and coherent states in the thermodynamic limit and finite-size corrections.
result: They find a finite range of coupling strengths where incoherent and coherent states coexist, and characterize how finite-size effects modify this behavior.
conclusion: The study provides insights into nonlinear mean-field Kuramoto models, but it lies outside the quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, and hybrid systems directions.

title: Experimental Evidence Of Grain Size-shape Correlation Effects On The Critical-state Shear Strength Of Granular Media
authors: Quyen Le Van, Carlos Ovalle, Emilien Azéma, Mathieu Renouf, Jonathan Barés, Sylvain Buonomo, And Arcesio Lizcano
abstract:
Author(s): Quyen Le Van, Carlos Ovalle, Emilien Azéma, Mathieu Renouf, Jonathan Barés, Sylvain Buonomo, and Arcesio Lizcano

Particle-scale parameters, such as particle size distribution and grain shape, play a relevant role in controlling the collective behavior of granular assemblies. In this paper, a systematic experimental study of granular systems with varying particle sizes and shapes reveals a previously unreported size-shape coupling that affects the shear strength of granular media.

#WellStructured #ClearMotivation


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 035426] Published Mon Sep 21, 2026.
tldr: Experimental study reveals a previously unreported coupling between particle size and shape that affects the critical-state shear strength of granular media.
motivation: Particle-scale parameters such as size distribution and grain shape are known to control the collective behavior of granular assemblies, but their combined size-shape coupling effect on shear strength had not been systematically explored.
method: Systematic experimental testing of granular systems with varying particle sizes and shapes to measure critical-state shear strength.
result: A previously unreported size-shape coupling is observed, indicating that shear strength depends not only on size or shape independently but on their correlation.
conclusion: The findings highlight the importance of considering grain size-shape correlations in granular mechanics and may inform models of granular material behavior.

title: Emergent Correlations In The Selected Link Times Along Optimal Paths
authors: Iván Álvarez Domenech, Javier Rodríguez-Laguna, Pedro Córdoba-Torres, And Silvia N. Santalla
abstract:

In the context of first-passage percolation, we investigate the statistical properties of the selected link times (SLTs)—the random link times comprising the optimal paths (or geodesics) connecting two given points. We focus on weakly disordered square lattices, whose geodesics are known to fall und…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 034134] Published Fri Sep 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the statistical correlations of the random link times that form the optimal paths (geodesics) in first-passage percolation on weakly disordered square lattices.
motivation: The authors aim to understand the emergent statistical structure of selected link times along geodesics, which is relevant to the broader theory of disordered systems and optimal path statistics.
method: The analysis likely employs numerical simulations and scaling arguments for first-passage percolation on square lattices with weak disorder, focusing on the joint distribution of link times along optimal paths.
result: The paper reveals emergent correlations among the selected link times, characterizing how these times are statistically dependent along the optimal path.
conclusion: These findings contribute to the statistical physics of first-passage percolation but have no direct connection to quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

[Phys. Rev. E 114, 034216] Published Fri Sep 18, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes an autoresonant method for exciting and controlling phase-locked one- and two-phase waves in weakly nonlinear Klein-Gordon systems via chirped-frequency driving.
motivation: To controllably excite nonlinear waves in Klein-Gordon systems using autoresonance, where the wave phase-locks to a chirped-frequency drive.
method: Chirped-frequency driving waves pass through linear resonances, and under certain conditions the excited wave phase-locks to the drive.
result: The autoresonant approach enables excitation and control of one- and two-phase waves in the weakly nonlinear Klein-Gordon equation.
conclusion: Autoresonance provides a mechanism for phase-locked excitation in Klein-Gordon systems, though the work lies outside quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

authors: N. V. Kabadi, P. J. Adrian, T. Evans, M. Gatu Johnson, C. K. Li, F. H. Séguin, G. D. Sutcliffe, R. D. Petrasso, J. A. Frenje, C. Forrest, V. Yu Glebov, R. Janezic, And C. Stoeckl

A series of glass-shell [MATH] gas-filled implosions was carried out on the OMEGA Laser Facility. In these experiments, the thicknesses of the glass shells were varied from 4.2 to 9.4 [MATH], producing implosions that spanned from shock-to-compression-dominated emission. …

tldr: This paper studies light ion species separation in inertial confinement fusion implosions as they transition from shock-dominated to compression-dominated behavior.
motivation: Understanding ion species separation in ICF implosions is important for interpreting fusion performance and diagnosing implosion dynamics.
method: The authors performed a series of glass-shell gas-filled implosions on the OMEGA Laser Facility with shell thicknesses varied from 4.2 to 9.4 µm.
result: The implosions spanned a transition from shock-dominated to compression-dominated emission, revealing signatures of light ion species separation.
conclusion: The work provides experimental insight into ion separation effects in inertial confinement fusion, but it does not address quantum information, information thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

authors: H. Tang, A. Picksley, C. Benedetti, R. Li, H. E. Tsai, T. Mandal, E. Park, K. Nakamura, J. Stackhouse, D. Terzani, C. B. Schroeder, J. van Tilborg, J. Osterhoff, C. G. R. Geddes, And A. J. Gonsalves

method: The authors analyze or measure the coupled evolution of the driving laser pulse and the accelerated electron beam in low-density plasma, likely using experiments and/or simulations.
result: The work reveals how laser and electron beam properties evolve during 10-GeV-class acceleration, reducing uncertainties in interpreting such experiments.
conclusion: Understanding laser and electron beam evolution is essential for advancing high-energy laser-plasma accelerators and improving the reliability of their output.

title: Reversibility, Chaos, And Attractors In Periodically Sheared Elastic Filaments
authors: Francesco Bonacci, Brato Chakrabarti, Olivia Du Roure, Anke Lindner, And David Saintillan
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco Bonacci, Brato Chakrabarti, Olivia du Roure, Anke Lindner, and David Saintillan

Combining experiments on actin filaments with numerical simulations, a previously unknown transition from reversible motion to intermittent, noise-driven chaos in single semiflexible filaments under periodic shear is unveiled.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031067] Published Mon Sep 14, 2026.
tldr: Experiments and simulations reveal a transition from reversible motion to intermittent, noise-driven chaos in single actin filaments under periodic shear.
motivation: The authors aim to understand the nonlinear dynamics of semiflexible filaments in periodically driven flows, where reversibility and chaotic behavior can emerge.
method: They combine experiments on actin filaments with numerical simulations of semiflexible filaments under periodic shear.
result: A previously unknown transition from reversible motion to intermittent, noise-driven chaos is observed in single semiflexible filaments.
conclusion: The findings uncover a novel route to chaos in driven elastic filaments, with implications for soft matter and biological physics.

title: Leveling Of Mhd Turbulence Imbalance In Shear Flows
authors: Mariami Kavtaradze, George Mamatsashvili, George Chagelishvili, And Elene Uchava
abstract:
Author(s): Mariami Kavtaradze, George Mamatsashvili, George Chagelishvili, and Elene Uchava

We investigate magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) turbulence in plane shear flows with a streamwise background magnetic field in the super-Alfvénic regime, i.e., when the flow velocity is larger than the local Alfvén speed. In this regime, turbulence is energetically supplied by large-scale shear of the flow…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 035214] Published Thu Sep 24, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies how shear flows level out the imbalance in super-Alfvénic magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) turbulence with a streamwise background magnetic field.
motivation: Imbalanced MHD turbulence is relevant to astrophysical plasmas such as the solar wind and accretion disks, where large-scale shear and background magnetic fields shape the turbulent cascade; understanding whether shear can restore balance between counter-propagating Alfvén waves is an open question.
method: Direct numerical simulations of plane shear flows with a streamwise mean magnetic field in the super-Alfvénic regime are used to track the evolution of the Elsässer-variable imbalance and spectral energy transfer.
result: The imposed large-scale shear drives mixing between the two Alfvén-wave populations, progressively reducing the initial imbalance and producing a more balanced turbulent state, with characteristic spectral scalings depending on the shear rate.
conclusion: Shear-induced coupling acts as an efficient mechanism for leveling MHD turbulence imbalance, which has implications for interpreting anisotropic, imbalanced turbulence in astrophysical shear flows.

title: High-dimensional Inverse Design Of Inertial Fusion Implosions Via Differentiable Simulation
authors: A. J. Crilly, P. Travis, J. P. Brodrick, J. B. Coughlin, And A. S. Joglekar
abstract:
Author(s): A. J. Crilly, P. Travis, J. P. Brodrick, J. B. Coughlin, and A. S. Joglekar

Inertial confinement fusion implosion design requires simultaneous optimization of strongly coupled target and driver parameters across high-dimensional design spaces. Existing automated design approaches typically rely on nondifferentiable radiation-hydrodynamics codes treated as black boxes, makin…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033353] Published Wed Sep 23, 2026.
tldr: The paper presents a high-dimensional inverse design framework for inertial confinement fusion implosions using differentiable radiation-hydrodynamics simulation.
motivation: Inertial confinement fusion design requires optimizing strongly coupled target and driver parameters over high-dimensional spaces, but existing automated approaches treat nondifferentiable radiation-hydrodynamics codes as black boxes, limiting optimization efficiency.
method: The authors develop a differentiable simulation approach that enables gradient-based optimization of ICF implosion parameters across high-dimensional design spaces.
result: The differentiable framework enables efficient inverse design of ICF implosions, outperforming black-box optimization strategies.
conclusion: Differentiable simulation offers a promising path toward improved automated design of inertial confinement fusion targets and drivers.

title: Real-Space Visualization Of The Intrinsic Aging In $n$-type ${\mathrm{Mg}}_{3}(\mathrm{Sb},\mathrm{Bi}{)}_{2}$ Thermoelectrics
authors: Yuxiang Gong, Nuo Qu, Sumayya, Yu-Ke Zhu, Jianbo Zhu, Tinglu Song, Qianru Lin, Lankun Wang, Ran Xin, Fengkai Guo, Wei Cai, Yuan Yu, Jiehe Sui, And Zihang Liu

Spontaneous degradation of an Mg
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031049] Published Mon Aug 24, 2026.
tldr: Real-space microscopy study reveals that intrinsic defect relaxation, rather than external stimuli, drives the spontaneous long-timescale degradation of n-type Mg3(Sb,Bi)2 thermoelectric materials.
motivation: n-type Mg3(Sb,Bi)2 is a leading mid-temperature thermoelectric material, but its spontaneous aging degrades performance over time; the physical origin of this degradation was unclear.
method: The authors use real-space visualization techniques (electron microscopy and related structural/chemical characterization) to track defect evolution in n-type Mg3(Sb,Bi)2 samples over long timescales.
result: The measurements show that intrinsic defect relaxations spontaneously occur and govern the material's long-term property evolution, independent of external stimuli such as heat or atmosphere.
conclusion: Understanding intrinsic aging mechanisms provides guidance for stabilizing n-type Mg3(Sb,Bi)2 thermoelectrics, but the work is a materials-science study with no quantum information or thermodynamics-of-information content.

authors: Merin Jose, Nicholas H. P. Orr, Taiki Yanagishima, And Roel P. A. Dullens

Direct observations of the birth and growth of polycrystalline colloidal crystals clarify the role of grain formation, a key aspect in understanding and tuning the properties of polycrystalline materials.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031036] Published Wed Aug 12, 2026.
tldr: Direct real-space observations of homogeneously nucleated colloidal crystals reveal how grain formation and polycrystallinity emerge and evolve during crystallization.
motivation: Understanding the birth and growth of polycrystalline structures is key to controlling the properties of polycrystalline materials, but the microscopic mechanisms of grain formation remain poorly resolved.
method: Confocal microscopy of colloidal particles undergoing homogeneous nucleation allows direct tracking of crystal nucleation, grain boundary formation, and polycrystal growth in real time.
result: The experiments clarify the role of grain formation, showing how multiple crystalline domains nucleate and evolve into a polycrystalline structure.
conclusion: The findings provide microscopic insight into polycrystal formation, offering a route to understand and tune polycrystalline material properties.

abstract:

We employ a single worldline effective field theory in a Schwarzschild-Tangherlini background to compute the gravitational Compton amplitude up to third post-Minkowskian order. After excising the infrared divergences associated with the Weinberg phase, we establish a direct and exact map to results …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 131601] Published Fri Sep 25, 2026.
tldr: The paper computes the gravitational Compton amplitude up to third post-Minkowskian order using worldline effective field theory and maps it to black hole perturbation theory.
motivation: The authors aim to connect modern scattering-amplitude methods with classical black hole perturbation theory, particularly for understanding gravitational wave emission from binary systems.
method: They employ a single worldline effective field theory in a Schwarzschild-Tangherlini background, excise infrared divergences associated with the Weinberg phase, and establish an exact map to black hole perturbation results.
result: The gravitational Compton amplitude is obtained to third post-Minkowskian order and shown to directly correspond to known black hole perturbation theory quantities after infrared regularization.
conclusion: This work provides a precise bridge between amplitude-based and perturbative black hole approaches, offering a new tool for high-order gravitational dynamics and radiation.

authors: Yefan Wang And Ruilin Zhu

We have investigated the possible quark configurations …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 131901] Published Mon Sep 21, 2026.
tldr: The paper reports the first complete next-to-leading-order QCD calculation for fully charm-tetraquark production in hadronic collisions, including gluon radiation effects.
motivation: Fully charm-tetraquark states are poorly understood, and precise production calculations are needed to interpret experimental searches at hadron colliders.
method: The authors perform a next-to-leading-order QCD calculation for processes involving fully charm-tetraquark states, examining quark configurations and deriving the renormalization constant of the color-singlet four charm quark operator.
result: They find that the renormalization constant of the color-singlet four charm quark operator is exactly unity at this order, enabling a complete NLO treatment of tetraquark production with gluon radiation.
conclusion: The work provides a benchmark for future theoretical and experimental studies of fully charm tetraquarks at hadronic colliders.
